# Isaiah 1-12

## ANNOTATIONS ON THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH

### THE ARGUMENT

By two sorts of persons did God anciently make known his mind, and will, to his people the Jews; by ordinary ministers, and by extraordinary messengers. The ordinary ministers were the priests, and Levites: both these, all of one tribe, the lineage of Levi; the former of them, all of one house in that tribe, the offspring of Aaron. The extraordinary messengers, were the prophets; so termed, of foretelling future events, by divine revelation; men immediately called by God himself, and by him immediately inspired. These were of any house, tribe, or profession, indifferently, as God was pleased to cull, and call. The prophets, whose monuments we have severally booked in Scripture, are in number sixteen: whereof the four former are called, in regard of the largeness of their prophecies, the greater; the latter twelve, in regard of the shortness of them, the lesser.

Of the four larger, Isaiah, as in place, and rank, so in order of time, is without question, the first; and lived also, in likelihood, some time at least, together with the first of the other twelve: no one of them, whose times are expressed, rising higher than the reign of Jeroboam the second king of Israel; who reigned fifteen years together, with Uzziah king of Judah, in whose reign this our prophet began his prophetical employment. What tribe he was of, or of what estate, and profession, before his entrance upon his office, is uncertain: no mention being made of his pedigree, either here, or elsewhere; further than his next progenitor. So that what the Jewish doctors tell us, concerning his being of the tribe of Judah, and of the blood-royal; as also of his father's being a prophet, and brother to King Amaziah, are matters of no certainty, having no footing in Scripture. His sermons, or prophecies, here recorded, abound with great variety of religious instructions, serious admonitions, sharp reproofs, severe menaces, and comfortable promises. And these all delivered in a style suitable to the subject matter, very lofty, and stately; full fraught with rhetorical garnishes, and such native elegancies, as in other languages cannot easily, if at all, be expressed. Besides his predictions of God's judgments to befall his own nation for their sins, partly by the Assyrians, and partly by the Chaldeans, and concerning the utter destruction of the adversaries of God's people, as well jointly, as severally; he is most plentiful in foretelling their deliverance from the Babylonian captivity by Cyrus, whom by name he mentions, above one hundred years before he was born, and well near two hundred, before the thing itself effected: and withal in declaring the restitution and enlargement of the church, whereof that was a figure; together with the calling in of the Gentiles by Christ; whose incarnation, birth, breeding, calling, offices (royal, priestly, prophetical), life, teaching, courses, sufferings, death, rising again, glory ensuing, kingdom's length, and extent, he so largely and lively describes, that he may seem rather to write a story of things already done, than a prophecy of things to come. In regard whereof, he is by the ancients not undeservedly termed *An Evangelical Prophet*, and *A Prophetical Evangelist*. Even his menacing predictions being usually tempered, and closed with some gracious promises of the gospel. His continuance in the prophetical function, is from the times of the kings under whom he prophesied, not improbably deemed to have been about threescore years. Howsoever, that which is from the Jewish doctors received, concerning his prophesying under Manasses, and suffering death by him, seems groundless: the inscription of his prophecies making no mention of any king under whom he prophesied, lower than Hezekiah; towards the latter end of whose reign, it is not unlikely that he died. Besides this book of prophecies, he wrote also the acts, first and last, of King Uzziah; as appears by 2 Chron. 26. 22. but that seems not now extant. See on Chap. 1. 1. So much of his writings has by God's providence been preserved, as he deemed necessary for the good of his church.

### CHAPTER 1

**V. 1.** *{The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah, and Jerusalem*} This first verse contains in it, the title, or inscription, not of this first chapter alone, or the sermon therein delivered, but of the main body of the whole book, and all the sermons, or prophecies therein contained; as by the times, and reigns of the several kings hereafter mentioned, may appear: see the like, Jer. 1. 1, 2. Hosea 1. 1.

*{the vision*} God's word, or mind made known to this his servant by *vision* or *revelation*, Rev. 1. 1. and 9. 17. a kind of divine, or spiritual rapture, Num. 24. 4, 16. Ezek. 1. 1. and 11. 24. one of those means, whereby God in those times imparted his mind to his prophets; of which see, Gen. 15. 1. Numb. 12. 6. so Obad. 1. Nahum 1. 1.

*{vision*} Put collectively for *visions*; as Chap. 22. 1. 1 Sam. 3. 1. Dan. 1. 17. because it has reference in general, to all the ensuing visions, prophecies, or sermons, as was before showed. So *ox*, and *ass*; for *oxen* and *asses*, verse 3.

*{of Isaiah*} Or *Jeshajah*, as *Amariah*, and *Azariah*, 2 Kings 15. 1. and *Jeshajah* also, Ezra 8. 7, 19. yet here, Heb. *Jeshajahu*: (for so is the name of this prophet constantly written) as *Uzzijahu*, *Chizkijahu*, and others, as well here, as elsewhere. Greek, *Esaias*, Mat. 15. 7. John 1. 23. and 12. 39, 41. as *Jeremias*, Mat. 16. 14. and *Zacharias*, Luke 1. 5, 12. In our ordinary speech, following the Greek, rather *Esay*, than *Isaiah*; as in *Ezekiel*, *Ezekiah*, *Jeremy*, *Zachary*, and the like. And so our ancient versions, speaking in English forms to English ears, not amiss render it. The word signifies, *God's salvation*. No unfit title for him; who so clearly, and largely prophesied of Christ, and of salvation to be achieved and accomplished by him; whereof, see the preface: and to this purpose, some of the Jewish doctors allege Chap. 49. 1. As if it were there intimated, that God for this cause had assigned him that name, before he was born. But of that, See more on the place.

*{the son of Amoz*} The Jewish doctors have a rule, that where any prophet has his father mentioned together with him, (as *Esay* here, and some others elsewhere, Jer. 1. 1. Ezek. 1. 3. Hosea 1. 1. Joel 1. 1. Zeph. 1. 1. Zach. 1. 1.) there both father, and son, were prophets; whence they conclude, that *Daniel*, *Amos*, *Obadiah*, *Nahum*, *Habbacock*, *Haggy*, and *Malachy*, were prophets indeed, but no prophets' sons; because, though the place of their birth, or abode, be mentioned, yet their parentage is concealed; which, albeit of *Amos* it be true, Amos 1. 1. and 7. 14. Yet of the rest of them is altogether uncertain. Nor has that rule concerning the former, any good ground; but is a mere fruit of their own fancy. The mention of the parents of some of them seems to have been added; either because their parents were of some eminent note or place, in church, or state; as Jer. 1. 1. or, because, there were some other of the same name, in those times, from whom they might, by such mention of their lineage, be distinguished. And so it might well be with this our prophet; in being not unlikely, that in his days, there were other persons, bearing the same name, as well as in divers other ages, both before and after the times he lived in; as appears, 1 Chron. 26. 25. Ezra 8. 7, 19.

*{Amoz*} Or, *Amots*. Not the same with the prophet *Amos*: as some have imagined: (for their names in the original differ, not in the two letters only; the first, and the last: but in notation also, the one having a signification of *might*, the other of *weight*) but some other. One, whom the Jewish writers affirm to have been the son of Joash, King of Judah, and brother (not to Uzziah, or Azariah, as most interpreters, by mistake, misreport them, but) to Amaziah. For which yet, because they produce no authentic record, their report of it deserves no great credit.

*{which he saw*} That is, was revealed to him, 1 Pet. 1. 12. 1 Cor. 2. 10. As clearly, and as certainly, as if he had seen it, 2 Cor. 4. 18. and 5. 1. Heb. 11. 27. From whence also the prophets were anciently termed *Seers*. 1 Sam. 9. 9, 19. Chap. 30. 10. So Chap. 2. 1.

*{concerning*} The Hebrew particle may signify *upon*; as Chap. 3. 6. or, *against*, as Jer. 50. 31. and 51. 21. But here rather, *concerning*; because the ensuing prophecies contain mixed matter, of mercies, and judgments. As Psal. 101. 1. so Jer. 16. 3. and 18. 8, 9, 10. Ezek. 27. 30. For so, there also it should be rendered. See Chap. 63. 7. and Jer. 49. 1, 7.

*{Judah, and Jerusalem*} As 2 Kings 23. 1. 2 Chron. 34. 3. Chap. 3. 1. Jer. 19. 7. and 27. 20, 21. Though the one be comprehended in the other; yet mentioned apart, the one from the other; because the latter, a more eminent, and remarkable part of the former. So, *the land, and Jericho*. Josh. 2. 1. *Of David's servants nineteen men, and Asahel.* 2 Sam. 2. 30. *Out of the hands of all his enemies, and out of the hands of Saul.* 2 Sam. 22. 1. Or, because Jerusalem, as the principal place both of church and state in Judah; Psal. 76. 1, 2. and 122. 4, 5. so (which usually falls out in bad times) more disordered than other parts of the land; and by her example, a leader of others into the like. Mic. 1. 5. *Judah* and *Jerusalem* put here for the state and people of either. As verse 27. Chap. 2. 1. and 3. 1. These are only here mentioned; because unto them, chiefly, was the prophet sent. Chap. 6. 9. Albeit he prophesied of, at least, if not unto other nations, besides them. But that also, for the instruction, consolation, or reprehension of God's people: those nations being, for the most part, such as they either had been oppressed by, as Assur, and Babel, Chap. 10. & 13. Or had too much relied upon: as Egypt, and Ethiopia; Chap. 20. and 30.

*{Judah*} The name of Jacob's fourth son by Leah; Gen. 29. 35. and 49. 8. whose posterity also did bear his name. Deut. 33. 17. Jud. 1. 2, 3, 4. and also the land that fell to their lot; and wherein they abode. Jud. 17. 9. and 18. 12.

*{Jerusalem*} The name of a city in the land of Canaan; formerly called *Jebus*; Judg. 19. 10. 1 Chr. 11. 4, 5. and *Salem*, Gen. 14. 18. Psal. 76. 2. In regard whereof, some suppose it to have been called, in process of time, from those two terms put together: first, *Jebu-Salem*, and then *Jerusalem*. Others would have it so termed, as a *formidable city*, in regard of the strength and impregnableness of it; as a place dangerous to be dealt with: 2 Sam. 5. 6. See Zach. 13. 3, 4, 6. Others, as a *peaceable possession*, or a *possession of peace*. See Heb. 7. 2. and others, lastly, and that most probable; as a place of *special providence*: whereof see further, Chap. 22. 1. The word is sometimes found in a dual form; because the city was divided into two parts, the upper, and the lower. See Jer. 39. 3. And Josephus of *the Jewish war*: l. 6. c. 13. or, because it stood in the confines of two tribes, Judah, and Benjamin; part of it belonging to the one tribe, and part to the other, Josh. chap. 15. verse 63. & 18. 28. Jud. 1. verse 21.

*{in the days*} That is, *the times, the reigns*, as Hos. 1. 1. Amos 1. 1. the usual manner of computation in Scripture, by *days*, Gen. 5. 4, 5, 8. & 47. 9. Psal. 39. 4, 5. teaching us to make reckoning of every day, as being for every day accountable, Psal. 90. 10, 12.

*{of Uzziah*} Heb. *Uzzijahu*, (as *Jeshajahu*, and *Chizkijahu*, before.) Greek, *Ozias*, Mat. 1. 8, 9. called also *Azariah*, 2 Kings 15. 1. having, it seems, two names, as *Ornan*, the Jebusite, 1 Chr. 21. 18. called also *Araunah*, 2 Sam. 24. 16. *Jehoiachin*, 2 Kings 24. 8. called also *Jeconiah*, 1 Chron. 3. 16. *Jehoiada*, 2 Chron. 24. 20, 22. called also *Barachias*, Mat. 23. 25. and divers others. See Jer. 22. 11. Of this king's reign, see 2 Kings 15. 1, 7. & 2 Chr. 26. Of his acts, it is said, that this our prophet wrote; but that book of his seems not now extant: no more than that of *Jasher*, 2 Sam. 1. 18. and that of *Jeremy*, 2 Chr. 35. 25. For it cannot well be understood of that short abridgment, in so few verses comprised, in the second book of the Kings; and coming so far short of that larger relation in the second of the Chronicles, where yet it is mentioned, as relating much more, than is there upon record.

*{Jotham*} Of his reign, see 2 Kings 15. 32, 38. 2 Chr. 27. 1, 7.

*{Ahaz*} Heb. *Achaz*: as *Achab*. And so the Greek, Mat. 1. 9. as *Rachab* also there, v. 5. Of his wicked reign, see 2 Kings 16. and 2 Chron. 28.

*{and Hezekiah*} Heb. here, *Jechizkijahu*: and Mic. 1. 1. *Jechizkijah*. Though most commonly *Chizkijahu*, as chap. 36. 1. and 38. 1. and sometime *Chizkijah*, as 2 Kings 18. 1, 10. Greek, *Ezekias*, Mat. chap. 1. verse 9, 10. Of his religious reign, see 2 Kings chap. 18, 19. and 20. and 2 Chron. from chap. 29. unto chap. 32. as also of some good part of it, in this prophecy, from chap. 36. unto chap. 39. He being the last king mentioned under whom Esay prophesied, it may be probably hence gathered, that the prophet Esay did not survive Hezekiah: and consequently, that he suffered not under Manasses, as is commonly, but groundlessly held.

*{Kings of Judah*} That is, of the kingdom, or state of Judah, consisting of that tribe, with those of Benjamin that adhered unto it: so termed, as distinguished from the other ten tribes, commonly called by the name of *Israel*; after their revolt from the house of David, under Rehoboam, 1 Kings 11. 31, 32. and 12. 16, 17. So Jer. 3. 8. Hos. 4. 15. Some suppose, that the sermons, or prophecies in this book recorded, are disposed, and digested in order successively, according to the times and reigns of the kings here mentioned: but of that there is no great certainty. See v. 2. Nor do we find the like in the writings of the other prophets observed. See Jer. 27. 1.

**V. 2.** *{Hear, &c.*} Here begins *Esay's* first sermon, or prophecy, contained in this book; and that concluded in this chapter: which yet to some, seems not to have been the first in time, after his designment to his office. See verse 7, 8. (where the desolations mentioned seem to have reference unto Ahaz his time:) and Chap. 6. 1, 8. In it the Lord first arraigns his people; as in the view of the whole world, of extreme unthankfulness, stupidity, and brutishness in their carriage towards him: Verse 2, 4. as also of desperate obstinacy under his hand, that had been so heavy upon them, for their sins: verse 5, 9. Secondly, acquaints them with the cause, why their sacrifices and services found no acceptance at all with him. verse 10, 15. Thirdly, invites them to a friendly debate, propounding them terms of composition, and reconcilement, verse 16, 20. Fourthly, complains of a strange alteration with them, in their rulers especially, for the worse. verse 21, 23. Fifthly, promises a restitution of them, upon their sincere and serious reformation, verse 25, 27. and withal denounces destruction unto those of them that shall still persist in their wicked courses, verse 24, 28, 31.

**1 SERMO.**

*{hear O heavens, and hearken O earth*} The forementioned arraignment of them the prophet makes entrance into, with a solemn contestation: wherein *heaven*, and *earth*, the whole frame of the creature, Gen. 1. 1. are summoned, and called upon: as to appear, and bear witness in God's behalf against his people, as Deut. 4. 26. & 30. 19. & 31. 28. so to hear, and to take notice of God's charge given in against them: as Mic. 6. 1, 2. Thereby implying them to be so extreme obstinate, and senseless; that the very lifeless creatures were more ready to hear, and obey God's word, than they, Numb. 20. 8. Psal. 105. 31, 34. & 107. 25. & 147. 15, 18. Mat. 8. 26, 27. And their carriage towards God so vile, base, and abominable, as might well make the very lifeless and senseless creatures to abhor it, and to be astonished at it. Jer. 2. 12. Luke 19. 40. Howbeit some by *Heavens*, here understand the blessed angels; whose abode is in heaven: as Job 15. 15. Psal. 97. 6, 7. By *Earth*, people living on the surface of the earth: as Psal. 96. 9, 13. & 98. 9. As if men, and angels, were both appealed unto, for the hearing, and deciding of the controversy between God, and his people: as Chap. 5. 3. Jer. 2. 9, 10. But the former seems the sounder, and more simple exposition. In like manner does Moses begin his song: Deut. 32. 1. as Esay here this prophecy: for frivolous and ridiculous is that conceit of the Chaldee paraphrast there, that Moses should say: *Attend, O heaven, and hear, O earth*, because he was near to heaven, and far from the earth: whereas Esay says, *hear, O heaven; and attend, O earth*: Because he was farther from heaven, and nearer the earth: whereas it is well known, that the words are promiscuously used; and either of them as well to those afar off, as to those that are near at hand: See Psal. 5. 1, 2. & 17. 1. & 49. 1. Verse 10. Chap. 28. 23.

*{heavens*} Or, *heaven*. As it is well rendered, Gen. 1. 1. 1 Kings 8. 23. Chap. 49. 13. & 66. 1. For, though the word have a dual form: supposed to have his appellation, from the waters, therein contained, whose name is also deemed to have the like form, in regard of those two general receptacles of water, the one above in the clouds, the other below in the sea: and other parcels, that either environ the earth, or shoot themselves into it: Gen. 1. 6, 7. And it be not denied, that there is mention in Scripture of more heavens, than one: Deut. 10. 14. 1 Kings 8. 27. Psal. 148. 4. Yet neither is that notation certain, or the deduction, and composition so exact. And we read of more than two heavens: a third, 2 Cor. 12. 2. and both in Hebrew, and other languages, many words are found, that under a plural form bear but a singular sense: as that of *water* among other. verse 22, 30.

*{O earth*} Not the inhabitants of the earth, as Psal. 2. 10. & 33. 8. but the earth itself, as Jer. 6. 19. & 22. 29.

*{for the Lord*} Not man, but God: not the prophet, but the Lord: 1 Thess. 2. 13. Heb. 13. 7. not the herald, or crier: Chap. 44. 3. Mar. 1. 3. but the King and Judge, Chap. 33. 22. By whose command, and authority, and in whose name, and person, he speaks: Chap. 6. 1, 9. & 40. 1, 6. He that speaks by him, and in him, Acts 4. 25. 2 Cor. 13. 3.

*{the Lord*} Heb. *Jehovah*, as Psal. 83. 18. The only true God, Deut. 6. 5. who alone has his being of himself, Exod. 3. 14. Chap. 43. 11, 13. and gives being to all things, Acts 17. 25, 28. Rom. 11. 36. Rev. 4. 11. See Exod. 6. 3. Chap. 26. 4.

*{hath spoken*} Or, *doth speak, speaks*. As Amos 1. 3, 6. & 3. 8. Or, *is about to speak*; (as *perish*, for, *about to perish, ready to perish*, Prov. 31. 6. Chap. 27. 13. And *say*, for, *am about to say*, 1 Cor. 12. 15.) And requires therefore all due attention, as chap. 41. 1. Which if Moses require, when he speaks, though by God's appointment, yet in his own person: Deut. 32. 1. Surely Esay, speaking in God's own person, much more.

*{I have nourished*} God begins this his contestation with his people, with a recital of his singular favors conferred on them, and continued unto them: in a more especial manner, than unto many, yea, unto any other people, Deut. 7. 6. & 10. 15. & 26. 18. Psal. 147. 20.

*{nourished*} Or, *nursed*. Heb. *reared, brought up*. So is the word used, Job 31. 18. Chap. 23. 4. & 51. 18. I have from their first beginning to be a people, while they were yet in Egypt as an abject infant, disregarded, and not looked after, taken them up, undertaken the charge of them: provided for them, protected them, supplied them with all necessaries, had as tender a care of them, as parents are wont to have of their children, until they come to their full growth, or to man's estate; chap. 46. 3, 4. Ezek. 16. 7, 14. Hos. 11. 3.

*{children*} The people of Israel, whom he had adopted to be his peculiar ones, his children. Deut. 32. 6, 14. chap. 63. 8.

*{and brought them up*} As chap. 23. 4. Or, *advanced, exalted*: As 1 Sam. 2. 7. Ezek. 31. 4. And this rather here: because that was, before, not implied only, but expressed: and this latter seems to be a further addition to the former. I have not only brought them up, but preferred, honored, advanced them, by entering into a solemn covenant with them, taking them to be so near to me, committing my sacred oracles to them, setting my place of special residence among them, working strange, and unheard of miracles for them; and raising them up to a kingdom of great note, and renown. Deut. 4. 6, 7, 8, 32, 36. Ezek. 16. 8, 14. Psal. 135. 4. & 147. 19, 20. & 148. 14. Chap. 42. 21. Rom. 3. 1, 2. & 9. 4, 5. For neither can I assent to the Jewish doctor that confounds this with the former, expounding both of *advancement* only: and much less approve of his father's nice distinction, restraining the former, unto God's giving them his law: chap. 42. 21. the latter to the settling of his sanctuary among them. Psal. 76. 1, 2. Chap. 11. 10.

*{and they have rebelled against me*} After the relation of God's goodness towards them, follows a narration of their unworthy demeanor towards him, who had dealt so graciously, and bountifully with them: The one much aggravating the guilt of the other, Deut. 32. 10, 18. 1 Sam. 2. 27, 29. chap. 63. 9, 10. Ezek. 16. 7, 20. Amos 2. 9, 13.

*{and*} Or, *but*. The copulative, for the adversative, as verse 20, 21.

*{rebelled*} As the word is used, 2 Kings 3. 7. & 8. 20. or, *transgressed*: as it is rendered, chap. 43. 27. Jer. 33. 8. yet disobedience and transgression is as rebellion, chap. 63. 10. 1 Sam. 15. 22, 23.

*{have rebelled*} Or, as it may well be rendered, *do rebel*, as v. 3. *know, know not, consider not*: as noting, not only their fore-passed rebellions, but their persisting still in them.

*{against me*} I set them up, and they set themselves against me. So Num. 16. 9, 11.

**V. 3.** *{The ox knoweth, &c.*} The very brute beasts, and the dullest of them (Psal. 32. 9. Prov. 7. 22. & 26. 3.) are brought in, by their carriage and courses toward their masters, and benefactors, such as feed them and make much of them; to control, and condemn the demeanor of God's people towards him, who took no notice of, nor regarded him that had done the like, and much more, for them, v. 2. So Jer. 8. 7.

*{ox knoweth*} Or, *oxen know*: *ox*, for *oxen*; and *ass*, for *asses*: as *vision*, for *visions*, ver. 1. and the like, verse 6. For those popish legendaries grossly and palpably abuse this place who out of it, have forged us a fable of an ox, and an ass; that being in the stable, where our Savior's mother was delivered of him, should take notice of him, and cherish him with their warm breath, as he lay in the cratch.

*{knoweth*} Takes notice of, regards; as Prov. 12. 10. chap. 42. 25. They so regard him, as not to offer to hurt, or wrong him; but are obsequious to him, however they be fierce, and offensive to others, Exod. 21. 28, 31.

*{his owner*} Or, *buyer*. Him, properly, that by bargain and sale, (Levit. 25. 28. chap. 24. 2. Ezek. 7. 12.) or more largely, that any way, or by any means, is possessed of him, Zach. 11. 5. It is given to God, as Lord and owner of all things, Gen. 14. 19, 22. but more especially, as by purchase, the possessor of his people, Deut. 32. 6.

*{and the ass*} The word here used, properly signifies the male; as another the female; but are both promiscuously used, as well for the one sex, as the other. As the word that signifies a *fish*, is used sometime in the masculine form; sometime in the feminine, of one and the same fish, Jon. 1. 17. and 2. 1. whatsoever the doting rabbins there dream of two fishes, a male, and a female. The word is used generally, to comprehend all of that kind, of whether sex, or for what use soever, as here, so elsewhere, Exod. 21. 33. as well those for burden, Gen. chap. 49. verse 14. as for the saddle, Exod. 4. 20.

*{his master's crib*} Heb. *the manger of his masters*. For the word is in a plural form; but such as is oft used in a singular sense: as of God, Mal. 1. 6. So of man, Exod. 21. 29, 36. He takes notice of him that brings him to the crib, or manger, and feeds him there: and to such a one God compares himself, Hos. 11. 4. *I was to them, as one that taketh the yoke off their jaws, and laieth them meat.*

*{but Israel, &c.*} The different, yea the contrary practice follows, of God's people towards God, as before, v. 2.

*{but*} Or, *yet*. A defect of the particle adversative, as v. 6. Psal. 30. 7.

*{Israel*} The name given to Jacob, (as he was at first called, Gen. 25. 25.) upon his wrestling with the angel, and prevailing therein, Gen. 32. 28. Hos. 12. 3. and transmitted from him, as the more honorable title, to his posterity; called sometime *the sons*, or, *children of Israel*, Gen. 32. 32. and 36. 31. and sometime simply, *Israel*, Gen. 48. 20. and 49. 7, 15. Psal. 149. 2. and so here. But so here styled in way of reproach, as having degenerated from him who first bore that name; nor answering to what it imported. So *Jeshurun*, though of itself a name of honor, Deut. 33. 26. yet in way of exprobation, enunciated of that people, Deut. 32. 15.

*{doth not know*} Heb. *hath not known*, see verse 2. *doth not know*, has not knowledge, or understanding: as Deut. 31. 13. Psal. 14. 4. *they are a people of no understanding*, Psal. 53. 4. so ch. 44. 18. *they know not, nor understand*. They have no more knowledge, nor understanding, than the brute beasts: Jer. 10. 8, 14. (whom yet, being endued by God with reasonable souls, they ought therein, to go beyond: Job 35. 11.) yea, herein they come short of them. Or, *doth not know me*, is ignorant of me: as Jer. 4. 22. and 9. 3. *they know not me, saith the Lord*: and, *there is no knowledge of God in the land*. Hos. 4. 1. But *know* here rather, for, *take notice of, respect, acknowledge*; as Psal. 1. 6. Prov. 27. 23. Jer. 2. 23. Mat. 7. 23. and 25. 12. *know not me*: a defect of the pronoun necessarily supplied, to make the sense perfect, as verse 15. They know not me, though their owner. Deut. 32. 6. their master. Mal. 1. 6. One, that from time to time have fed them; and most kindly entreated them, Deut. 8. 3, 4. and 32. 13, 14. They know not me, whom I have known above others, Amos 3. 2.

*{my people*} Who have been better taught than others, having been trained up under me. Deut. 4. 8, 14. Psal. 147. 19, 20. And to whom I have been more beneficial, than to any other. Psal. 105. 11, 45. Mal. 1. 2, 3.

*{doth not consider*} As the word is rendered, Psal. 37. 10. and 52. 15. Or, *understand*; as it is translated, Psal. 107. 43. either, they are of no understanding, as before, chap. 27. 11. Jer. 5. 4, 21. They are more blockish, and sottish, than the brute beasts; they have not so much understanding as they have: Jer. 8. 7. Or, they consider not the great things that God has done for them: nor the great goodness that he has from time to time showed them, Deut. 29. 2, 3, 4. Psal. 92. 5. chap. 42. 18, 20. Ezek. 12. 2. they neither take notice of him, nor think upon him.

**V. 4.** *{Ah sinful nation*} He proceeds here to aggravate their sins, and to bewail their misery thereby procured: so chap. 24. 16, 18. Jer. 9. 1, 2, 3.

*{ah*} The word here used, is sometimes a note of compellation; as chap. 55. 1. sometimes of denunciation, as chap. 5. 8, 11, 18, 20. (See chap. 10. 5. and 18. 1.) and so some take it in this place; sometime of lamentation, as 1 Kings 13. 30. chap. 6. 5. Jer. 22. 18. And so rather here: but sometimes mixed with indignation; as verse 21. and with detestation, as chap. 28. 1. And so it may well also be in this passage.

*{sinful*} Addicted, and given wholly to sin, and to looseness of life: Psal. 1. 1, 5. Luke 7. 34, 37. John 9. 31. Gal. 2. 15.

*{nation*} The term usually given to those people that lived without the pale of the church: and were strangers from the commonwealth of Israel, Eph. 2. 12. so Psal. 96. 5. chap. 11. 10. and 42. 6. and 61. 9. and 66. 19. Jer. 10. 2, 25. And which the Jews to this day, are wont in way of reproach, to style all other by, but their own. The prophet may the rather seem here to have used it; thereby partly to imply, that they had made themselves no better, if not in some respect worse, than any other people, in God's repute, by their sins and excesses, Jer. 9. 25, 26. Ezek. 5. 6, 7. And partly, to intimate the generality of their sin, and apostasy; which not some few, or more among them, but the main body of the nation, stood guilty of. It was a general defection, a national evil. chap. 59. 4. and 64. 6, 7. Jer. 5. 1. and 9. 2. Mic. 7. 3, 4. Mal. 3. 9. see verse 6.

*{a people laden with iniquity*} Heb. *a people of heaviness of iniquity*. Not laden with sin, as groaning under the burden of it: as Psal. 38. 4. Mat. 11. 28. But committing, and standing guilty of, not small so much, as heavy and heinous sins: *heavy*, for, *great*, and *grievous*: as chap. 21. 15. and 30. 27. and 36. 2. Great and grievous sinners: such as the Sodomites: Gen. 13. 13. and 18. 20. and as Eli's sons are said to have been, 1 Sam. 2. 17.

*{a seed of evil doers*} A wicked, and wretched race, that tread, and run on in the footsteps of their ungodly progenitors; and transmit their ungodliness unto those that come of them, Num. 32. 14. Psal. 78. 8. and 106. 6. chap. 57. 3. Jer. 7. 18, 26. and 16. 11, 12.

*{children that are corrupters*} Or, as some, *corrupt children*, *children, that deal corruptly*, 2 Chron. 27. 2. Jer. 6. 28. Or, that have *corrupted themselves*, Exod. 32. 7. Deut. 32. 5. and *their doings*: Zeph. 3. 7. Heb. *children corrupting*, or, *corrupters*, that is, *wasteful*: or, *wasters*; as Prov. 18. 9. or, *destroyers*, as Prov. 28. 24. *stroy-goods*; or *wasteful children*. A metaphor taken from riotous, or prodigal younkers; that waste, and consume their patrimony, the means left them by their parents. Luke 15. 13, 30. Applied to this people, as having embezzled their spiritual patrimony, derived and transmitted to them, from their religious predecessors, Gen. 17. 7. Deut. 7. 6, 8. and 32. 9, 20. Psal. 147. 19, 20. and 148. 14. Rom. 3. 1. and 9. 4, 5.

*{they have forsaken the Lord*} By refusing to walk according to the prescript of his law: and by following false gods, and addicting themselves unto the service of such, verse 28. Jer. 1. 16. and 2. 13. and 16. 11. and 22. 9. See chap. 2. 6.

*{the Lord*} Heb. *Jehovah*. See verse 2.

*{they have provoked unto anger*} As Num. 14. 11, 23. and 16. 30. Or *despised, contemned, set light by*: as Deut. 31. 20. Psal. 107. 11. Prov. 1. 30. and 15. 5. or, *abhorred*, as Deut. 32. 19. 1 Sam. 2. 17. Jer. 14. 21. or, *reproached, blasphemed*, as 2 Sam. 12. 14. Psal. 10. 13. and 74. 10, 18. chap. 52. 5. They so carried themselves, in their wicked courses, sinning with a high hand; Num. 15. 30, 31. As if they did what they did, on purpose, to provoke God to wrath, chap. 3. 8. and 65. 3. Jer. 7. 18, 19. and 27. 10.

*{the holy one*} *The holy God*, or *Lord*; a defect of the substantive, as chap. 5. 19, 24. so verse 24. to be supplied: as chap. 5. 16. he, who both is holy himself, chap. 6. 3. and sanctifies those that are his; Levit. 19. 2. and 20. 7, 8. Ezek. 20. 12.

*{of Israel*} Who was in covenant with them, and was to be worshiped, and served by them: Deut. 6. 5, 6. and 26. 27, 28. so Psal. 89. 18. Of the name, See verse 3.

*{they are gone away backward*} Heb. *they are severed, or alienated, or estranged backward*. That is, *they are severed*, or *alienated*, (to wit, from him) *and turned backward*; or, *gone*, or, *go backward*: A defective speech; the like whereunto see chap. 38. 14, 17, 21. as also in the like argument, Hos. 9. 10. *they are severed*, or *have separated themselves* (to wit, from the Lord) *unto that shame*, or *shameful thing*; that is, and betaken themselves to it.

*{gone away*} Or, *alienated*: they have *severed*, or *estranged* themselves from God by their sins, Psal. 58. 3. chap. 59. 2. Eph. 4. 18, 19. Col. 1. 21. by their idolatry especially, Ezek. 14. 5, 7. Where yet the same word is rendered, *estranged*, in the former place; and *separated himself*, in the latter place: as if the words there used, came from two several roots. And in like manner the Jewish critics, speak doubtfully of the word here used; one while referring it to that root, that has a notion of *separation*: Levit. 22. 2. Another while to that which has a notion of *alienation*, Job 19. 13. Psal. 78. 30. But whether way we here take it, it will come in effect to one: *separation*, or *estrangement*, in the present case, being in a manner the same.

*{backward*} It seems a metaphor taken, either, from undutiful children, or servants; that turn their back on their parents, or masters, in disdain, when they like not what they are bidden to do: Jer. 2. 27. and 15. 6. and 32. 33. Ezek. 8. 16. Or, from restive jades, that go the more backward, the more the rider, or driver, strives to put them on forward. See verse 5.

**V. 5.** *{Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more, and more*} Or, may be read, as one continued sentence, Thus, *Why, the more ye are, are stricken, do ye more and more revolt?* Or, *why should ye be stricken any more; since ye will, or do, revolt more and more?* What avails it, to seek, or strive to amend you, by chastisements: (Gen. 6. 3. Psal. 95. 10, 11. Jer. 5. 3.) when as the more you are chastised, the worse you wax: 2 Chr. 28. 22. Jer. 7. 24.

*{stricken*} With variety of judgments: which are as God's rods, or strokes, Deut. 28. 22, 27, 28. 2 Sam. 7. 14. Psal. 89. 32. Amos 4. 9. Mic. 6. 9.

*{ye will*} Or, *since that ye will*; a defect of the particle, as Job 32. 22. and 38. 21.

*{will*} Or, *do*; the future for the present: as Deut. 25. 3. Ruth 1. 17. 1 Sam. 3. 17. See chap. 3. 16.

*{revolt more and more*} Heb. *increase*; or, *add revolt*: as verse 13. chap. 7. 10. Clean contrary to that which God intended in smiting them: he smote them to reclaim them, and bring them home to him; chap. 9. 12, 13. Amos 4. 6, 11. And they took occasion thereby, to go further away from him, Jer. 44. 17, 18, 21, 22. See verse 4.

*{the whole head is sick*} The whole state, both civil, and ecclesiastical, is distempered, and out of frame: and those worst, and weakest, that should support and strengthen the rest; Psal. 75. 3. and 82. 5. So some, understanding it of their excess of sin, and wickedness; in such especially, as were as the *head*, and *heart* of the state: Numb. 25. 4. Mic. 3. 1, 9. But it seems rather to be spoken of their lamentable condition; by means of God's judgments inflicted on them, for their sins. The evils, that have befallen, and lie still heavy upon you, are both general; few or none escaping scot-free in them; and withal sore, and grievous, like hurts received (Gen. 3. 15. Psal. 68. 21.) or diseases lying in the head. 2 Kings 4. 19, 20. Or, such as strike, and pierce to the heart: Jer. 4. 18, 19. and 8. 18.

*{the whole head*} Or, *every head*: as Ezek. 29. 18.

*{is sick*} Heb. *unto sickness*: or, *in sickness*. For so the particle here used, is observed, oft to signify, Psal. 16. 10. Hos. 7. 3. In a lamentable plight; in a grievous disease: 2 Chr. 21. 18. Psal. 38. 7. The phrase is emphatical: as *in sin; in iniquity*. Psal. 51. 5. John 9. 34. *In the gall of bitterness; and in the bond of iniquity*, Acts 8. 23. Not lightly touched with it, but wholly possessed of it.

*{and the whole heart*} As noting the extremity of the evil, Psal. 22. 14. and 25. 17. and 102. 4. Or, *every heart*; as implying the generality of it. see verse 4. chap. 2. 9. The Jewish doctor refers it to that commination, Deut. 28. 28.

*{is faint*} It is, as with women in their infirmity of course, Levit. 15. 33. and 20. 18. or, *languishing*, Lam. 1. 22. and 5. 17. As with those that pine away, through grief, or affliction, or by means of some lingering and wasting disease, Deut. 7. 15. and 28. 60. 2 Sam. 13. 4. Lam. 1. 13.

**V. 6.** *{From the sole of the foot, even unto the head*} You have been so scourged, over and over, that there is no part free, from top to toe: a proverbial speech; the use whereof, see 2 Sam. 14. 25. Job 2. 7. The meaning is: that in the calamities and afflictions, which in those times had befallen them, none had escaped God's hand; but all, as well greatest and highest, as least and lowest had suffered: they had been plagued all, one with another: 2 Chron. 28. 5, 8.

*{the sole*} The Hebrew word signifies, *bending*, or, *hollow*; and it is applied sometimes to the foot, as here, *the sole*, Deut. 2. 5. and 11. 24. Sometimes to the hand, *the palm*, Levit. 14. 15, 18, 19. Sometimes to the thigh, *the hollow*, wherein the hucklebone rests, Gen. 32. 25, 32.

*{even*} Heb. *and*: as Deut. 4. 32.

*{unto the head*} Inclusively, taking it with the rest of the body: as 2 Chron. 34. 30. Psal. 14. 3. Jer. 8. 10. Elsewhere more fully: *unto the top, or crown of the head*, Deut. 28. 35. Job 2. 7.

*{there is no soundness*} Or, *nothing, no part sound*: so is the word used, Exod. 29. 1. Levit. 9. 2, 3. Or, as some, *there is no shape of a man*: for, so is the word taken, Jud. 20. 48. He compares the Jewish state, to a man's body; so generally possessed with some malignant disease, that no part of it is sound, or free, either from the inward taint, or the outward symptoms thereof: or to such a body, as either by the like malignity, or by sore and often scourging, or evil usage otherwise, is with tumors, and ulcers, so overspread, that no shape or figure of a man, almost, appears on it. So Psal. 38. 3, 7. where the very same phrase, is found.

*{but wounds*} The adversative particle is wanting, as verse 3.

*{wounds*} Heb. *wound*; taken collectively, as Prov. 20. 30. So *bruise*, and *sore*, or *stripe*, and *stroke*, afterwards, of which see, verse 1. *vision*, and verse 3. *ox*, and *ass*. Yet there seems to be some emphasis in it: nothing but *wound*, and *bruise, stripe*, or *mark*: as if the party were so to be martyred, as we use to say, that the whole body might seem to be, but as *one wound, one stripe, one ulcer, one tumor, one sore*.

*{bruises*} Heb. *bruise*. The word properly signifies the mark of a stripe formerly given; remaining still to be seen on the body, Psal. 38. 5. Prov. 20. 30. chap. 53. 5. The Jewish critics thus distinguish, this and the former. A *wound*, say they, is that which makes a breach in the flesh, and brings out blood; a *bruise*, such as makes no breach in the skin or flesh, but coagulates the blood under the skin.

*{putrifying sores*} Heb. *moist*. That is, either *green hurts*; as *a green jawbone*, Judg. 15. 15. New hurts, lately made. Or, as other *matur*: moist with matter: such as old festered sores use to be. The word is said to be in Arabic writers, used for a *green wound*: but in the Talmudic language, says one of the Jewish commenters, for a *matury sore*.

*{sores*} Heb. *stroke*; as Lev. 26. 21. Chap. 14. 7. and 27. 7. Jer. 30. 12. see verse 5. *stroke*, for *strokes*, as before; so verse 13.

*{they have not been, &c.*} No means, at least, available, have been used for the cure or removal of these evils wherewith our state is thus surprised, and defaced, see 2 Chron. 28. 13. Expressed here by metaphorical phrases, borrowed from the art and practice of surgery: the like whereunto are found, Psal. 60. 2. and 147. 3. chap. 3. 7. Jer. 30. 12, 13.

*{closed*} To make up the wound, or the breach in the body: chap. 30. 26. Or, *crushed*, rather: (for so the word properly signifies) as chap. 59. 5. or, *wrung out*. As Jud. 6. 38. To express, and force out the mature: as in the festered sores, where the corrupt mature must be removed, before they be closed, or made up. Yet one of the Jewish commenters seems to understand it of *washing*: as wounds are wont to be, commonly, before they be closed: referring us to Job 18. 15. *Brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.* And then it would be rendered *sprinkled*, or *syringed*: but the roots are divers. And another, whom he also cites, is too large, who renders it, *healed*; building on, Jer. 30. 13. Whereof in its place.

*{neither bound up*} As wounds and sores wont to be, when the purulent matur is wrought out; to keep out wind, and air: and to cause the lips of the wound, or sore, to solder, Chap. 3. 7. and 61. 1. Ezek. 30. 21. Hos. 6. 1.

*{neither mollified*} Psal. 55. 21.

*{with ointment*} Heb. *oil*. As Eccles. 7. 1. and 9. 8. To assuage the swellings: and to supple the sores, Ezek. 16. 4.

**V. 7.** *{Your country*} Or, *land*. Heb. *earth*: as chap. 1. 19, 21. He proceeds to declare the miserable condition of their state; by the lamentable devastation, and desolation of their land. So Jer. 4. 21, 26.

*{is*} The verb substantive to be supplied; most render, in the present tense, *is*: understanding it of such waste, as had already been made of it, by the Syrians, and others joining with the Israelites, under Ahaz: 2 Chron. 28. Others render it, in the future; *shall be*: supposing it a prediction, of an evil to come: but the former is rather to be admitted, see verse 5.

*{desolate*} Heb. *desolation*. That is, *most desolate*. As desolate, as desolation itself: so chap. 64. 10. The abstract for the concrete, as Jer. 27. 16. Ezek. 25. 13. & 35. 4. Or, brought *unto desolation*: as Jer. 12. 11. or, is *in desolation*, the particle wanting: as Job 1. 18. In *desolation*, as *in sickness*, verse 5. see chap. 3. 26.

*{your cities are burnt*} By the enemy; either in the surprisal of them, or afterward, in the extremity of rage, to satisfy their fury: or, that they might not be places of refuge, or habitation again, to those that formerly held them. Josh. 11. 11. Jer. 37. 8, 10.

*{your land*} *Your ground*; Or, tilled land. Gen. 2. 5. & 3. 17. and 4. 2, 12.

*{strangers*} The Syrians, Edomites, Philistines, and others, 2 Chron. 28. 5, 17, 18. chap. 9. 12.

*{devour it*} That is, consume, and eat up the fruit of it, Deut. 28. 33, 51, 53. Jer. 5. 17. *It*, or *your land*; for, the fruit of it, as *the tenth of the land*, Levit. 27. 30. For *the tenth of the fruit of it*, Deut. 26. 12. See Lev. 26. 16. Jer. 5. 17.

*{in your presence*} Heb. *before you*. Before your faces, in your sight, to increase your grief, being unable, either to rescue aught from them, or to restrain their rage, Deut. 28. 32, 33, 34, 51, 52.

*{and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers*} Heb. *according to the overthrow of strangers*. That is, say some of the Jewish doctors, such as those of Sodom and Gomorrah, verse 9. people *estranged* from the fear of God, who were therefore overthrown by God; and the word *overthrown* shall be taken passively, Jer. 49. 18. But rather, as strangers are wont to overthrow a land, making havoc of all before them, as being none of their own; nor like long to enjoy it: And so it is taken actively, as Jer. 50. 40. Amos 4. 11. See the like phrase, Deut. 29. 23. chap. 13. 19. But as those Jewish doctors pervert the sense; so those of them also corrupt the text, that instead of the word that signifies *strangers*, would substitute another somewhat like it; that signifies a *storm*; Chap. 25. 4. and 28. 2. As alluding to those Egyptian storms, Exod. 9. 23, 25.

**V. 8.** *{And &c.*} From the condition of the whole land, and state, he passes here unto the state of the chief city, see Jer. 15. 8. and 34. 1.

*{the daughter of Zion*} Or, *the daughter Zion*, Psal. 9. 15. Zach. 2. 10. and 9. 9. As *the daughter of Zidon*, or, *the daughter Zidon*, chap. 23. 12. (for so it would rather be rendered) for *Zion* itself, and *Zidon* itself. Or, if it be the former way rendered, it is no otherwise to be understood; than as when we say, *the city of Rome*, and, *the city of London*; and the Evangelist, *the feast of Passover*: Luke 2. 41. And the apostle Paul, *the sign of circumcision*, Rom. 4. 11. that is, *circumcision*, which is *a sign*, or, *for a sign*: and so *Zion*, that is, as *a daughter*; because the speech is metaphorical: see chap. 3. 1. For, they are far out of the way, who by *daughter of Zion*, conceit it to be meant (which conceit yet some great ones seem taken with) either a parcel of buildings, branching out of the old [unclear], or, the whole nether city, as descending from, or issuing out of it: not considering, how absurd a thing it is, to imagine, that from some inferior, and meaner part, the denomination, as here it is, should be given to the whole city: nor observing, or attending at least, the usual manner of Scripture wherein great cities, and states, as compared to goodly, and beautiful *daughters*, or *damsels*, are commonly so styled: See of Babel, chap. 47. 1. Of Egypt, Jer. 47. 11. Of Edom, Lam. 4. 21. And of others, elsewhere. Though of Zion, it is not improbable, that God in a more special manner, does here so speak: as the prophet in the like, Jer. 9. 1. Because as dear to him, as a daughter: (see chap. 22. 4.) That which makes the misery the more strange, and grievous: that one so dear to God, should be so destroyed, or distressed, Lam. 1. 15. and 2. 1, 2. and 4. 12.

*{Zion*} That is, *Jerusalem*. So termed, from a principal part of it: to wit, that mountain, or upper part. 2 Sam. 5. 6, 7. Wherein both God's temple, and the king's palace, were seated: Psal. 2. 6. and 48. 2. Zach. 9. 9. See chap. 2. 2, 3. and 14. 13.

*{is left*} Not by the *keeper*, that is, God, Psal. 121. 4, 5. *the keeper of Israel*; as some of the Jewish commenters expound it: but left standing alone by itself, as other of them better: like such a *lodge*, or *cottage*, hereafter described, that has no other housing usually about it, or near it: and so Jerusalem; all about her being destroyed, and laid waste: either, as some of them apply it, by the Assyrian invasion, chap. 7. 17, 20. and 36. 1, 2. or rather, by the waste of the land, made in Ahaz his reign, by the Syrians and Israelites, 2 Chron. 28. 5, 8, 17, 20.

*{as a cottage in a vineyard*} As a *shed*, or, a *booth*, set up in the midst, or on the one side of a vineyard, for the keeper there to watch; or repose himself in. Job 27. 18. ch. 4. 6.

*{as a lodge*} Made for the gardener to lodge, or rest in, chap. 24. 20. Lam. 2. 6.

*{in a garden of cucumbers*} Or, *melons*. A fruit frequent, as in Egypt, so in those eastern parts, Num. 11. 5. Howbeit it seems a mere nicety, which from the Chaldee paraphrast, one of the Jewish doctors here has, that it is not said, *in a garden*, simply, but *in a garden of melons*, as before *in a vineyard*; because, in a garden, there may be still use and need of a keeper, though this, or that plant, or fruit be gone; whereas in a vineyard, or field of melons, when the grapes are gathered in the one, and the melons gone in the other, there is now no need or use of a keeper in either: For this is grounded upon a misexposition, before mentioned.

*{as a besieged city*} Heb. *kept, watched*. As Ezek. 6. 12. Or, as some, *wasted*, as chap. 65. 4. where some, as here also, strain the word over far, to make it signify, a place so defaced and horrid, that men shun it, and keep aloof from it for fear, as Psal. 30. 11. Nahum 3. 7. but the former rather: As desolate, in regard of the country round about; so in great distress itself, being so straitened, that none can go in, or out, in safety, 1 Kings 15. 17. 2 Kings 6. 24, 25. and 18. 27. Jer. 4. 16, 17. and 5. 6.

**V. 9.** *{Except, &c.*} From the devastation of the country, and distress of the city, he proceeds now to the consumption of the people; appearing by the paucity of the persons surviving. See ch. 4. 1.

*{the Lord*} That all is not clean gone, and utterly destroyed, it is God's gracious work, his great and mere mercy, Lam. 3. 22.

*{the Lord of hosts*} Heb. *Jehovah Sabaoth*. Which some suppose to be a defective form of speech, thus to be supplied, *The Lord*, or, *Jehovah, the God of Hosts*, as Levit. 12. 5. But that needs not, since that we have the one without the other, frequently in the prophets; so with the apostles, Rom. 9. 29. Jam. 5. 4. Nor hinders it, that the word is not in a contracted form: for the word, *Elohim*, is also, oft-times, used in the very same phrase entire; four times in one Psalm, Psal. 80. 4, 7, 14, 19. And this may be the privilege of the word, *Jehovah*, that it admits no such contraction: the rather, if it have (as may well be deemed) a prick, or point, in its last letter, as *Jah*, and *Eloah*, both have: which keeps the word, so marked, always entire. For the word itself, see verse 2. The *Jehovah*, or, *the Lord of hosts*. That is the powerful, and sovereign commander of all the creatures, in heaven, and earth; which are, as his hosts, ready prest to do him service, Gen. 2. 1. and 32. 1, 2. Josh. 10. 11, 13. Judg. 5. 10, 11. Psal. 68. 17. and 103. 21. and 119. 91. and 148. 8. chap. 14. 26, 27. Joel 2. 11, 25. Mat. 26. 33. Luke 2. 13. See further, verse 24.

*{had left unto us*} Had rescued, and reserved some few of us, as brands snatched out of the fire, Amos 4. 11. Zach. 3. 2. That which God does in mercy, that he may have some ever to serve him, and to be monuments of his mercy, Psal. 130. 3, 4. chap. 4. 3. & 6. 13. Mat. 24. 21, 22. See Rom. 9. 27, 29.

*{unto us*} The prophet, very frequently, here varies the person, speaking sometime, as in the person of God, verse 2, 3. Sometime, as in his own person, verse 4. Sometime in the person of his people; and so here: the usual manner of the pathetic speeches.

*{a very small remnant*} A handful, in regard of the whole. A very poor, and sorry company, in regard of those that had perished in the calamities of the times, chap. 10. 22. and 17. 6. *a remnant* only, and that *very small*. So is the word used, Psal. 105. 12. Ezek. 16. 47. Yet some render it, *almost*, (and it is also frequently so used, Gen. 26. 10. Psal. 94. 12. and 119. 87.) referring it to the latter clause, *We had almost been as Sodom, &c.* But the pointing in the original, carries it rather the other way.

*{we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah*} We should have been utterly ruined, and consumed; (none, or nothing left of us) as those cities, and the regions adjacent were, with all their inhabitants, Gen. 19. 24, 25. Deut. 29. 23. Lam. 4. 6. Amos 4. 11. The defect of the copulative, makes the sentence the quicker, as verse 3, 4, 8. and needed not therefore to have been expressed.

**V. 10.** *{Hear*} Here God begins to turn the tenor of his speech, from the heaven and earth, unto those, whom what he had before said, concerned; to the princes of Judah, and the people. And his speech to them, he enters upon here, with a very tart and sharp increpation; and continues, afterward, with no less vehement and passionate expostulation, verse 11, &c. Nor is this, as some have thought, the beginning of some new sermon, but a continued pursuit of the former discourse.

*{hear*} Hear you, whom that which I speak, concerns, so, Mic. 6. 1, 2, 3. Mal. 2. 1, 2.

*{the word of the Lord*} The word of me, who am the Lord, (Heb. *Jehovah*.) So after here, verse 20. See ch. 2. 1.

*{ye Princes*} You first, because the worst; and by your example encouraging others, to do evil. See v. 28.

*{of Sodom*} Like them for wickedness, Deut. 32. 32. as bad as they, or worse rather, Ezek. 16. 46, 48. and justly therefore deserving to be destroyed, as they were. See verse 9. from whence he takes the hint of the terms, here given.

*{give ear unto the law*} Or, *doctrine*. Not the law delivered you sometime by Moses; but those lessons, (though consonant to that) and that message, which from God I now bring, and deliver unto you in his name. So the word, *Law*, is used, Psal. 78. 1. Prov. 1. 8. and 3. 1, 21. and 6. 20.

*{of our God*} The God whom we profess to serve, and whom, both you, and we, ought to hear and obey; so chap. 55. 7. Yet here speaking to them who neither regarded to hear, nor take notice of him: he says *our God*, as not theirs; who owned not him, verse 3. as God afterward; *your sacrifices*, as not his, because not owned by him, from them, v. 11.

*{ye people of Gomorrah*} People as like them, as if you were of the same lineage, as Ezek. 16. 3. and in the same repute with me, as Amos 9. 7.

*{Gomorrah*} So Rom. 9. 29. Jude 7. as *Gaza*, Acts 8. 26. Heb. *Amorah*, as *Amos*, v. 1.

**V. 11.** *{To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me, saith the Lord*} Heb. *upon what*, or *for what*. Not, as demanding, as some would have it, on what part he should smite them; there being already no part free: nor, as others, with what new plague he should smite them: as having tried them with such variety of judgments already. But *For*; or, *To what*, to wit, *end?* in plainer terms: *wherefore?* or, *why?* as the same term is used, Psal. 10. 1. But here the words run expressly thus; *To what end*; or *purpose, unto me?* that is, either, brought *to me?* or, *in regard of me?* as if I liked them, or accepted of them. It is spoken in way of expostulation, as Jer. 6. 20. implying, that all they did in their daily devotions, was in vain, to no end; all but lost labor: neither grateful to God, nor useful therefore to themselves: not unaccepted with God only, but abhorred of him, and abominable in his sight, v. 13.

*{is the multitude of your sacrifices?*} Or, *your multitude of sacrifices*. That is, *your many sacrifices*. As, *a multitude of words*: for, *many words*, Prov. 10. 19. and, *thy multitude of witchcrafts*: For, *thy manifold witchcrafts*, chap. 47. 11. Now such sacrifices as these, though God had commanded to be brought, and offered to him, as all the other duties ensuing, to be done; yet being done, as well the one, as the other, by such as they were, and in such manner as they did them, without hearty repentance, and due devotion: he refuses to own them, and accept them; he rejects them, as not his, but theirs. See v. 10. *our God*. So Psal. 50. 8, 16. Prov. 15. 8. and 21. 27. chap. 61. 8. and 66. 3. Jer. 6. 20. and 7. 21. Amos 5. 21, 22. Mic. 6. 7.

*{I am full of*} I am cloyed with them, as a man is with some meat which he loathes, and his stomach goes against, Psal. 107. 18. Prov. 27. 7. and is ready, even to cast up again, Prov. 25. 16. Rev. 3. 16.

*{the burnt-offerings*} Such as were wholly consumed with fire, Levit. 1. 3, 9. Psal. 40. 6. and 51. 19. Mar. 12. 33. Heb. 10. 6.

*{of rams*} Male sheep, above a year old. For, those that came short of that age, go under the name of *lambs*, Exod. 12. 5. Levit. 1. 10. Of *lambs* was the daily sacrifice, Numb. 28. 3. Of *rams*, those in their principal solemnities, Numb. 28. 11, 27. and upon some other special occasions, Levit. 5. 15. & 6. 6. & 8. 2. 1 Sam. 15. 22. Psal. 66. 15.

*{and of the fat*} Not of the flesh, or the body of the beast, (for that, the Hebrews have two other words to express, Psal. 63. 5. and 109. 24. and it might lawfully be eaten, Neh. 8. 10. chap. 25. 6. & 55. 2.) but the *fat*, or *suet*, that is about the flank, and the kidneys, or about, and upon the entrails, Levit. 3. 3, 4. which out of all the sacrifices, was reserved as God's portion, to be burnt upon his altar, Levit. 3. 15, 16. & 4. 8, 10. & 17. 6. Deut. 32. 38. 1 Sam. 2. 15, 16. (alluded to, Psal. 37. 20.) and is forbidden therefore to be eaten by any, Levit. 3. 17. & 7. 23, 25.

*{of fed beasts*} Not fat beasts, but fatted on purpose, Luke 15. 23, 27. the best and choicest you can bring, 2 Sam. 6. 13. 1 Kings 1. 9. Amos 5. 22.

*{I delight not in*} Heb. *have not delighted*. See v. 2, 3. Though he much delighted in the good affection, and obedience of his faithful people expressed in, and testified by such performances, Gen. 4. 4. and 8. 21. Psal. 20. 3. & 51. 19. Mal. 3. 4. Yet not at all, in the things themselves simply considered, Psal. 50. 15. (howsoever the Gentiles had such a fond and gross conceit of him, as of their own false gods, Deut. 32. 37, 38.) much less in them, by such persons, and in such manner performed, ch. 57. 6. Jer. 7. 22, 23.

*{the blood*} Reserved, as the fat, to make atonement for their souls, Levit. 17. 11. As a type of the Messiah his blood, whereby our propitiation, and peace with God is procured, and purchased, Rom. 3. 25. Eph. 1. 7. Col. 1. 14, 20. Heb. 9. 12, 22. The principal cause of the prohibition of eating blood, Lev. 7. 26, 27. & 17. 10, 12.

*{of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he-goats*} Of these three kinds of cattle only their sacrifices were, *bullocks*, or *heifers* of the herd; *sheep*, or, *goats*, of the flock, Gen. 15. 9. Levit. 1. 2, 3, 10. & 4. 23. Numb. 19. 1. Psal. 50. 9. & 66. 15.

*{lambs*} Because *rams* were mentioned before, Psal. 37. 20.

*{he-goats*} The Hebrew word signifies the greater sort of that kind, chap. 14. 9. Jer. 50. 8. For there is another word that signifies ordinarily, *Male goats*, Gen. 37. 31. Levit. 4. 23. and *goats*, in general, a third. Levit. 1. 10. & 3. 12. See before, *fed beasts*.

**V. 12.** *{When ye come to appear before me*} Which thrice a year, all their males were enjoined to do, Exod. 23. 17. & 34. 23. Deut. 16. 16. As also upon other occasions, many of them, oft, at other times, did, 1 Sam. 10. 3. Psal. 42. 2, 4. & 66. 13.

*{to appear*} Heb. *to be seen*. As Exod. 34. 23. Deut. 31. 11. Which, though the ordinary phrase of such access and approach, yet may here have some emphasis, more than ordinary: as implying, that they repaired thither, only to be seen there; and that was all the good that thereby they gained. So our Savior of the Pharisees, Mat. 6. 2, 5, 16.

*{before me*} In my house, in my temple: the place of my special residence, Deut. 12. 5, 11. Psal. 42. 2. & 84. 7. & 95. 2. Jer. 7. 10.

*{who hath required this*} Or, *who doth require it?* As before, *I delight not*, verse 11. yet had he required it, Deut. 12. 5, 6. But not so much that, as other things, which he more regarded, Jer. 7. 21, 23. Ezek. 20. 39, 40. and that from such as were accordingly qualified, Levit. 10. 3. Ezek. 14. 3, 4. So that it is, as if he had said; I neither desire, nor require, either the company of you, or aught from you: What I required sometime of my people, I require not now so of you: being such as you are, and coming so as you do. Against whom therefore, he wishes his temple doors shut, Mal. 1. 10.

*{at your hand*} Heb. *from your hand*. That is, *of you*, or, *from you*, as 2 Sam. 4. 11. Mal. 1. 9, 10, 13. Yet, there may be some eye to their hands, being such as he says they were, v. 15.

*{to tread*} Or, *trample on*. As ch. 63. 3. As if by repairing to his house, they did but trample upon the pavement of it, as a company of beasts would do; and foul it only, and wear out the stones of it, with their feet. That was all the good they did, or was gotten by their appearance there, Ezek. 23. 38, 39.

*{my courts*} The courts of the temple, or sanctuary, Psal. 84. 2. and 116. 19. which were principally two; the inner court, wherein the priests and Levites ministered; and the outer court, wherein the people met, 2 Chr. 4. 9. Ezek. 40. 31, 44. Luke 1. 10. This reproof therefore seems to reach the priests, as well as the people. Howsoever, *courts* may be put for *court*, as chap. 62. 9. And the great court, into which the people had free access, seems to have been divided into divers partitions. See Jer. 26. 10. and that also is styled the temple: for there they were whom our Savior drove out, Mat. 21. 12, 14.

**V. 13.** *{Bring no more*} Heb. *add not to bring*, as verse 5. chap. 23. 12. He would rather have none brought, than any brought in that manner: rather not be served at all, than to be served by such, Jer. 7. 21. Ezek. 20. 39. Mal. 1. 10.

*{vain oblations*} Heb. *an oblation of vanity*, as, Lam. 2. 14. *Oblation*, for, *oblations*, as verse 1, 6.

*{oblations*} Meat-offerings. Sometime offered alone, Levit. 2. 1. Sometime additionals to other sacrifices, Numb. 15. 4. The word signifies, in general, a present solemnly tendered unto God, or man; in acknowledgment of honorable respect to either, or for procurement of grace and favor with either, Gen. 4. 3, 5. & 32. 13, 18, 20, 21. & 43. 11. 1 Sam. 10. 27. 2 Kings 20. 12. Psal. 45. 12. in regard whereof, it is by some deemed to descend from a word that signifies, *to bring*; by others, from one that signifies, *to pacify*, or make quiet. But it is more specially applied to some certain sort of religious oblations; whereof, see further on ch. 57. 6.

*{vain*} Because a service, not sincerely, but feignedly, performed, chap. 29. 13. & 59. 4. Lam. 2. 14. Or, *vain*, because in vain offered, as not regarded, nor accepted, Gen. 4. 4. verse 11. Mal. 1. 9, 10. and 2. 13. Mat. 15. 9.

*{incense*} Both that which the priests daily burnt on the golden altar, Exod. 30. 3, 7, 8, 35, 36. As that also which the people brought, together with their offerings, Levit. 2. 1, 2.

*{is an abomination to me*} Heb. *abomination it to me*. *It*, for, *is*. The pronoun, for the verb substantive: a thing in Hebrew very frequent, Psal. 44. 4. Eccles. 1. 5, 10. & 5. 9. *Abomination*, that is, *very abominable*, Levit. 18. 22. As *desolation*, for *very desolate*, verse 7. That which was formerly reputed, a pleasing, and pleasant savor unto God, Exod. 29. 7, 8. Psal. 141. 2. Ezek. 20. 41. That now, from them, as a thing most unsavory, and of evil scent, he utterly abhors, Levit. 26. 31.

*{the new moons, and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies*} Or, *the calling of assemblies, in the new moons, and the sabbaths*. A defect of the particle, *in*, as Jer. 9. 2. so Numb. 12. 8. Psalm 10. 4. and elsewhere.

*{new moons*} Heb. *new moon*, as Psal. 81. 2. So, *sabbath*, and *assembly*. See verse 1, 3, 6.

*{sabbaths*} Either weekly, or yearly, Levit. 23. 3, 32, 38, 39.

*{calling of assemblies*} Heb. *to call*; Or, *proclaim a convocation*. Which was done in those solemn times of convening, by sound of trumpet, as well to give warning to the people of meeting, as to incite them unto due preparation of themselves thereunto, Numb. 10. 2, 7, 10. Psal. 81. 2. Joel 2. 2, 15. A learned annotator, lately divulged, gives two other readings here; either taking the words absolutely, *As for the new moons and sabbaths, and calling of assemblies*. Or, with supply from the former branch, *Add not to call*, that is, *call no more meetings, on the new moons and sabbaths*. Which latter I mislike not.

*{I cannot away with*} Heb. only, *I cannot*: Or *am not*: or, *shall not be able*; to wit, to bear it, or, to endure it any longer, or the like: *I cannot*; for, *I cannot bear*: as, *ye could not*; and *ye cannot*; for, *ye could not bear*; and, *ye cannot bear*, 1 Cor. 3. 2. and, *I could not*; for, *I could not forbear*, Jer. 20. 9. An imperfect speech, intimating an inexpressible measure or degree of discontent. Such a burden it was to him, that he was even tired out with it, and no longer able to endure it. See v. 14. Jer. 44. 22. Amos 2. 13.

*{it is iniquity*} So most interpreters. As declaring the cause, why these offices were so displeasing to him, in regard of the iniquity inherent in those by whom they were performed, or adhering to the duties in their performance of them, Psal. 66. 18. Prov. 15. 8. & 22. 27. chap. 43. 23, 24. Others rather, *it is an affliction*, or, *a grievance*, as the word is used, Job 5. 6. ch. 10. 1. and oft elsewhere. And this seems the more probable.

*{even the solemn meeting*} So it is generally rendered; or, much to the same purpose. Yet with that late learned annotator, I find this last clause thus fastened to the words foregoing, *I cannot endure iniquity, and a convent*: that is, says he, a solemn meeting joined together with wickedness, as with you it is: And much to the same purpose, with one only before him: but in another construction, *iniquity, and congregation*, that is, *a wicked congregation*. As *a consumption, and determination*, for, *a determinate consumption*, chap. 10. 23. And it is true that such kind of construction as this, is not unusual: of which, see chap. 4. 5, 6. As also that the word here used, and another not unlike it, do both sometime signify, *a solemn assembly*, or *day of restraint*, Jer. 9. 2. Joel 1. 14. So termed, because the people were thereon restrained, from their ordinary employments, and affairs, Levit. 23. 7, 8, 21, 24, 25, 27, 31. For thence, I suppose it rather so termed, than as that learned annotator, because it *closed*, or *concluded* the festival, being given therefore to the last day thereof, Levit. 23. 36. Numb. 25. 35. Deut. 16. 8. 2 Chron. 7. 9. for the word is used more generally, of days of such solemn meeting, with the like restraint implied, Amos 5. 21. and that also, where no other of that nature at all had then preceded, as 2 Kings 10. 20. Joel 2. 14. But yet to me it seems rather to have a signification of *vexation*. As another of the same original has the like, Psal. 107. 39. ch. 53. 8. And so the words may well be rendered, *It is a grievance or affliction and a vexation, to me*. The last words are to be supplied from the former clause, concerning incense. So verse 14.

**V. 14.** *{Your new moons*} Both the solemnities themselves, and the sacrifices offered in them. Numb. 10. 10. 2 Chr. 31. 3.

*{your appointed feasts*} Heb. *set meetings*. And so it would rather be rendered, more generally, both here, and Hos. 2. 11. to comprehend, as well *fasts*, as *feasts*, Levit. 23. 2, 4, 27, 37. see ch. 58. 3, 6. and of the word, further, on ch. 14. 13.

*{my soul hateth*} *I hate*, or, *I abhor*, as Job 6. 7. or, *I hate* them *from my heart*, Psal. 11. 5. Prov. 6. 16. Zach. 11. 8.

*{they are a trouble to me*} Or, *a cumbrance*. As Deut. 1. 12. where *burden*, and it, are joined together. They are such an encumbrance, as wearies, and tires me out. Job 37. 11.

*{I am weary to bear them*} Or *with bearing of them*. Or, *of bearing them*. For so we use to speak: as Gen. 19. 11. *they were weary*, or, *wearied, to find*, (that is, of seeking, or, with seeking to find) *the door*. And Jer. 6. 11. *I am weary with holding.* See verse 13. Jer. 15. 6. and 20. 19. a defect of the pronoun: as verse 3, 15.

**V. 15.** *{And when, &c.*} Or, *when also*. As Jer. 1. 3. Neither your sacrifices, and oblations; nor your suits, and supplications: the incense of your prayers, Psalm 141. 2. nor, the calves of your lips, Hos. 14. 2. shall find any acceptance with me, Prov. 1. 28. Jer. 11. 11. and 14. 12. Mic. 3. 9. Zach. 7. 13.

*{ye spread forth your hands*} To wit, in prayer; described by the gesture therein ordinarily then used, with arms spread forth, and hands laid open; especially in solemn and earnest prayer, Exod. 9. 29, 33. 1 Kings 8. 22, 38. Ezra 9. 8. Job 11. 13. Psalm 88. 9. and 143. 6.

*{I will hide mine eyes from you*} I will not regard, either you, or your prayers; but I will hide *my face*, as Psalm 27. 9. and 30. 7. chap. 8. 17. (for *eyes*, are sometime put for *face* Ezek. 23. 40. compared with Jer. 4. 30. as, *face*, for *eyes*, chap. 25. 8.) Or, *myself*, as Psalm 10. 1. chap. 57. 17. from you; as one that withdraws himself, and will not be spoken with, Hos. 5. 6, 15. Or, I will turn mine eyes from you, as from some loathsome, and abominable thing, that one cannot endure the sight of, Psalm 109. 7. Prov. 15. 8. and 21. 13. and 28. 9. See the phrase, Prov. 28. 27. and the like, chap. 58. 7. Ezek. 22. 26.

*{yea, when ye make, &c.*} Though you be never so instant, and importunate, by such your instancy and importunity, hoping and expecting to speed, and prevail, Matth. 6. 7. Luke 11. 8. Yet it shall not avail you, Prov. 1. 28.

*{yea*} Heb. *also*. As Psalm 41. 9.

*{when*} Or, *though*. As Gen. 8. 21. Josh. 17. 18. Psalm 23. 4.

*{ye make many prayers*} Heb. *multiply prayers*. As *multiply soap*, Jer. 2. 22. and *multiply medicine*, Jer. 48. 11. For, use much soap, and many medicines.

*{I will not hear*} *I will not hear you*. The pronoun wanting to be supplied. As verse 3. *Israel knoweth not me*: So here, *I will not hear you*: and chap. 40. 5. *all flesh shall see it*. To *hear*, with man, is sometime, to *obey*: as verse 19. 1 Sam. 15. 22. with God, to *grant*, Psalm 4. 1. and 20. 1. But there seems here, to be some emphasis in it, more than ordinary. I will not so much as give you the hearing, much less grant your requests. See Zach. 7. 11, 13.

*{Your hands are full of blood*} The reason why God so abhorred their prayers, because their hands which they spread out in prayer, and ought therefore to have been pure, and clean, 1 Tim. 2. 8. were polluted, and that with blood, ch. 59. 3. see v. 12.

*{blood*} Heb. *bloods*. That is, *blood-guiltiness*, Psalm 51. 14. and 55. 23. ch. 26. 23. Murder, cruelty, oppression, extortion, verse 20. which are as murder, in God's repute, verse 21. chap. 3. 25. Mic. 3. 3. 1 John 3. 15. That which was the cause why their prayers sped no better, seemed they never so devout, chap. 58. 2, 3, 4. and 59. 2, 3. Job 27. 8, 9. Ezek. 8. 17, 18. See ch. 4. 4.

**V. 16.** *{Wash ye*} An exhortation taking its rise, from the reason before rendered, of the evil success of their suits; and directing them, to what was to be done by them, if they desired to speed in prayer, and to have their services accepted. So ch. 58. 6, 10.

*{Wash ye, make yourselves clean*} If the foulness of your hands be that which hinders the acceptance of your services, and the success of your suits, then must you wash and cleanse them, ere you can hope to have gracious acceptance of the one, or effectual audience for the other, Job 11. 13, 14.

*{wash ye*} Cleanse both your hands and hearts, Psal. 26. 6. and 73. 13. Jer. 4. 14. Jam. 4. 8. An allusion to the rites of washing, then in use, of men's bodies, their garments, and their sacrifices, Exod. 19. 10. Levit. 1. 9. and 8. 21. Numb. 19. 28, 29. Deut. 21. 6. and 23. 11. Heb. 9. 10. and 10. 22.

*{make ye clean*} Heb. *be cleansed*, ch. 52. 11. as verse 24. See ch. 9. 1. Wash yourselves sedulously, and diligently, over, and over; again, and again, until you be effectually, and thoroughly cleansed, Psal. 51. 2, 7.

*{put away the evil of your doings from mine eyes*} Which cause me to turn my face away, and to hide mine eyes from you, verse 15. Let me not hear, or see any more of them, if you would have me to regard, and hear you, your services, and your suits, Job 11. 14. Remove them from before my face, lest I set them before yours, Psalm 50. 21.

*{cease to do evil*} The first step to amendment, Psalm 34. 14. and 37. 27. 1 Pet. 3. 11. Surcease your cruelty, your injurious and merciless carriage towards your brethren, chap. 4. 6. Ezek. 45. 9.

**V. 17.** *{Learn to do well*} Apply yourselves unto the practice of the contrary duties, Psal. 34. 14. and 37. 37. Luke 3. 9, 14. and 19. 8, 9. Eph. 4. 22, 24, 28. Col. 3. 5, 13.

*{learn*} Be instructed, and taught: take out a new lesson: as Deut. 5. 1. Psal. 119. 71, 93. ch. 26. 9, 10. Eph. 4. 23, 24. Phil. 4. 12. Or, inure, and accustom yourselves unto it: as Jer. 13. 23. and 31. 16. Hos. 10. 11.

*{to do well*} To exercise mercy, and beneficence, ch. 58. 6, 7, 10. Dan. 4. 27.

*{seek judgment*} From the general he descends to those particulars wherein they most failed: and presses them with the duties of the second table. Because hypocrites, though professing a great deal of devotion, yet are therein wont much to falter and fail. So Psal. 50. 16, 18. Mic. 6. 7, 8. Matth. 23. 23. Jam. 1. 26, 27. and 2. 14, 26. While they vainly imagine, that their sedulity and assiduity in the one, may make amends for their defects and defaults in the other, Prov. 21. 27. Jer. 7. 9, 10. Howbeit these are the things, that God professes to prefer before sacrifice, Prov. 21. 3. ch. 61. 8. Mark 12. 23.

*{seek judgment*} Consider seriously, and sedulously, what belongs to you in your places of judicature, and do it, chap. 16. 5. So *seek peace*, and the like, Psalm 34. 14. Amos 5. 14. Zeph. 2. 2. He bends his speech to the princes, and rulers especially; because they were principally in fault; and by their example encouraged others to those evils, which they ought to have redressed in others, verse 23. Eccles. 3. 16.

*{relieve*} Heb. *righten*, as Prov. 23. 19. do them right. Set things right, and straight, between the oppressed and those that oppress them. Do as God himself does, whose vicegerents you are, Psal. 82. 1, 3. and 146. 7.

*{the oppressed*} The word properly signifies those whose hearts are so vexed with evil usage, that their spirits are made as sour as *vinegar*, or *leaven*; or as with *vinegar*, or *leaven*, Exod. 12. 39. So Psal. 73. 21. and the same intimates the term given to the *oppressor*, so called, as a *sourer* of the hearts and spirits of those, whom he so deals with, Psal. 71. 4.

*{judge*} *Judge for them*. Do them justice: as Deut. 32. 36. Psal. 7. 8. and 26. 1. or, judge the cause of *the orphan*, as verse 23.

*{the fatherless*} Heb. *the orphan*. Such as want either parents, or either parent, to protect them. Concerning whom therefore, God gives special charge, Exod. 22. 21. Deut. 10. 18. and 24. 17. and 27. 19. Psal. 82. 3. the want hereof is complained of, and reproved, v. 23.

*{plead for*} Heb. *debate, contend for*, Prov. 25. 9. chap. 3. 13. or, *upon debate, decide for*, Psal. 43. 1. and 119. 154. Mic. 7. 9. or, *plead the cause of the widow*, as before.

*{the widow*} Who wants now her husband to help her; and whom God therefore takes special care of, Exod. 22. 21. Psal. 68. 5. Jer. 7. 6. and 22. 3. *widow*, for *widows*: as before, *vision*, verse 1. and *orphan* here.

**V. 18.** *{Come now*} A gracious invitation, with offer, and promise of reconcilement, remission of fore-passed transgressions, and restitution of former blessings, and benefits, upon such reformation, as was before here required. So chap. 55. 1, 3, 6, 7. and 58. 6, 12. Ezek. 18. 21, 22.

*{let us reason together*} Let us debate the matter between ourselves, setting apart the creatures formerly called in, verse 2. Consider well, you yourselves, whether the terms I propound be not equal and reasonable, and for your own good. Thus is God content to condescend, and stoop so low to sorry wretches, as to argue with them, and to make them even as judges in their own cause, Job 9. 32. & 16. 21. chap. 5. 3, 4. Jer. 2. 5, 31. Mic. 6. 1, 2, 3.

*{though*} Heb. *if*. As Job 14. 7, 8. and 16. 6.

*{your sins be as scarlet*} That is, *as red, as scarlet*: as Exod. 4. 6. *his hand was as snow*; that is, as white as snow: as red as scarlet, that is, of the deepest dye, of the heinousest guilt: of a scarlet color that comes nearest unto blood; sins in grain, as we use to say, chap. 63. 1, 2. alluding to that of blood, v. 15.

*{scarlet*} The word is by some supposed, to signify cloth *double-dyed*, either first in the wool, and then again in the web: or, after it has passed the weaver's hand, twice dipped to make the color the deeper, and the cloth to keep color the better. But this seems not so probable; for the sentence should then fall in the latter branch: which is not so agreeable to reason. Nor is it probable, that the invention of those *double-dyes*, were anything near so ancient, as the use of this word, in matter of dye, or color, is found in Scripture; being of so late a date in comparison of Moses, that seven hundred years were over, after the building of Rome, ere it came to be in use there. See Plin. lib. 9. cap. 39. The word is indeed used sometime for *double garments*, Prov. 31. 21. and sometime for a *twined*, or *twisted thread* Gen. 38. 28, 30. or, *line*, or, *cord*, Josh. 2. 15, 18, 21. For there is little reason to imagine, that a woman of so mean condition, as was Rahab, should have in her house, a cord of *crimson*, or *scarlet*, and that *double-dyed* too, as some have rendered it, so strong, and so long, as to let the spies down, from the top of the town wall, of whose height, see Deut. 1. 28. Howbeit, the word is most commonly used, for such a deep red, as the *cochineal*, or the *scarlet grain* yields, 2 Sam. 1. 24. Cant. 4. 3. Jer. 4. 30. Seldom is it found without the latter hereafter mentioned: and it is here in the plural, as Prov. 31. 21. but in another sense there, *scarlets*, for *scarlet*, as we also sometime use to speak but in that form, never elsewhere.

*{they shall be as white as snow*} *They*, That is, your sins. But the phrase is metonymical, for to speak properly the sins themselves are not purified; but the persons, whose sins they are, when they are done away: as the garments of such are said to be *whitened*, when the spots of them are done away, Rev. 7. 14. and so Christ is said, to *purge our sins*, Heb. 1. 3. when he purges us from our sins, Heb. 9. 14. The meaning is, that the guilt of your sins shall be so utterly abolished, being washed away in the blood of the Messiah, 1 John 1. 7. Rev. 1. 5. & 7. 13, 14. that you yourselves, who were formerly so tainted, and discolored with them in your souls, as if your bodies had been from top to toe, dyed all over with some deep red shall appear, as clean, as pure, as white, as snow, in God's sight Psal. 51. 7. Cant. 4. 7. *as white as snow*, and *whiter than snow*, a proverbial form of speech, very frequent in Scripture, Psal. 68. 14. Dan. 7. 9. Lam. 4. 7. Matth. 17. 2. and 28. 3. Mar. 9. 3. Rev. 1. 14.

*{though they be red like crimson*} Or, *as crimson*: that is, *as red as crimson*, as 2 Kings 3. 22. *red as blood*: that is, *as red as blood*. Some of the rabbins take this to be a deeper color than the former; and so in reason it should be, if they be several colors. But others of them, affirm them to be one and the same: they are most commonly joined together, as importing one and the same thing, both in the description of the work of the tabernacle, and the priestly apparel: as also in the purification of the leper, and other unclean ones: save, that this is put first, that after, in the one, Exod. 25. 4. & 26. 1, 31. & 28. 5, 6. Whereas, this follows that in the other, Levit. 14. 4, 6, &c. Numb. 19. 7. being found alone and in a masculine form, twice only in this place, and Lam. 4. 5. But in both the forms of speech formerly mentioned, wherein they are conjoined, the construction is such, as argues a concurrence of both, in one and the same subject: *scarlet of crimson*, and *crimson of scarlet*, (to use the words, whereby they are commonly rendered) as *a rock of flint*, or, *a flinty rock* Deut. 8. 15. and, *a flint of rock*, or, *a rocky flint*; as Deut. 32. 15. (which in effect are all one) or, (to render it, as I suppose the genuine notion of either, to be) *the scarlet grain of crimson*, or, *of the worm*: that is, *the wormy*, or *crimson grain*, (for thereof has the *crimson* its name; from the *worm*, not from *the grain*) and *the worm of the scarlet grain*; or, *the grainy worm*: or, *crimson*. For the latter word here used signifies a *worm*, chap. 41. 14. Jon. 4. 7. and a worm ordinarily grows in that grain, wherewith the crimson is dyed; from whence also, both in Arabic, and in other tongues, it has its name. Of this worm, see Pausanias *in Phocicis*. & Plin. lib. 24. cap. 4. The former word therefore, I conceive to signify the *grain*, the latter, the *worm*: & the same color to be in both intimated: unless this latter add aught to the deepness of the dye, the *worm* being of itself, a deeper red than the *grain* is by itself alone. See Nahum 2. 3.

*{they shall be as wool*} That is, *as white, as wool*, as of *snow* before: a defect of the former epithet, to be from the particle of similitude understood, as 2 Kings 5. 27. or out of the former branch to be here supplied: as the term, *red*, in the former, out of this latter.
