*{as wool*} That is, as *pure wool*, as Dan. 7. 9. or as *white wool*, Rev. 1. 14. For, there are as well black, or brown; as white wools in those parts, as well as with us, Gen. 30. 32. as white wool undyed, another defect of the epithet: the like whereunto, see chap. 5. 2. Mal. 1. 14. and the very same, where *snow* and *wool* are joined together: and snow likened to wool, Psal. 147. 16. the very same thing that was spoken in the former branch, is (after the usual manner of this prophet) repeated; but with other terms of expression in this latter. For, as for that, which one of the Jewish writers has, that God's meaning should be, that if their sins were but as *scarlet*, they should be made as white as *snow*: but if they were, as *crimson*, (which is a deeper dye) they should be made no whiter than *wool*, that comes short of snow: It is a frivolous fancy; wronging the text, and mincing God's mercy: whose mind and intent, doubtless, was to give his people assurance of a full, and entire purging of them, from the guilt of their sins, by the blood of his Son, were they never so heinous, upon their repentance, 1 John 1. 7. Besides, that it is affirmed by those that are well skilled in such affairs, that wool, even with us, artificially dressed for worsted, is not, for whiteness, inferior to snow itself. As little credit, I suppose, is to be given to that groundless conceit, that some of our rabbinical writers have of late vented; (who yet tax all for blind buzzards, that dealt with this place before them,) to wit, that the prophet in these words, alludes to a rite used in sending out of the *scapegoat* Levit. 16. 10. between whose horns (as the Talmudists tell us) the high priest, before the dismission of him, was wont to put a piece of scarlet, cut out like a tongue; which if it of itself it turned white, (as it may be, by some juggling, the priests made the people believe sometime that it did) they then believed that their sins were remitted. But of this rite, there is no precept; of this miracle, no mention in Moses. And it is more likely, that from this place the fable was forged, than that the prophet should here have reference to any such figment.

**V. 19.** *{If ye be willing, &c.*} If you can be content to accept of the terms before propounded, v. 16, 17.

*{willing, and obedient*} Implying, that whatsoever they had hitherto suffered, was to be justly ascribed to their former willful disobedience, Psal. 81. 11, 16.

*{be willing and obedient*} Or, *will consent*, (as Prov. 1. 10.) *and obey*, or, *consent to obey*, as Ezek. 3. 7. to what is now required of you.

*{obedient*} Heb. *hear*. As 1 Sam. 12. 15. & 15. 27. See verse 15.

*{ye shall eat the good of the land*} You shall reap, receive, perceive, and enjoy, whatsoever benefit and commodity the land is able to afford you, Levit. 26. 3, 5, 10. Deut. 21. 11, 12. it shall not be devoured, as before, by your enemies, v. 7. but you yourselves shall enjoy it chap. 62. 8, 9.

*{good*} Heb. *goodness*. For good things, as Neh. 9. 36. Jer. 2. 7. the abstract for the concrete, as v. 7. chap. 64. 10. Of the goodness of the land, see Gen. 13. 10. Numb. 13. 27. & 14. 7. Deut. 8. 7, 9. Joel 2. 3.

**V. 20.** *{But*} Heb. *And*: as v. 2, 21. So Gen. 4. 2. chap. 29. 13.

*{if ye refuse*} Opposed to consenting, Neh. 9. 17. Psal. 78. 10. Prov. 1. 24.

*{and rebel*} Opposed to obeying v. 2. chap. 63. 10.

*{ye shall be devoured*} A fearful commination annexed, to enforce them to acceptance of the conditions propounded. So Lev. 26. 14, &c. Deut. 28. 15, &c.

*{devoured*} Heb. *eaten up*. So Jer. 21. 7. the sword is said to have *a mouth*; and therewith to *devour*, Jer. 46. 10, 14.

*{with the sword*} Of your enemies, chap. 3. 25. yet called also *the sword of the Lord*, Jer. 12. 12. because sent in upon them, by him, Levit. 26. 25. and coming with his commission, and by his command, Jer. 47. 6, 7. Ezek. 14. 17. See a passage parallel to this, Job 36. 11, 12. the *sword*, as comprehending by a synecdoche, all warlike weapons, chap. 21. 15. Jer. 51. 35, 37. is put frequently for hostile invasions, and all such calamities as are wont to accompany the same, Deut. 28. 22. Ezek. 14. 17, 21.

*{for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it*} God himself, as by word of mouth has spoken it, chap. 40. 5. and 58. 14. and it is therefore of most undoubted truth, and shall assuredly be effected, 1 Kings 14. 12. chap. 11. 17. & 55. 11. Jer. 44. 28, 29. Ezek. 12. 25.

*{the Lord*} Heb. *Jehovah*. He, who, as he has his being in himself, Exod. 3. 14. and gives being to all things, beside himself, Rev. 4. 11. So to his word also, as well as to his works; whether of promise, or of menace, Exod. 6. 3. See v. 2.

*{spoken it*} A defect of the pronoun, or affix, as chap. 21. 17. Hos. 8. 4.

**V. 21.** *{How is, &c.*} A new increpation of them for their general defection; as promising little hope of a sound reformation.

*{How*} Spoken in way of admiration, as wondering at so strange an alteration with them. So Jer. 2. 21.

*{is the faithful city become an harlot?*} Jerusalem, which had plighted fidelity unto God, 2 Chr. 15. 2, 15. & 33. 16. and had for some time continued faithful to him, (even when Israel fell away) as a loyal wife to her husband, 2 Chron. 13. 9, 11. Hos. 11. 12. but now carried herself disloyally, as a harlot, or common strumpet, Psal. 73. 27. & 106. 39. chap. 57. 4, 11. Jer. 2. 20. & 3. 20, 21. Ezek. 16. 15, 23. & 23. 3, &c.

*{it was full of judgment*} A place, wherein judgment and justice had been plentifully and constantly exercised, and executed under her religious kings, and righteous rulers, 2 Sam. 8. 15. 1 Kings 10. 9. 2 Chr. 19. 5, 10. Jer. 22. 5, 6.

*{full*} Of it, as a river of water at high tide, or swelled up with a land-flood, Amos 5. 28. See ch. 11. 9. For the Jewish doctor here dallies, who from the word rendered *full*, gathers, that there were 480 either *courts of judicature*, or *oratories* (for the term of *convention* used by him, may import either) in Jerusalem; because the letters of that term make up that number, as indeed they do, and one over. Which pity it is, he took not notice of, to coin us out of it some other mystery: that letter especially being a radical, which the two last are not.

*{righteousness lodged in it*} Or, *in her*. The meaning is, that matters were there so evenly carried, and uprightly decided, that *Justice* itself might seem to have taken up her abode there. See Psal. 85. 9, 11. and the contrary hereunto, Psal. 55. 9, 11. Howbeit, in regard of *murderous* persons in the opposite member mentioned, some by *justice*, understand here, *men of justice*: *just men*, as *might*, for, *men* *of might, mighty men*, chap. 3. 25. and *righteousness*, for, *the most righteous ones*, chap. 64. 6. See v. 26. For our Jewish masters here again dally with us in their descants upon the word, *lodge*: as if that term were here used in relation to the manner of their judiciary proceedings, wherein pecuniary controversies were usually decided the same day; but in cases of life and death, or capital crimes, the judgment was not dispatched the same day that the cause was heard; but unless the party appeared to be guiltless, the doom of death was deferred unto the day following, being put off till then, of purpose, in this regard, if aught meanwhile might come to light, whereby the party's innocence might appear: and *justice* therefore should be said to *lodge* there. But as one of them well observes, the word is not here in the notion of *a nightly stay*, as Jud. 19. 15, 20. Jer. 14. 8. but in a notion rather of *constant abode*; as Job 17. 2. & 41. 22. Psal. 25. 13. Jer. 4. 14. Zach. 5. 4. So 2 Pet. 3. 13. *wherein righteousness dwelleth*; the same with *lodged* here.

*{but*} Heb. *and* as v. 20, 28.

*{now murderers*} That is, men given to oppression and cruelty, v. 15. ch. 3. 11. For our Jewish masters here, either dally again, renewing their former note, of condemning and executing men without respite, or reprieval, the same day that their cause was heard; or shoot wide, referring the prophet's words to times far remote, to the murder of Zachariah under King Joash, 2 Chr. 24. 21, 22. which was long before Esay's days, and of Uriah, under Jehoiakim, Jer. 26. 23. which was again as far later than his times. Whereas the prophet speaks expressly of the time he lived in, & that more particularly, at which he delivered this prophecy; *now murderers*. It is a defective form of speech, (but quick and emphatical) to be supplied from one of the members in the foregoing sentence: as the like, verse 18. ch. 2. 6. either such now *lodge* in it, or it is *full* of such. And if it were so in Manasseh's time, 2 Kings 21. 16. it is very probable, that it was no otherwise in Achaz his days.

**V. 22.** *{Thy silver is become dross*} Some understand it, as the letter sounds, of the counterfeiting, or embasing of their coin. But it seems rather to be a figurative speech, implying, that whatsoever purity or goodness had formerly been among them, it was all now clean gone: and if any outward form of it remained, it was but as dross, which though it may sometime have a show of good metal; yet it is of no true worth, or value, Prov. 26. 23. ch. 64. 6. Jer. 6. 28, 30. Ezek. 22. 18, 19. 2 Tim. 2. 20, 21. & 3. 5.

*{dross*} Heb. *drosses*. Either the plural, bearing the same sense with the singular, Ezek. 22. 18. where both are used, as *tins*, v. 25. or the plural used by way of excess; for all dross, or all manner of dross: not of silver alone, but of other baser metals too. See Ezek. 22. 18, 19.

*{thy wine is mixed with water*} Some understand this also, of the vintners' fraud, and the like in other trades, practiced by mixing unsound stuff with the better sort of their wares, thereby to vent the one, for, or, with the other. Yea, there want not those, that refer both this and the former, to their vintners, that cheated their customers, as well with counterfeit coin mixed with base metal, as with wine mingled and marred with water, but these go too low, far beneath the prophet's purpose. The passage, doubtless, is figurative as the former; implying that nothing was retained by them, in church, or state, but it was some way or other, grossly and grievously corrupted. So Hos. 4. 18.

*{wine*} The word properly signifies *strong wine*, or *wine mere*, and unmixed, Rev. 14. 10. such as usually, and easily, is wont to overcome men, ch. 56. 12. Nah. 1. 10. the best and excellentest ordinances are thereby signified; or those that in former times, had been kept most free from corruption.

*{mixed*} Or, *spoiled with water*. Which both takes away the purity, and abates the strength and efficacy of wine. The word is nowhere else found in Scripture.

*{water*} Heb. as some think, *waters*. But of that, see *heavens*, v. 2.

**V. 23.** *{Thy princes, &c.*} See v. 10.

*{are rebellious*} Or, *revolters*. As it is well rendered, Hos. 9. 15. For these two are distinguished, Jer. 5. 23. and the verb, whereof it comes, signifies *to turn away, go aside*, or, *depart from*, Psal. 34. 14. Jer. 6. 4, 8. See v. 4, 5.

*{and companions of thieves*} Maintaining extortioners, and evildoers; not winking only at them, Levit. 20. 4. but countenancing, encouraging, bearing them out, partaking with them, Prov. 37. 24. Mic. 3. 11. & 7. 3. and doing themselves, the very same that such do, Eccles. 3. 16. chap. 5. verse 23.

*{thieves*} Put here, for all manner of wrongdoers; such as wrong others by force, filching or fraud. So Jer. 7. 9.

*{every one loveth gifts*} Heb. *a gift*, or, *bribe*. So Psal. 28. 10. taken collectively, as v. 1, 2.

*{loveth*} Desires, likes, expects, requires, and takes, Ezek. 22. 12. Hos. 4. 18. a practice forbidden, Exod. 23. 8. Deut. 10. 17. & 17. 19. and that with a curse on him that so does, Deut. 27. 25. Job 15. 34. noted, and condemned in some, 1 Sam. 8. 3. chap. 5. 23. and the contrary approved, & commended in others, Psal. 15. 9. ch. 33. 15.

*{and followeth after rewards*} He is as eager upon them, as a martial man is in the field, on the enemy, whom he has in pursuit, Judg. 4. 16. Psal. 18. 38. or, as a merchantman in his trade, on such commodities as he deems to be most advantageous, Psal. 34. 14. ch. 51. 1. Prov. 1. 21. Eph. 4. 19. and omitting no means, or occasions, of procuring them, Prov. 1. 19. & 28. 21.

*{rewards*} Doing nothing freely in their places, but all for hire, and retribution, Mic. 7. 3. And because this latter word has a notion of *retribution*, or, *requital* in it; some of the Jewish commenters expound it, of the judges complotting and combining among themselves, to give by turns, wrong judgment, one for another, as either's occasion should require. But the word seems to look another way; and has the same with the former.

*{they judge not the fatherless*} They *judge not for them*, be their cause never so just, (as verse 17.) but against them rather, Psal. 109. 31. or, they refuse to hear them, because they are not able to bribe them; as in the next clause, *the widow's cause comes not before them*, Jer. 5. 28. Zach. 7. 10.

*{fatherless*} Or, *orphan*; &, *widow*, collectively, as *gift*, before. So v. 17.

*{before them*} Heb. *to them*. as Neh. 2. 13. Jer. 6. 21.

**V. 24.** *{Therefore thus saith, &c.*} A dreadful commination, yet mixed with a promise of reformation, and restoration. v. 25, 26.

*{saith*} Heb. *the saying of the Lord*. And so chap. 3. 15. & 14. 22. and oft elsewhere.

*{the Lord*} Heb. *Adon*. The title given to God in regard of his creatures, as their sovereign Lord, and owner, Josh. 3. 11, 13.

*{the Lord, the Lord of hosts*} As chap. 3. 1. & 10. 16. the latter would be retained, as in the Hebrew *Jehovah*: to distinguish it from the former: *the Jehovah of hosts*. See v. 9. And hereby it may appear, that the word *Jehovah*, is sometime taken appellatively: as it is also, Deut. 6. 4. where it is said, *Jehovah our God, is one Jehovah*; that is, is the only true and essential God, 1 John 5. 20. *one*, for *only*: as Zach. 14. 9.

*{the mighty one of Israel*} The mighty Lord, or God, or protector of *Israel*; as of *Jacob*, Gen. 49. 24. ch. 49. 26. and 60. 16. See v. 4. He that was formerly their powerful protector, will now exercise his power in punishing of them, ch. 63. 9, 10.

*{mighty one*} And able therefore to master them, be they never so strong, or great, v. 31. Yet some suppose the word to signify rather *Chieftain*, than *Mighty*, as 1 Sam. 21. 7. Job 34. 20.

*{Ah*} An expression of grief, as Jer. 22. 18. & 34. 5. See v. 4. Thus God goes about the punishing of his people, with grief; as enforced by their sins to do that, which otherwise he has no mind unto, Lam. 3. 33. Ezek. 18. 31, 32. and 33. 11. Hos. 6. 4. and 11. 6.

*{I will ease me*} Heb. *I will be comforted*; or, *I will comfort myself*: as v. 16. I will satisfy myself, and ease my mind, by taking vengeance. See ch. 57. 5. Spoken after the manner of men, so insufferably provoked, and so much enraged, that they cannot therefore be at rest, until they be avenged; Gen. 27. 41, 42. So ch. 47. 24. Jer. 5. 9. Ezek. 5. 13. and 16. 42. Hos. 10. 10.

*{of mine adversaries*} My people, whom I account now, not as children, but as enemies, and *adversaries*: Such as by setting themselves against me, and walking crossly with me, have enforced me to carry myself, as an enemy toward them, Levit. 26. 21, 24. Deut. 32. 5, 15. verse 2. chap. 63. 10. Jer. 30. 14. Luke 19. 14, 27.

**V. 25.** *{And I will turn mine hand upon thee*} Some render it *against thee*. (See v. 1.) Understanding it, as a prosecution of the former denunciation in the full rigor of it. Mine hand, that had wont formerly to be stretched out for you, as my friends, against your foes, Psalm 89. 21, 23. & 136. 11, 12, 15. shall be now turned against you, to take vengeance upon you, and to destroy you, as my foes, Judges 2. 14, 15. But others rather, *unto thee*, (as the particle is found used, Psal. 13. 6. ch. 53. 1.) I will put mine hand again unto you, as a workman sets his hand to work, Prov. 31. 19. chap. 11. 11. (for to *return* is usually in Hebrew, *to do a thing again*, Gen. 26. 18. Eccles. 4. 7. chap. 8. 5. Dan. 9. 25.) I will once more set upon reforming of you: and the new molding of you again, as at the first, v. 26. supposing it, by what follows, to be spoken in way of mitigation, and moderation in part, at least of that dreadful and direful intermination, v. 24. as God intending by the doom therein denounced, the destruction, only of the worser sort; and the amendment of the better, Dan. 12. 10.

*{thee*} Jerusalem, v. 21.

*{and I will purely purge away thy dross*} I will, by those calamities that I shall send upon you, destroy out of you, the incorrigible wicked ones, Psal. 119. 119. Ezek. 20. 38. & 22. 19, 22. v. 31. and purify the rest, ch. 4. 4. Jer. 9. 7. Dan. 9. 35. Zach. 13. 8, 9. Mal. 3. 3.

*{purely*} Thoroughly. Heb. *according to purity*, as Psal. 18. 20, 24. (but in another sense,) or, *by purity*, as Job 22. 30. some render it, *as with soap*. And the word here used, comes near indeed to that of *soap*; both of them descending from the same stock: Yea, the very word here used, seems to be so taken, and were most fitly so rendered, Job 9. 30. where *snow water*, and it, are joined together; but the words following, carry it rather another way. For *soap*, as also *nitre* is for the scouring of men's bodies, and garments, Job 9. 30. Jer. 2. 22. not for the melting and trying of metals, here intimated: and it may rather therefore well be rendered, *as with the fire of purity*: the noun enclosed in the verb. *Purity*, for purifying matter, whether *soap*, as Job 9. 30. or *fire*, as here, (*he is as the finer's fire, and as the fuller's soap*, Mal. 3. 2.) as *fining*, for *fining pot*, or *fire*, Prov. 17. 3. & 27. 21.

*{purge away*} Heb. *melt*; or, *burn out* by melting, ch. 4. 4. Jer. 6. 29. and 9. 7. Ezek. 22. 20.

*{thy dross*} Heb. *drosses*. See verse 22. the wicked themselves, which are as the refuse of a state, Psal. 119. 119. Prov. 25. 4, 5. Jer. 6. 30. or the vices and corruptions of men's hearts and lives, Prov. 17. 3. & 27. 21. ch. 48. 10. Ezek. 36. 25, 27. or both.

*{and I will take away all thy tin*} Tin is mentioned among the baser metals, Num. 31. 22. Ezek. 22. 18. & it is said, being mixed with gold and silver, to make them harder, or shorter, and more brittle. Heb. *tins*, as *drosses*, v. 22. though in the singular number more usual, to intimate an utter riddance of such wicked ones, and wickednesses of all sorts. Some by *dross*, understand gross iniquity: by *tin*, glittering hypocrisy: or persons openly profane by the one, inwardly unsound by the other. Which may well be, for that *tin* carries an outward resemblance of silver; as copper, or brass burnished, of gold, Rev. 1. 15. Howbeit, I suppose rather with the Jewish commenters here, that by several resemblances, the same wicked ones, are here, after our prophet's usual manner, represented and intended.

**V. 26.** *{And I will restore*} Heb. *bring back*: or, *cause to return*: as 2 Sam. 15. 15. Jer. 34. 11. See v. 25.

*{thy judges*} Your rulers and governors, Judg. 2. 16. Acts 13. 20. not, by raising up the same again; but others like them, in their room, as Mal. 4. 5. with Matth. 11. 14. Luke 1. 17.

*{as at first*} Such as you had at first, Moses, Joshua, David, &c. fulfilled in Ezekiah, Josiah; and after the captivity, in Zorobabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, and others.

*{and thy counsellors*} Such as by their advice, were assistant to the rulers in chief, 1 Chr. 27. 32, 33. 2 Chron. 25. 16. and are, if prudent and faithful, a great stay to a state, Prov. 11. 14. chap. 3. 3.

*{as in the beginning*} At the first settling and constitution of you, as a state, after the coming out of Egypt, chap. 44. 2. and 46. 3. Jer. 2. 2.

*{afterward*} Heb. *after so*, or, *thus*. When God has thus purged you, and set good rulers over you. See chap. 4. 2, 3. and Ezek. 36. 33.

*{thou shalt be called*} Heb. *it shall be called to thee*; or, *of thee*: as ch. 64. 4, 12. you shall both be so, and be so accounted, as ch. 4. 3. & 61. 6. Matth. 5. 9.

*{the city of righteousness*} Or, *a city of righteousness*, Jer. 31. 23. and 50. 7. as, *a city of truth*, Zach. 8. 3. that is, a true and righteous city: as, *weights, and measures of justice*: for *just weights and measures*, Levit. 19. 36. or, *a city of just*, or *righteous ones*, of men of *righteousness*, chap. 4. 3. and 60. 21. the abstract for the concrete, as Prov. 12. 27. and 21. 26. See v. 21. chap. 41. 2. and 64. 6.

*{the faithful city*} Or, *a faithful city*. As returned to her former loyalty, v. 21. Hos. 2. 7, 16. *faithful*, as *a faithful spirit*, Prov. 11. 13. or, a *firm*, settled, well established state; as *a firm house*, 2 Sam. 7. 16. For the word is in both places the same. See chap. 2. 2.

**V. 27.** *{Zion*} Jerusalem, and the whole state of Judah. See v. 8. Here the place for the people; as ch. 40. 9. & 49. 14.

*{shall be redeemed*} Rescued, and delivered from her fore-passed calamities, by her sins formerly procured, and from her sinners, and sins, whereby they have been procured. So the word of *redeeming*, is commonly taken in Scripture, Psal. 55. 18. & 107. 2. & 130. 5. ch. 29. 22. These promises are added, for the support and comfort of the faithful, as ch. 4. 2. and 10. 24. Jer. 3. 14.

*{in judgment*} Or, *by judgment*. To wit, executed by God upon the wicked among them, and upon the enemies of his people, chap. 4. 4. and 5. 16. and 34. 2. Ezek. 20. 38.

*{and her converts*} Those that are reformed in her, from their former evil courses, ch. 10. 20, 21. & 59. 20. Or, those of her that return, to wit, from captivity, being bettered (as Manasseh sometime, 2 Chron. 33. 22, 23.) by their bonds, Ezra 6. 21. Psal. 126. 1.

*{in righteousness*} That is, in *faithfulness*, showed on God's part, by fulfilling his promises to his people, as Psal. 143. 1, 2. chap. 51. 5. and 56. 1. or, *by righteousness*, that is, by setting righteous rulers over them, and settling the due execution of justice (before wanting, v. 23.) among them, Psal. 122. 5. ch. 32. 2. and 33. 5. and 54. 14. and 60. 17.

**V. 28.** *{And*} Or, *But*. The copulative for the adversative, as v. 2. ch. 29. 23.

*{the destruction of the, &c.*} The wicked shall have no part or portion in the blessings promised. Being either cut off by God's judgments before denounced, Psal. 38. 37. or, continuing still in an accursed condition, by reason of their obstinacy in their sins, chap. 65. 20. The dross is consumed, or cast away, when the gold is once fined. So Job 31. 3. Psal. 1. 6. and 37. 20. and 73. 26. and 92. 9. and 104. 35.

*{destruction*} Heb. *breaking*. Alluding to the breaking of some earthen vessel, Psal. 2. 9. ch. 30. 14. Jer. 19. 11. So chap. 14. 25. & 15. 5. Jer. 4. 6, 20. and 6. 1.

*{transgressors*} See v. 2. men openly profane; such as have cast off all profession of piety, ch. 46. 8.

*{and sinners*} Men of lewd life; though retaining some outward show and semblance of devotion, ch. 48. 1, 2. & 58. 1, 2. Luke 7. 37, 39. 2 Tim. 3. 5. Tit. 1. 16. See v. 25.

*{shall be together*} They shall be destroyed as well the one, as the other, as v. 31. or the main body of them, at once, Psal. 35. 26. and 37. 38.

*{and they that forsake the Lord*} Verse 4. by going after strange gods, ch. 65. 11. Jer. 1. 16. & 5. 7. or by breach of his commandments, and their covenant with him, Deut. 29. 25. Jer. 11. 10.

*{shall be consumed*} By the fire of God's judgments, verse 31. ch. 26. 11. or, there shall be an utter riddance of them, Psal. 37. 20. Jer. 16. 4.

**V. 29.** *{For*} Or, *when*, As verse 30. Some understand it, as noting the time when they should so perish: others, as one reason, why they should so miscarry; to wit, because their idols were unable to help, save, or relieve them, chap. 46. 12. Jer. 2. 28. and 11. 12.

*{they shall*} Or, *ye shall, &c.* The person changed, as Job 18. 4. ch. 3. 14, 26. & 42. 20. Ezek. 31. 26. See v. 9.

*{shall be ashamed*} Of your idols, when you find them unable to relieve you, or to stand you in any stead. So ch. 30. 5. & 44. 9. See ch. 2. 20.

*{of the oaks*} Or, *groves*. Of such trees, Ezek. 31. 14. Or, as some, *of the gods*, idols, false gods, Exod. 15. 11. See the like ambiguity, chap. 57. 5. but the former here rather, for that which follows. Trees and groves set apart for idolatrous services, ch. 65. 3. Jer. 2. 20. & 3. 6. Ezek. 20. 28. forbidden, Deut. 12. 2, 3. & 16. 21.

*{oaks*} Yet some of the Jewish doctors expound it not *oaks*, but *elms*. That it was some kind of shroudy and shadowy tree, appears, Hos. 4. 13. where it is also rendered *elms*.

*{which ye have desired*} Or, *delighted in*. As chap. 2. 16. Jer. 22. 28. not so much in regard of the pleasantness of them, as for the worship of your idols, which your hearts were wholly set upon, and taken up with, chap. 57. 7, 8. & 66. 3. Jer. 17. 1, 2.

*{and the gardens*} Abused in like manner to the practice of idolatry, ch. 65. 3. & 66. 17. intimating, that in every place they had their idols and exercised their idolatry, as well in their gardens, as in the woods and groves. See ch. 2. 8. & 27. 9.

*{that ye have chosen*} Made choice of for such purposes, chap. 65. 12. and 66. 3.

**V. 30.** *{For*} Or, *when*. As Psal. 75. 2. See v. 29.

*{ye shall be as an oak*} Like one of those *oaks*, or *trees*, (which you delighted so much in, v. 29.) when you shall be stripped of all your wealth and state; as it is of all its leaves and verdure, chap. 28. 1, 2. Jer. 17. 6. & 48. 6. See the contrary in the blessed estate of the godly, illustrated by the same kind of resemblance, Psal. 1. 3. Prov. 11. 28. Jer. 17. 8.

*{whose leaf fadeth*} Heb. *fading*, or, *falling, with her leaf*, that is *shedding*, or, *having shed her leaves*, (see on chap. 10. 14.) despoiled of all its bravery, chap. 34. 4. *leaf*, for, *leaves*, as Jer. 8. 13. Ezek. 47. 12. See v. 1, 6.

*{and as a garden that hath no water*} Heb. *to which water is not*. That is, not watered, either from heaven, chap. 5. 6. Amos 4. 7. or with the hand, and help of man, Deut. 11. 10. As one of those gardens you made such choice of, verse 29. wanting water in time of drought: wherein nothing thrives, but all windles and withers away, ch. 5. 13. & 10. 17. & 17. 4. See the contrary, ch. 58. 11. He alludes to the *trees*, and *gardens*, that these idolaters had offended in: as to those *flowers* and *garlands*, that the drunkards use to wear at their drinkings, chap. 28. 1.

**V. 31.** *{And the strong*} Either the strongest of you, and all that they are able to do, as Psal. 76. 5, 6. Amos 2. 14, 16. or your strong idols, as you esteem them; and all the makers of them, as Psal. 97. 7. and 115. 18. shall perish together, when the Lord truly mighty, v. 24. shall come to deal with them. See ch. 2. 18, 21.

*{the strong*} One, for *strong ones*, as Amos 2. 18. See verse 30.

*{shall be as tow*} As easy to take fire as tow, (see verse 17.) which from the least spark that is, fires, and is suddenly therewith consumed, Judg. 15. 14. & 16. 9.

*{and the maker of it*} To wit of the idol, Hab. 2. 18. or, *and his work*, that is, all that he (to wit, the *strong man*) does, or can do. So the word is used, Psal. 104. 22. Jer. 22. 13.

*{as a spark*} To set the tow on fire. See Zach. 12. 6.

*{and they shall both burn together*} Both perish together; the one, by, and for the other, ch. 2. 18.

*{and none shall quench them*} The fire that God kindles, none but he can quench, Jer. 4. 4. & 17. 27. & 21. 12. Ezek. 20. 47, 48. Amos 5. 6.

### CHAPTER 2

**V. 1.** *{The word*} Here begins a second sermon; contained in the three ensuing chapters, concerning the restitution of the church, principally under Christ. Which he both begins with chap. 2. 2, 4. and after the denunciation of many heavy judgments inserted, to be inflicted upon the main body of the Jewish people, for their manifold gross and grievous sins, at length concludes with ch. 4. 2, 6.

*2 Ser.*

*{the word*} Or, *thing*; or, *matter*. As the word is frequently used. So 1 Sam. 14. 6. and 16. 18. Job 4. 12. *That which Esay saw*.

*{that Isaiah*} Or, *Esay*. See ch. 1. 1.

*{the son of Amoz*} See ch. 1. 1.

*{saw*} Had revealed unto him from God, and was as sure of, as if he had seen it done. See ch. 1. 1. and 5. 9. Amos 1. 1. Hab. 1. 1.

*{concerning Judah, and Jerusalem*} Both their ruin and restitution. See ch. 1. 1. Thus far the title, or inscription of this particular prophecy.

**V. 2.** *{And*} Or, *Now*. As 1 Sam. 9. 1. Ezra 1. 1. Neh. 1. 1. For the ensuing discourse has no connection, with any foregoing. But the particle is here used, as oft-times in the Hebrew, to make entrance into some new relation, without dependence upon, or reference unto any other. So Hos. 1. 2. Jon. 1. 1.

*{it shall come to pass*} Heb. *it shall be*, Chap. 4. 3. a prediction of the restoration and enlargement of the church, in the times of the gospel. See the very same, Mic. 4. 1, 2, 3. but Micah in likelihood after Esay, if we compare Mic. 4. 12. with Jer. 26. 18, 19. And the church, to be gathered out of all nations, is here described & illustrated, by its eminency, frequency of repair to it, v. 2. alacrity and fervency of people repairing to it, ver. 3. and tranquility and peaceableness of them among themselves, v. 4. Closed up with an incitement unto the Jewish people, to imitate their forwardness, v. 4.

*{in the last days*} Heb. *posterity*: or, *latter end of days*, as Jer. 23. 20. & 30. 24. The phrase commonly used to design (as the Jewish commenters themselves on this place observe) the last age of the world, the days of the Messiah, the times of the gospel, Jer. 48. 47. and 49. 39. Ezek. 38. 8. and 16. Dan. 10. 14. Hos. 3. 5. Joel 2. 28. Acts 2. 17. 1 John 2. 18. And yet a late annotator, (in this kind too oft faulty) would have this so pregnant a prophecy of the times of the New Testament, fulfilled in Ahaz his days, upon the deliverance of Jerusalem from Resin and Pekah, ch. 7. 1, 7.

*{that*} A defect of the particle, as chap. 4. 3. & 36. 1.

*{the mountain of the Lord's house*} The mountain on which the house of the Lord stands. Mount Zion, on the north wing whereof, (where Ornan's threshing floor sometime was, called also Mount Moriah, as bearing the name of the region) the temple was by Solomon built. See Gen. 22. 2. 1 Chron. 21. 18, 26, 28. 2 Chron. 3. 1. Psal. 48. 2. & 87. 1. chap. 14. 13. Zach. 8. 3. put here for the church, whereof it was a type, Psal. 2. 6. and 87. 5. chap. 40. 9. and 61. 3. and 62. 1. Though some would have it here to signify Christ, the *stone*, that being cut out of a rock, became *a great mountain*, Dan. 2. 34, 35. But the tenor of the text, and use of the type here, carries it rather the former way.

*{shall be established*} As chap. 16. 5. or *prepared*, as Hos. 6. 3. So Psalm 108. 1. or *set, placed, seated*, as Psalm 93. 2.

*{in the top of the mountains*} In a most conspicuous place, Matth. 5. 14. and, in regard of spiritual glory, advanced above all secular state, and power, Psal. 68. 15, 16. chap. 60. 1, 16. 2 Cor. 3. 9, 10, 18. Rev. 21. 2, 10, 23.

*{in*} Or, *on*. As, *on the mount*, 1 Kings 19. 11. *on a hill*, Matth. 5. 14. *on earth*, (for so it would be rendered) Matth. 6. 10.

*{top*} Heb. *head*. Num. 25. 4. chap. 42. 11.

*{and all nations*} The calling in of the Gentiles is here foretold; which out of all parts of the world should adjoin themselves to the church, Psal. 87. 5. chap. 11. 10. Jer. 3. 17. & 31. 12. Matth. 8. 11.

*{nations*} Who are now in so mean and vile repute with you, that you esteem them unworthy of any society with you, Acts 10. 14, 15, 28. and 11. 3. and 22. 21, 22. Eph. 2. 11, 12. See chap. 1. 4.

*{shall flow unto it*} Shall by whole flocks, and shoals, come into the church, and embrace the gospel, like lesser rivers, that meeting together, run all into some one common stream; or as great rivers, swelling up at the flood, or tide, come flowing with a full stream, up into the land. A metaphor intimating as well a plentiful, as a voluntary confluence: for the waters are thus wont to flow in, not forced, but of themselves, Psalm 110. 3. Matth. 11. 12. Acts 2. 41. and 4. 4. So Psalm 34. 5. Jer. 31. 12. & 51. 44. A learned writer observes the elegant consonancy and similitude of sound, in the original, between this word of *flowing*, and the term foregoing, that signifies a *mountain*; so thence called, as he deems, because *rivers* use to *flow* down from it; and it seems to *flow* with them chap. 30. 25. & 64. 1, 3. Joel 3. 18. and withal, hence gathers, as therein intimated, the alacrity of the people here spoken of, making as fast up the hill, as rivers run down from the hill. But neither does the notation of the word seem sound and solid; and the notion built on it, rather witty than weighty. But see more hereof on Jer. 3. 17.

**V. 3.** *{And many people*} Heb. *peoples*. As Psalm 100. 1. v. 4. a numerous company out of several nations, verse 2. Rev. 7. 9.

*{shall go*} Heb. *walk*. As after here, so ch. 60. 14. they shall be content to take, though long journeys to such places, where they may be partakers of God's ordinances, and join themselves unto the congregations of God's people, Psalm 84. 6, 7. Jer. 50. 4, 5. Eph. 2. 13.

*{and shall say, Come*} The zeal and forwardness of the people is here described, that should be in those times; not content, alone to flock unto God's house, and to embrace the Christian faith and profession themselves; but inciting others also: and each one another, thereunto, Psalm 122. 1. Jer. 31. 6. Zach. 8. 20, 23. John 1. 36, 37, 40, 41, 45.

*{let us go up*} Or, *repair unto*; as chap. 37. 14. and 38. 22.

*{unto the mountain of God*} That, which at Mount Sinai (called also the mountain of God, 1 Kings 19. 9.) what time the law was delivered, they might not do, Exod. 19. 12, 21, 23. Heb. 12. 20.

*{unto the house of the God of Jacob*} The *house*, the *temple*; the place of his special abode. So Gen. 28. 17, 19. 1 Sam. 10. 3. 1 Kings 8. 17, 19, 27. Psalm 42. 4. Jer. 7. 11.

*{the God of Jacob*} Whom he and his posterity worshiped, and were in covenant with, Psalm 46. 11. & 105. 10.

*{Jacob*} The son of Isaac, the brother of Esau; born (but the latter) with him, at the same birth. So called; because, by holding his brother by the *heel*, at the time of his birth, he seemed to *supplant* him, who had started out before him, and thereby gotten the privilege of birthright; whereof yet afterward he defeated him. See Gen. 25. 26, 33. and 27. 36. Hos. 12. 2. His posterity were also called by his name, Psal. 14. 7. Hos. 12. 2.

*{and he will teach us*} Or, *that he may teach us*. Intimating, either the effect, or the end of their repairing to God's house, to be taught, to learn, Deut. 31. 12. Neh. 8. 1, 8, 12. Acts 13. 44. See the like use of the particle, Josh. 24. 9. Psalm 86. 11. Mal. 1. 9.

*{he*} Christ, the teacher of his church, Matth. 23. 8, 10.

*{his ways*} The manner of his service, and such courses of life and conversation, as he approves of, and are well pleasing in his sight, Psalm 18. 21. and 25. 4. and 119. 33. 1 Thess. 4. 1.

*{and we will walk*} As in way of promise, as Mic. 4. 5. or, *that we may walk*, in notion of end, and purpose; as before. The end, as of repairing to learn; so of learning to practice. Deut. 6. 1. Matth. 7. 24. Luke 11. 28. John 13. 17. Jam. 1. 25.

*{in his paths*} As he shall direct us; *ways* and *paths*, are here the same, as Psalm 25. 4. Prov. 3. 17.

*{for, &c.*} Some take this clause, as a part of the people's speech, rendering a reason, why they repaired thither to be taught; to wit, because the true knowledge of God was there only to be had, ch. 60. 2. Zach. 8. 23. Others rather, (and so the Jewish commenters) as the words of the prophet, showing by what means the people should be induced to flock, and flow in such manner, thither; to wit, by the notice given them, through the preaching of the gospel, of what was there to be had, Psalm 66. 10. and 98. 2. ch. 61. 9. and 66. 19. Rom. 10. 18.

*{the law*} The doctrine of salvation by Christ, Psalm 19. 7. Rom. 3. 27. and 16. 25, 26. Eph. 3. 3, 5, 6. *Law*, for, *doctrine*: as ch. 1. 10.

*{shall go forth out of Zion*} Or, *from Zion*: as after, *from Jerusalem*. See ch. 1. 8, 27. *from Zion*, Psalm 50. 2. as before, *from Sinai*, Deut. 33. 2. Heb. 12. 18, 22.

*{and the word of God*} His message concerning the Messiah, now exhibited, Acts 2. 22, 36. and 3. 13, 18. and 10. 36, 43. & 13. 23, 39, 44.

*{from Jerusalem*} A type of the spiritual Jerusalem: the *mother*; and *mother-city*, of all the faithful, Gal. 4. 25, 26. Heb. 12. 22. The gospel was to be preached, first at Jerusalem, and among the Jews; and from thence, to go abroad into all parts of the world, Psalm 110. 2. Luke 24. 47. Acts 1. 8. and 13. 46, 47. See v. 2.

**V. 4.** *{And he shall judge among the nations*} The Lord Jesus, having all power of judicature given him by the Father, Matt. 11. 27. John 5. 22, 23. shall, by the powerful scepter of his word, exercise his royal authority, not among the Jews alone, but among the Gentiles abroad, and subdue their hearts unto the obedience of it, Psal. 2. 8, 9. and 45. 5. and 110. 2, 6. Matth. 28. 18. Mark 16. 15, 16. 2 Cor. 10. 4, 5. Rev. 6. 2. and 19. 21, 26.

*{and shall rebuke many people*} Heb. *peoples*: as verse 3. He shall convince them of their sins, and bring them to repentance, and faith in him; that so he may assoil them of their sins, and they may be saved by him, John 16. 8, 9. Acts 2. 37, 38. and 3. 26. and 5. 31. and 11. 18. and 15. 9. and 26. 18.

*{and they*} The people so convinced, and converted.

*{shall beat their swords into plowshares*} *Beat*: as Zach. 11. 6. Or, *break*: as ch. 30. 14. That is, *by beating*; or, *breaking*; or, *having beaten out*, or, *broken*; *they shall convert*, or, *turn, their swords into plowshares*. See the like phrase, ch. 1. 4. A description of that peace and concord, that the gospel preached does produce among those that embrace it, Psalm 46. 9. chap. 9. 6. Hos. 2. 18. Zach. 9. 10. Luke 2. 14.

*{swords into plowshares*} Which in time of peace, is wont to be done; when, of arms there is little use. As on the contrary, in times of war, such instruments of tillage, are wont to be converted into arms and ammunition, Joel 3. 10. And men are careful to furnish themselves therewith, Luke 22. 36.

*{into plowshares*} Albeit they leave warring one with another; yet not living idly, but applying themselves to other honest, and peaceable employments, Eph. 4. 28. 2 Thess. 3. 10, 12.

*{and their spears into pruning hooks*} Chap. 18. 5.

*{nation shall not lift up sword against nation*} *Nation against nation*, as Matt. 24. 7. That is *one nation against another*. This, some expound of the general peace, that was, throughout the whole Roman Empire, about the time of Christ's coming into the world, which as it is apparent, from the Roman histories: so may be gathered from the universality of the tax, or muster, mentioned in the story of the Gospel; which could not well be, but in time of a general peace, Luke 2. 1. But it seems rather to be understood of that peace, and agreement, that should be among those, one with another, persons, and peoples, who had sincerely embraced the faith of Christ. Who as he is called, *a Prince of peace*: and is said to *leave peace*, as a legacy to his, John 14. 27. So his doctrine is called, *a Gospel of peace*, Eph. 6. 15. And is such as works people to a peaceable disposition towards each other, Phil. 4. 2, 7. Col. 3. 14, 16. Jam. 3. 17. The meaning is, that these nations, which were before at enmity, should then be in amity, one with another, Luke 9. 52, 55. and 10. 33, 37. compared with John 4. 9. Acts 11. 3, 12, 18. Eph. 2. 14, 16. That which is indeed the proper and genuine fruit, and effect of the gospel, Rom. 14. 17, 18. Heb. 12. 11. Jam. 3. 18. For, as for that *war*, and *jar*, *fire*, and *sword*, that the gospel is said to bring with it, Matt. 10. 21, 22. Luke 12. 49, 53. It springs not from the nature of the doctrine itself, which enjoins the faithful to be at peace, so far as lies in their power, with all men, Rom. 12. 18. Heb. 12. 14. and much more to maintain it among themselves, Mark 9. 50. John 14. 27. Rom. 14. 19. 1 Cor. 14. 33. Eph. 4. 1, 6. Phil. 2. 1, 2. But it arises from the corrupt nature of man's heart, wholly unsubdued, as yet in the enemies of the truth, whose corruptions it crosses, which sets them therefore on work, with all eagerness to oppose it, Acts 13. 8, 10, 50. and 14. 2, 19. and 28. 22. Rom. 8. 7. 1 Thess. 3. 16. and from the relics of that corruption, even in the faithful themselves, still remaining, Rom. 7. 17, 20, 23. Whence jars arise sometime among them, by the prevalency thereof, warping from that gracious disposition, that God, and his Spirit have in part wrought them unto, Mat. 9. 34. Luke 9. 54, 55. Gal. 2. 19, 26. Jam. 3. 14, 17. and 4. 1.

*{neither shall they learn war any more*} *Learn*; or, *exercise, accustom themselves unto war*. As Jer. 13. 23. and chap. 1. 17. Warlike exercises, being much disused in times of peace. Yet, neither is this so spoken, as if all use of arms, either defensive or offensive, were to Christians utterly interdicted. (See Luke 3. 14. and 22. 36, 38. compared with Matt. 26. 52.) or, as if under the gospel no wars at all, should at any time be among those that profess the same; (which by woeful experience, we find, and feel to be otherwise.) But by these, and the like expressions, the prophet would intimate, what a strange temper of meek, and peaceable disposition, men's hearts should be wrought unto, by the ministry of the word, who had been fiercely, and furiously affected before; as if men, that had been bred soldiers, and trained up all their life long in martial, and military affairs, should now wholly give over, and, as grown out of love thereof, should abandon that course of life, and betake themselves to other more peaceable employments. See ch. 11. 6, 9. and to hold forth withal, that entire affection, and conjunction of spirit, that truehearted Christians should bear either to other. Whereof see a singular example, Acts 4. 32. *Five thousand* (at least, if not eight thousand, Acts 2. 40. and 4. 4.) *believers*, all of *one heart*, and *one mind*. As if one *soul* had dwelt in so many bodies. Lord, for your mercy, vouchsafe us the like.

**V. 5.** *{O house of Jacob*} The prophet here turns his speech to his own people: to provoke them, by the example of other peoples' forwardness to come in unto God, Deut. 32. 21. Rom. 10. 19. and 11. 13, 14. Yea, to endeavor to prevent them; and by going before them, (as they were first called upon) to show other people the way, to serve, and obey him, Jer. 50. 8.

*{house of Jacob*} You Jews of the family, and lineage of Jacob, verse 6. ch. 8. 17. Called also *the house of Israel*, chap. 5. 7. As *the house of Aaron*, Psalm 115. 10. And *the house of David*, ch. 7. 2. See verse 3.

*{Let us walk in the light of the Lord*} Let us (whatsoever others do, Josh. 24. 15. Psalm 26. 11. Hos. 4. 15.) frame our lives, and courses, according to the direction of that spiritual light, that God in his word, and by his Spirit, affords unto us; Psalm 89. 15. and 119. 105. Prov. 6. 23. ch. 8. 20. John 12. 35. 2 Cor. 4. 5, 6. Eph. 5. 8.

*{in the light*} Micah renders it, *in the name*, Mic. 4. 5. That is, the service, and worship, by God himself prescribed, Deut. 12. 5, 11, 21.

*{of the Lord*} Heb. *Jehovah*. (See ch. 1. 2, 10.) our God; as other nations do of their gods. Mic. 4. 5.

**V. 6.** *{Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people*} At these words begins the second part of this long sermon, consisting of a very sad subject, God's desertion of his people, and proceeding in wrath against them for their great and grievous sins; together with their impudence and obstinacy therein, ch. 3. 8, 9. The crimes charged upon them, may be referred to two heads: First, their impiety, in abundance of idolatry, sorcery, and confidence in the creature, chap. 2. 6, 8. for which God threatens, *First*, To abate & abase their pride, by pulling down whatsoever height, or strength, they confide in, verse 9–18. And so to distress them, that neither their idols, nor any human help should be able to relieve them, v. 19, 22. *Secondly*, To withdraw from them all those stays and shores, wherewith, either man's life is sustained, ch. 3. 1. Or, church and state supported, verse 2, 3. Whereupon should inevitably ensue, a general confusion in all estates, verse 4, 5. and ruin irrecoverable, ver. 6, 9. Where yet, by the way, is a word of comfort inserted, for the support of the faithful, verse 10, 11. The second head of crimes charged upon them, the rulers especially, is, their cruelty and oppression, verse 12, 15. Whereunto is subjoined the pride, excess, vanity, and levity of their women, discovered in their attire and carriage, verse 16. for which God threatens to strip them, and expose them to much sorrow and shame, verse 17–24. And in conclusion, to dispeople the land, verse 25, 26. and chap. 4. 1.

*{Therefore*} So indeed seems the particle, here used, not amiss rendered, Psalm 116. 10. compared with 2 Cor. 4. 13. as also Jer. 9. 20. Howbeit I conceive, it would rather be here rendered, *But*. And so it is used also, Psalm 118. 17. Neh. 6. 8, 12. Job 9. 31. and 23. 10.

*{thou hast*} The prophet here turns his speech again from the Jewish people, to God; lamenting his desertion of them, procured by their cross walking with him; and their grievous excesses in all manner of sin, ch. 50. 1. Rom. 11. 20. Of this change, and passage from person to person, See on ch. 1. 9. and hereafter, ver. 9.

*{hast forsaken*} As if he should say, What, do I call on this people, whom, for their sins, God has deservedly rejected? and little hope therefore left of prevailing with them, Jer. 6. 29, 30.

*{forsaken*} As, Judg. 6. 13. Jer. 12. 7. where the same word is used. You have forsaken them; because they have forsaken you, Jer. 15. 6. where the same word is again. See ch. 1. 4, 28.

*{thy people*} In part, or for the greater part; the main body of them; yet not all, Rom. 11. 1, 2, 25.

*{the house of Jacob*} See v. 5.

*{because they be replenished from the east*} With matters (such rites, superstitions, and idolatries, as come to them) *from the east*. Or, *they are fuller*, (of such abominations) *than the east*; they go beyond it in those vanities. See the like phrase, Psalm 18. 17. and 45. 7. and 69. 4. and the like ambiguity, Jer. 4. 15. and 49. 19. They seem, needlessly to vary here from the more received interpretations, who would have it rendered, either, *they have filled the land, with easterly matters*; because the verb has, sometime, an active notion; as Job 36. 17. Or, *they have drawn* such matters *from the east*; Because the Chaldee and Syriac versions do so oft use the word.

*{the east*} That is, the eastern parts, or people. Those of the east, the Syrians that lay east from Judah, 2 Kings 13. 17. ch. 9. 12. See 2 Chr. 28. 23.

*{and are soothsayers*} Or, *and with soothsayers*. (for the particle instrumental, is oft deficient, as Psalm 44. 2.) They are replenished, or, abound; as before. The sentence, either running on in the same continued tenor, *They are full of things from the east, and of soothsayers*; or, the verb supplied, and repeated again from the former branch. See chap. 1. 21.

*{soothsayers*} Concerning the proper signification of the word here used, there is much variety of opinion, as well amongst the Jewish doctors, as among our own writers. Some will have it to signify, such as take upon them to foretell future events, by the view of the sky, and the posture of the stars, and planets, ch. 47. 13. And they deduce it from a word that signifies, *to eye*; or *observe*, 1 Sam. 18. 9. From whom those swerve not much, who would have the term used of such, as raise their conjectures, from the various figures, and motions of the *clouds* in the sky; or from the flight of fowls, that fly in the sky towards the *clouds*, Gen. 1. 20. Deut. 4. 17. Prov. 23. 5. And they derive it from a word, that commonly signifies *a cloud*. Others, such as by magical skill delude men's sight: as drawing a cloud, or casting a mist, (as we use to say) before men's eyes; whereby things are made to appear other, than in truth they are. So it is thought, the magicians in Egypt did, Exod. 7. 11, 12. And of these, some deduce it from a word that signifies an *eye*: others, from a verb, that signifies *to cloud*, Gen. 9. 14. Others understand by it, such as give answers to those that repair to them, for advice and direction, concerning their affairs, and success of them; deriving it from a word that signifies *to answer*: but this seems over general. Others, such as observe days and times, as good, or bad; lucky, or unlucky: such as those, that cast lots before Haman, Esth. 3. 7. fetching its original from a word, which signifies, as they suppose a set time, Exod. 21. 19. but that word seems rather to bear another sense. The first, and second, are the most probable.

*{like the Philistines*} Of these, see Gen. 10. 14. chap. 14. 29. These bordering on the west of Judah, as the Syrians on the east, ch. 9. 12. were much addicted to such superstitions, 1 Sam. 6. 2. and the Jewish people, though forbidden them, Levit. 19. 26. Deut. 18. 4, 10. Yet had from these learned the practice of them; contracting much evil from bad neighbors on both sides. See 2 Kings 21. 6. 2 Chr. 33. 3. chap. 57. 3. Jer. 27. 9. Mic. 5. 12.

*{and they please themselves in the children of strangers*} They are much taken, affected with, and addicted unto the rites and fashions of outlandish people, Jer. 10. 2, 3. Zeph. 1. 8. Or, they delight in commerce, and matches with such, Ezra 9. 14. Nehem. 13. 23. Psal. 106. 35. though by God forbidden so to do, Deut. 7. 2, 3. 1 Kings 11. 1, 2. Nehem. 13. 25. Or, which I take to be the genuine sense of the place, With such *they abound*: For the word is used for plenty, and abundance; as 1 Kings 20. 10. And it fits better so, both with what went before, and with what follows, ver. 7. so it is taken, Job 20. 22. where *fullness*, and it, are both joined together. It signifies indeed, sometime *the stroke* of the hand, Job 36. 18. or the *clapping* of the hands, Job 27. 23. but that in indignation, this in derision: neither of them *in delight*. For that Jewish master seems to go out of the way here, who by the use of the word for *to suffice*, 1 Kings 20. 10. would have the text here understood, of their *contenting* themselves with the superstitious courses, and arts of heathen people, which made them set light by God's law.

*{children of strangers*} For *strangers* themselves; as Nehem. 9. 2. Psal. 18. 44, 45. and 144. 7, 11. chap. 60. 10. and 61. 5. Though some expound it of children abused contrary to nature. A vice grown too common, even among the Jewish people, 1 Kings 14. 24. and 15. 12. and 22. 46. and 2 Kings 23. 7. but this seems too coact. As they have delight in such, so to such they shall be left, and by such plagued, chap. 7. 17. and 9. 12. and 10. 5, 6.

**V. 7.** *{Their land also*} Heb. *His earth*. *His*; as having reference to the word, *people*; taken collectively, ver. 6. and so also, ver. 8. *earth*; as ch. 1. 6. and so likewise, ver. 8.

*{also*} Heb. *and*: as Jer. 1. 3. and so v. 8.

*{is full of silver, and gold*} Not that these things are simply evil, Gen. 13. 2. Job 22. 24. Hag. 2. 8. but they are taxed for their abuse of them, and about them. Their greedy, and undue gathering of them by fraud, and oppression, ch. 3. 14. Mic. 6. 10. Hab. 2. 9. their detaining of them from those, unto whom they were due, Prov. 3. 27, 28. Jer. 22. 13. Their priding themselves, and putting of vain confidence in them, ch. 28. 15. Psalm 49. 6. and 52. 7. and 62. 10. Hab. 2. 9. 1 Tim. 6. 17. Their excess by occasion of them, in attire, chap. 3. 18, 23. And in fare, and all manner of delights, ch. 5. 11, 22, 22. Amos 6. 1, 4, 6. And the converting of them to idolatrous uses, verse 8, 20. chap. 30. 20, 22. Ezek. 16. 17. Hos. 2. 8.

*{neither is there any end of their treasures*} Implying, as some think, the great abundance of their wealth; as Nahum 2. 9. and 3. 3, 9. Or as others, their insatiable greediness, as having never enough, Prov. 30. 15. Eccles. 5. 10. But the former rather, and so in the next clause.

*{their land also is full of horses*} Wherein also they much confided, ch. 31. 1. though forbidden to multiply them, Deut. 17. 16, 17.

*{neither is there any end of their chariots*} Whereof no use, without horses; another ground of vain confidence, Psalm 20. 7. because of much use in war, Exod. 14. 9. Judg. 4. 3, 13.

**V. 8.** *{Their land also is full of idols*} They are in all parts, and all places full of false gods, ch. 1. 29. and 57. 5, 8. Jer. 2. 28. and 11. 13. So that their land might justly be termed as, Babylon is, *a land of idols*, Jer. 50. 38.

*{idols*} So commonly termed in Scripture, Levit. 19. 4. Psalm 96. 5. ver. 18. Either because *no gods* in truth, howsoever men may esteem them, Jer. 2. 11. and 5. 7. and 16. 20. Or, because *nothing worth*; as a thing of nothing, Jer. 2. 11. Hab. 2. 18, 19. 1 Cor. 8. 4. So the same word is used, Job 13. 4. Jer. 14. 14. Zach. 11. 17.

*{they worship the work of their own hands}* That, which they themselves had made, instead of him that made them, ver. 20. Jer. 25. 6. and 32. 30.

*{worship*} Heb. *bow down themselves*. (As Exod. 20. 5. ver. 9.) To them, as to somewhat more excellent than themselves; which if it be an unworthy thing, for man, bearing God's image, to do in a religious way of worship, to any, even the most glorious creatures that God himself has made, Deut. 4. 19. How much more base and abominable to do so, to some sorry piece of his own making, ch. 44. 15, 17.

*{their own hands*} Heb. *his own hands*; and after, *his fingers*. Either distributively; which each one has either made himself, or, procured to be made for him; as ver. 20. Or, *his*; for *their*, collectively, as ver. 7, 8.

*{that which their own fingers hath made*} A further amplification of the same matter; as ch. 17. 8. because the fingers are in such curious artifices most employed. So the heavens are said to be *the work of God's fingers*, Psalm 8. 3. Yet it may here have some emphasis, to imply the sottishness of such, as having been so long time fingering of that matter whereof their idols were framed, had not all that while the wit to consider, what manner of stuff it was that they intended to adore, as their God, ch. 44. 18, 19.

**V. 9.** *{And*} As proceeding in the relation of this their folly. Or, *Therefore*; as Job 10. 15. and 21. 14. and 42. 8. Jer. 6. 11. as a passage to God's judgments on them, procured by such their course.

*{the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself*} Or, *shall be bowed down, shall be humbled*, That is, pulled down, and abased. All sorts, and states, concur in these idolatrous practices. Or, all sorts and states being alike guilty herein, shall, for such their carriages and courses, be abased, and laid low: so chap. 5. 15. And so the Jewish doctors also here take it, save that (therein going out of the way) they put it off from their own nation, to the people of Gog and Magog, that shall invade Jerusalem under the Messiah, Ezek. 38. and 39.

*{the mean man*} Heb. *Adam*. The name of our first parent; from the earth, whereof his body was at first framed, and unto which, after decease, it returns and is resolved into, again by God himself imposed on him, Gen. 1. 26, 27. and 2. 7. and 3. 19, 23. Eccles. 12. 7. and from him derived unto all his posterity. Job 25. 6. There are four names given to *man* in Scripture; two of honor, two of disgrace. 1. *Geber*, a man of strength, *a mighty man*, ch. 22. 17. Jer. 30. 6. 2. *Ish*, a *man of worth*, of value, and valor, an eminent man: and it is used therefore to distinguish the sex, Gen. 2. 23. and the age, Judg. 8. 20, 21. and 1 Cor. 13. 11. 3. *Adam*, a man of clay, *an earthly man*, 1 Cor. 15. 47. 4. *Enosh*, a *sick, sorrowful, corruptible mortal man*, Psalm 8. 4. and 9. 19, 20. For so signifies the word whence it is derived, 2 Sam. 12. 15. Psalm 69. 20. Jer. 30. 12. Mic. 1. 9. The name that Seth first imposed on his son, to mind him of this miserable and mortal condition, Gen. 4. 26. & 5. 6. And became afterward a common term to mankind, in general; as the name of Adam; from him to all his, Psalm 39. 5. and 144. 4. in both which places, allusion is to the name of *Adam*, and *Abel*. To these we might add a fifth; but that never found out of a plural form, *Methim*, Psalm 17. 14. and in signification, it seems to come near home to the last of the four; as properly signifying *mortal man*, as mere mortals, for it differs scarce in a letter, in a point only from the word *Methim*, that signifies, *dead*. But to return to the word here used. The word *Adam*, commonly imports *man*, in general, without distinction of place or state, and so *Adam*, and *Ish*, are all one, Prov. 3. 13, 30. But where these two are found together, as counter-distinguishing, either mankind in general; as Psalm 49. 2. and 62. 9. or some special persons, or number of people; as here the main body of the Jewish state; there is by *Adam*, understood *a mean man*, a man of low degree, alluding to his first original from *the dust*, Gen. 2. 7. and 3. 19. which, as it is the lowest, and basest of the elements: so in Scripture language, it notes lowness and baseness, Gen. 18. 27. Psalm 113. 7. ch. 47. 1. Jer. 17. 13. whence that speech, Job 30. 8. *Sons of base men more vile than earth.*

*{boweth down*} To do honor to his idol; as ver. 8. Or, *shall be brought down*, as ch. 5. 15. As they bow down to their idols, so will God bow and bring them down by his judgments, ver. 11, 17. Thus is God wont to retaliate men's sins and excesses with judgments, in some kind or other, correspondent thereunto. See ch. 1. 30. and 66. 3, 4.

*{and the great man*} Heb. *Ish*. The word *Ish*, is taken most usually, and generally for any man indifferently, Gen. 2. 23. Levit. 7. 8, 10. and 15. 3. But sometime more specially for *a married man, a husband*, Numb. 30. 8, 9. Hos. 2. 16. Or, as in this place, where opposed to, or distinguished from, *Adam*, for a man of more than ordinary state, and degree. See before, *Adam*.

*{great man*} And, *mean man*. Collectively, for men of their state and degree; as Job 7. 1. and 14. 1, 10. ver. 11.

*{humbleth himself*} Forgetting his own excellency, and eminency; either by creation, as bearing God's image; and, as God's viceroy set above the rest of the creatures, Gen. 1. 27, 28. Or, by place and degree, in the civil state, being raised and set aloft above others, as, in some sort God's vicegerent among men, Exod. 22. 28. Psalm 82. 1, 6. abases himself by advancing that, as his God, above himself, which God had set far beneath him, chap. 44. 15, 17. Jer. 2. 26, 27. Or, *shall be humbled*, abased, and laid low. God, by his just judgment, abasing, and pulling those down from their state and greatness; who by their service done to things of no worth, have formerly so abased themselves; so ver. 11, 12. The meaning is, that none, high, or low, great, or small, shall be exempted from his judgment, ch. 5. 15.

*{therefore*} Heb. *and*. Which particle is indeed sometime so used; See the beginning of the verse. But here, it may well be taken, as a copulative, in his first and native sense.

*{forgive them not*} So most interpreters, taking this clause, as spoken by way of imprecation. As if the prophet in a holy fervor of spirit, transported by the consideration of such foul enormities, and insufferable abuses, by all sorts and degrees among them, committed; should entreat God not to pardon, or to spare them any longer. See somewhat the like, Nehem. 4. 5. & 6. 14. Psalm 59. 9. & 109. 14, 15. 2 Tim. 4. 14. But the words may well rather be rendered, as a mere prediction or denunciation, (albeit, that the prophet by way of apostrophe, in the delivery of it, turns his speech unto God; as in passionate expressions, passage from person to person is not usual. See ch. 1. 2, 4, 9. & 26. 3, 7. Rev. 1. 5.) *and thou wilt not forgive them*: thereby intimating the former doom, and sentence passed on them, to be so peremptory, that God would not revoke it; and that he had been so far provoked by their sins, that he would not remit them, but the judgment for the same denounced against them, should unfailably take effect. See the like denunciations, 1 Sam. 3. 14. 2 Kings 23. 26, 27. & 24. 4, 5. chap. 22. 14. Or, that God, who had formerly borne with them, and a long time forborne them; would now, at length, without further delay, proceed most severely in judgment against them, chap. 27. 11. The particle here used, (which alone against this version can be objected) though it usually import matter of inhibition, or deprecation; yet, in sundry places, it implies no more than a bare negative; so Psalm 121. 3. Prov. 12. 28.

*{forgive*} Or, *spare*. Heb. *take away*; or, *take off*. Which is said to be done, when the present punishment is remitted, or removed, Psalm 72. 28. & 99. 8. Or the sin itself abolished, chap. 38. 17. Jer. 31. 34. Mic. 7. 18, 19. This latter, yet God questionless would, and did make good, upon the sincere repentance, and serious return of any of them, according to his gracious promise, ch. 1. 18. Unto those among them, that by sincere repentance, at any time, returned unto God, 2 Chron. 15. 4. Whom, therefore, he failed not to take special notice of, either to save them from perishing in the common calamity, with the rest; or so to sanctify their sufferings unto them, that they were disposed to their greater good; albeit the sentence, so far as concerned the outward judgment, touching the destruction of the main body of the obstinate wicked, were not reversed, 2 Kings 22. 19, 20. chap. 57. 1, 2. Jer. 21. 9. & 45. 5. Ezek. 11. 16. Rom. 8. 18, 28. 2 Cor. 4. 17. 2 Pet. 2. 5, 9.

**V. 10.** *{Enter into*} The prophet here turns again his speech from God, to the people, whom he spoke before to, ver. 5. As if he should say, Since that you cannot be persuaded to return unto God, and to shape your courses according to his will and word, for the prevention of his wrath; make what shift you can, to shelter yourselves from that storm of his indignation, that will shortly seize upon you, for this your disobedience and refusal, Jer. 5. 3, 6. and 6. 8. and 11. 12, 13.

*{enter into the rock*} This is spoken by the prophet, not as advising them so to do; not, as if any such place could afford shelter, and security against God, Psalm 139. 7, 10. Jer. 23. 25. Amos 9. 2, 3. but as foretelling, what their estate and condition, then, should be; and unto what sorry shifts they would be ready then to betake themselves, when God should come to execute judgment upon them, ver. 19, 21.

*{the rock*} The holes, and clefts of the rocks; where they might seem, in likelihood, to be most secret, and most secure, ver. 19. Psalm 104. 18. Cant. 1. 14. Rev. 6. 15. *Rock*, for, *rocks*: as ver. 9. ch. 1. 1, 3.

*{and hide thee*} Heb. *be hidden*, As ch. 1. 16. So Judg. 9. 5. 1 Sam. 10. 23. Jer. 36. 29.

*{in the dust*} In the caves of the earth, ver. 19. Josh. 10. 17. Judg. 6. 2. 1 Sam. 13. 6. Job 30. 6. *Dust*, for, *earth*; as Hab. 1. 10.

*{for fear of the Lord*} Heb. *from the face of*; or, *from before* (as chap. 21. 15.) *the dread of the Lord*; as ch. 8. 13. You shall so do, by reason of that terror that shall surprise you, at his appearance, ver. 19. See the like phrase, Jer. 7. 12. & 44. 3.

*{and for the glory of his majesty*} Heb. *from the glory*; or, *excellency, &c.* as ch. 35. 2. To be hid from his majestical appearance, in a most resplendent and magnificent manner; when he shall come in pomp and state, as a judge, to sit on the bench, Psalm 50. 1, 5. & 97. 1, 7. Dan. 7. 9, 10. Acts 25. 23. Rev. 6. 16. ver. 19, 21. See ver. 12.

**V. 11.** *{The lofty looks of man shall be humbled*} The effect of God's judgments, the pulling down of man's pride; and the laying low of all those things wherein he prided himself, ver. 9, 12, 17. ch. 5. 15. & 10. 33. Lev. 26. 19. Job 33. 17.

*{the lofty looks of man*} Heb. *the eyes of loftiness*; or, *haughtiness* (as v. 17.) *of a man*; for, *a man of lofty looks*, Psalm 101. 5. Prov. 6. 17. a sign of a haughty heart, and spirit, Prov. 16. 5, 18. & 21. 4.

*{shall be bowed down*} See v. 9.

*{and the Lord*} Heb. *Jehovah*. See ch. 1. 2, 9.

*{alone shall be exalted*} He only shall be magnified, when all man's pride and power shall be depressed, v. 17.

*{in that day*} Or, *then; at that time*; as ver. 20. ch. 26. 1. & 27. 1, 2. But withal, *day*, for, a *set*, a precisely determinate *time*. Zach. 14. 7, 8. implying, that God keeps his word to a day, Exod. 12. 41.

**V. 12.** *{For the day of the Lord*} Or, *the day for the Lord*; as, Psalm 7. & 102. & 127. in the titles. The time that he had set, as a solemn day of session, or assize; for the execution of judgment, either special, as here, and ch. 13. 6, 9. or general, Acts 17. 31. Rom. 2. 16. 1 Thess. 5. 2.

*{of hosts*} Wherewith he is attended, when he comes to judgment, as a judge with his train, Dan. 7. 10. Matth. 16. 27. & 24. 30. & 25. 31. See on ch. 1. 24. & v. 10.

*{shall be upon*} Or, *against*; as Jer. 5. 25. The day wherein he will come to sit in judgment upon them, ch. 18. 12. & 27. 1. or to proceed against them, ver. 17. ch. 3. 13, 14.

*{every one that is proud and lofty*} Such God most opposes, because they most oppose him, Prov. 6. 17. & 16. 5. Jam. 4. 6. 1 Pet. 5. 5.

*{and upon every one that is lifted up*} In state, or in heart. No man's might, or height shall support, or secure him, Jer. 51. 53. Ezek. 31. 1, 10, 18. Obad. 3, 4.

*{and he shall be brought low*} As ver. 9, 11. Matt. 23. 12. Luke 14. 11. and 18. 14.

**V. 13.** *{Upon the cedars of Lebanon*} A mountain lying on the north part of the land, Deut. 1. 7. Josh. 1. 4. So called, as some, from some store of sweet wood, or gummy trees, that there grew: For it comes near the word that signifies *frankincense*, Lev. 2. 1. ch. 43. 23. See Cant. 4. 11. Hos. 14. 7. Others rather from the *whiteness* of it, by reason of the snow, that is wont to lie constantly on the tops of high mountains, Psalm 68. 14. Hence, *the snow of Lebanon*, Jer. 18. 14. It was of special note for goodly tall cedars, 1 Kings 5. 6. Psal. 29. 5. & 104. 16. ch. 14. 8. Zach. 11. 1.

*{that are high and lifted up*} Above the other trees that grow near them, Ezek. 31. 4, 5.

*{and upon all the oaks of Bashan*} A region beyond Jordan, Josh. 17. 5. Sometime the kingdom of Og, Deut. 3. 1, 4. famous for fair, and choice oaks, Ezek. 27. 6. Zach. 11. 2. By tall *cedars*, and great *oaks*, are understood, either their stately buildings, framed out of such materials, as Jer. 22. 6, 14, 15, 23. Zach. 11. 2. Or, men proud and haughty, or powerful and mighty; high, and great in state or stature, or both, ver. 11, 12. Judg. 9. 15. Ezek. 31. 3. Amos 2. 9. See Ezek. 31. 14. For they seem overcurious, who by *cedars of Lebanon*, would have meant the king, and princes of Syria; by *oaks of Bashan*, the king, and princes of Israel.

**V. 14.** *{And upon all the high mountains; and upon all the hills, that are lifted up*} Above the plain. By high mountains and hills, likewise seems to be understood, men of strength and state; and whatsoever is in them advanced against God, Psalm 68. 15, 16. & 114. 6. ch. 40. 4. Zach. 4. 7. Yet not without some respect unto those mountains, whereof they gloried, as places of impregnable strength; and wherein they confided, as sure succors for retreat, and relief in times of difficulty and distress, Jer. 5. 17. & 21. 13. & 49. 16. Matth. 24. 16.

**V. 15.** *{And upon every high tower; and upon every fenced wall*} No fort, or strong wall, shall be able to fence, or secure any, chap. 30. 25. Jer. 51. 44, 58. Lam. 2. 2, 5, 8.

**V. 16.** *{And upon all ships of Tarshish*} The land lying, a good part of it, upon the Midland Sea, the western bound of it, Deut. 34. 2. Josh. 1. 4. Their shipping was matter, both of strength and wealth to them, by furnishing of them, both with treasure, and other rich merchandise, with matters, as well of necessary use, as of pleasure also and delight, Gen. 49. 13. Deut. 33. 19. Judg. 5. 17. 1 Kings 9. 26, 28. 2 Chron. 9. 21. Prov. 31. 14. For they are wide here, who would have Tyre here intended, ch. 23. 1. as confederate with Syria: The prophet dealing here only with his own people, ver. 5, 6.

*{ships of Tarshish*} *Tarshish*, Or, *Tharshish*, Was the name of one of the sons of Javan, Gen. 10. 4. whose posterity bearing his name, and settling, as some suppose, in some part of Spain, gave that denomination, both to the city they there built, and the region thereunto adjacent; which, by some corruption of language, afterward came to be called, *Tartessus*, the one; *Tartessia* the other. And of this place, they understand that passage, Ezek. 27. 12. Others, (and this way the most go) are opinion, that having seated in Cilicia, they gave the name of *Tarshish*, as to the whole region, in general, which they supposed to be mentioned, ch. 23. 10. so, more specially, to the chief city, and port town of that territory, called, in aftertimes, *Tarsus*; the place of Paul's birth, Acts 21. 39. and 22. 3. The former suppose, that by *ships of Tarshish*, here, as also, ch. 23. 1. Psalm 48. 7. & Ezek. 27. 25. are meant such ships, as either belonged to that port town in Spain; or that belonging to other places, were wont to trade thither: as also, that those *ships of Tarshish* mentioned, 1 Kings 10. 22. and 22. 49. 2 Chron. 9. 21. & 20. 36. were so termed, because they traded to a place in India, of the same name with that in Spain; which they imagine also, to be that which is usually called, *Ophir*. But that seems not to be so; because in the story of Jehoshaphat, it is said, that he built *ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir*, 1 Kings 22. 49. 2 Chr. 20. 36. Those therefore that go the latter way, suppose, that from the city of Tarsus, being a port town of note in the Mediterranean Sea; and its territory lying much upon that sea; the Midland Sea, was sometime called, *Tarshish*; so understand they that, Jon. 1. 3. and that the ships, either belonging to that port, or trading to and fro, in that sea, were thence called, *ships of Tarshish*. Now that sea being the greatest, that they, of those parts, were acquainted with, in regard whereof it is called, *This great sea*, as nearest also at hand, Psalm 104. 5. in way of distinction, from that other less, and more remote, *the Red Sea*, Psalm 106. 7. Hence, in process of time, it might well come to pass, that the name of *Tarshish*, was given more generally, unto any more vast *ocean*, or *main sea*. From whence also the Greek word, that signifies the *sea*, seems derived, by the interchange only of one letter, not unusual. And so *ships of Tarshish*, in general, those that were usually employed in any such great sea. Thus it is said, that *the king had at sea, a navy of Tarshish*, 1 Kings 10. 22. That is, such a fleet, as was employed in the eastern *main sea*; by which it traded to Ophir. But howsoever it be, for the original of the name, or the place from whence the term was first taken; both parties herein agree, that by *ships of Tarshish*, are meant ships of great bulk and burden; such as used to trade in the main seas, in great, wide, and deep waters, Psalm 107. 23. So termed in way of opposition to such smaller vessels, of less size and strength, as were commonly employed in the shallower waters, and more shoaly seas; such as the inland lakes; called also *seas*, ch. 9. 1. and the Red Sea, ch. 18. 1.

*{and upon all pleasant pictures*} Heb. *pictures of desire*; or, *delight*. As ch. 32. 12. *fields of desire*; or *delight*: and, *a vessel of desire*, or, *delight*, Jer. 25. 34. Hos. 13. 15. Some understand it, of such curious pictures, or other ornaments, as their ships here spoken of, were beautified, painted, or inlaid with, Ezek. 26. 5, 6, 7. Acts 28. 11. Others, of such as their chambers, were hanged, and adorned with, Ezek. 8. 12. Others, of their images, made for idolatrous purposes, such as they were forbidden to make use of, Levit. 26. 1. and commanded to destroy, Num. 33. 52. The word has affinity, with one, that signifies *imagination*, Psal. 73. 7. Prov. 18. 11. and it fitly answers a Greek word, used, Acts 17. 29. In regard whereof, some render it, *rare devices*. But the word being used for *imagery*, and pictures, we may very well here take it, for all such curious pictures, as being either for superstitious uses, or civil ornament intended, they were much taken with, and took much delight in. See ch. 1. 29.

**V. 17.** *{And the haughtiness of man shall be bowed down*} Or, *humbled, abased*; when they are stripped of all those goodly matters, implements, and ornaments, wherein they so much formerly prided themselves, chap. 39. 4, 6. Lam. 1. 7, 10. See v. 9, 11.

*{and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day*} See v. 11.

**V. 18.** *{And the idols*} Of the name, or word, see before, v. 8. their idols shall not be able to save themselves; much less those that served them, and expected safety from them. See chap. 1. 31. 2 Sam. 5. 21. ch. 46. 1, 2.

*{he shall utterly abolish*} He, to wit, the Lord, of whom, v. 17. or, *the idols shall utterly pass away*; or, *be abolished*. For the verb is of a passive sense, and signifies such a *changing*, or *passing away*, as is accompanied with dissolution, and destruction, Job 14. 14. Psal. 102. 26. Prov. 31. 8. compared with Prov. 24. 11. or more fully, (the noun being plural, and the verb singular) *the idols, each of them, shall be utterly abolished*. For, that is usually intimated, in such kind of construction. The like is found, Gen. 49. 22. Exod. 17. 20. & 31. 14. Prov. 3. 18. and 14. 1. See v. 20. ch. 3. 9, 10. & 26. 19.

*{utterly*} So the word, here in an adverbial notion, is found adjectively oft used elsewhere; as of the sacrifices, *wholly*, or, *utterly* consumed and burnt all to ashes, Levit. 6. 22, 23. Deut. 13. 16. & 33. 10. Psal. 51. 20. the rather to be observed, (as implying a general and utter abolition of their idols) because a writer of some note, denies the word here used, so to signify, and would have the text read, *they shall pass away, as the night doth at the sunrising*, Cant. 2. 17. But this the vowel points will not bear.

*{abolish*} *Abolished* they shall be, either, by God's judgment executed upon them, Exod. 12. 12. 1 Sam. 5. 3, 4. Jer. 43. 12. & 46. 25. See ch. 1. 31. or by the hands of those, that had before made, and adored them; being now either ashamed of them, when they find how unable they are to help them; v. 20. or abhorring them, and seriously repenting of their folly, in the worship of such vile and base stuff, ch. 17. 7, 8. & 27. 9. & 30. 22. Hos. 14. 8.

**V. 19.** *{And they shall go into the holes of the rocks*} The wicked idolaters, terrified with the dreadfulness of God's judgments, shall betake themselves to any place, where they might, if it were possible, be sheltered from God's wrath, or be hidden from his sight. See v. 10.

*{they shall go*} Or, *men shall go*, or, *there will then be going into the holes of the rocks*. An impersonal, or indefinite manner of speech, (like that, Numb. 19. 5. *and he*; or, *one shall burn the heifer*; that is, *the heifer shall be burnt*. And Mal. 1. 5. *and they*; or, *men shall call them*: that is, *they shall be called*,) which makes it, here, the more emphatical. As if he had said, (naming none that should so do) there will be nothing on all hands, but running into holes, and caves, to hide themselves, Hos. 10. 8. Luke 23. 10. Rev. 6. 16. & 9. 6.

*{holes*} Dark, and blind places; as the word imports, 1 Sam. 13. 6. & 24. 3, 4.

*{and into the caves*} Heb. *holes*; or, *hollow places*. For it comes from a word, that signifies *to pierce*, or, *bore*; or *thrust through*. Ezek. 28. 9. and has affinity, both, with that, which signifies *windows*, that are broken through the wall, to let in air, and light, Jer. 22. 14. and with that also, that signifies *pipes*, that are made hollow, for wind and breath to pass through, Judg. 11. 34. Such holes, or hollow places, as are as windows, or pipes, in the ground. The word is nowhere else found.

*{of the earth*} Heb. *dust*, as verse 10.

*{for fear of the Lord*} See v. 10.

*{when he ariseth*} So is God said to do, when he comes to execute judgment; who before seemed to sit still, as not regarding what men did. So Psal. 3. 7. and 76. 8, 9, 19. & 68. 1.

*{to shake terribly the earth*} Or, *land*, as ch. 1. 7. and 9. 19. and verse 7. when he comes to make a terrible earthquake in the state, Psal. 75. 3. Great commotions and concussions in a state, are compared to great earthquakes, that overturn houses, and buildings, and swallow up, sometime, whole cities, Rev. 6. 12, 14. & 8. 5. and 11. 13, 19. and 16. 18. Zach. 14. 4. So v. 21. Yea, such sometime come before, as presages of further judgments, Matth. 24. 7. Mar. 13. 8. Luke 21. 11. and so it seems, one did, as a warning piece, or peal, to that here denounced. See Amos 1. 1. Zach. 14. 5.

**V. 20.** *{In that day*} *Then*; or, *at that time*; as v. 11. chap. 3. 7.

*{a man shall cast his idols*} *Man*, for *men*; as verse 9. Idolaters shall with indignation and disdain, cast their idols, the most precious of them, not the treen, and the stone only, Ezek. 20. 31. but their silver, and golden ones, Psal. 115. 4. into the vilest and filthiest holes and corners; when they shall perceive them utterly unable to stand them in any stead. See ch. 1. 29. & 8. 21. Though some (but with less probability) understand it, of hiding them in such places for security, in regard of the richness of their materials. But the verb here used, seems to imply, not a care to keep, but a contempt, and disregard, as Ezek. 7. 19.

*{which they made each one for himself*} Heb. *which they made for him*; or, *for himself*. Which may be taken, either indefinitely, and impersonally, *which they made*; that is, *which were made for him*: as Gen. 41. 13. *he restored me to mine office; and him he hanged*: that is, *I was restored to mine office, and he was hanged*. And ch. 60. 14. *they shall call thee*; that is, *thou shalt be called*. See v. 19. or, by a transition from number to number, in Scripture not unusual; as Psal. 127. 5. & 140. 8. distributively, as our English well renders it; *each one for himself*. The rather, because the word is taken collectively in the former branch. See v. 8, 18.

*{made*} Made themselves, as ch. 44. 15, 16. or caused to be made for them by others, ch. 46. 6.

*{to the moles and to the bats*} Some join these words with the next foregoing; and so render the text, *which they made to worship moles, and bats*. As if the meaning were, that they made golden, and silver images; as the Egyptians sometime of *mice*, 1 Sam. 6. 4, 5. So of *moles*, and *bats*, thereby to worship those creatures, whom those figures did resemble. And true it is, that the idolaters, in those times, did, in their idolatrous services, make use of the pictures and images, even of the vilest and basest creatures, Ezek. 8. 10. yet, not in likelihood, to worship those very creatures, but such imaginary deities, as by those forms they intended symbolically to represent.
