*{and she*} The land or the mother city Jerusalem, Lam. 1.1.

*{being desolate*} Heb. *cleansed*: that is *emptied* of goods and people: or *destroyed*: *cut off* as the word is rendered, Zach. 5.3. But of that version there is some doubt. The word seems to have a metaphor in it, taken from the sweeping of an house, with *brooms* or *besoms* Matth. 12.44. which by this very word, are of some deemed to be so termed, Exod. 25.29. and elsewhere. But that is not so probable; for the vessels or instruments there mentioned, were of gold, and belonged to the holy table; and the use of them seems to look and lead another way. Howbeit, to the use of such implements, the prophet might well be supposed here to allude; nor is it any unusual resemblance in God's menaces. For so of Jeroboam's house, God threatens *to sweep it away, as a man sweeps away dung, until it be all gone*, 1 King. 14.10. that is the sense of the place; though the very term of *sweeping* be not there expressed. But of Babylon he says expressly, that he will *sweep it with the besom of destruction*, ch. 14.23. and of Tyrus, that he will *scrape*, or *sweep her very dust away*, Ezek. 26.4. Or, it may be a trope, taken from the *wiping*, or *cleansing of a dish*, Matth. 23.25. For in allusion hereunto, in the story of Manasses God threatens *to wipe Jerusalem, as a man wipes a dish, and whelms it*, when he has so done, 2 King. 21.13. whether of the two, the phrase here used has respect to; apparent it is, that by *cleansing* of it, is here meant, a depopulating of it; or an emptying the place of its inhabitants; who, as before they were compared to *dross* and such refuse stuff, as must be severed and consumed, ere the gold can be purified, ch. 1.25. So are they here likened, for their wickedness, to the grease or filth of a dish; or the dust and dirt that sticks fast to the pavement of an house, that cannot therefore be cleansed; the one, or the other; until the one be thoroughly wiped: and the other swept accordingly: and to such stuff, as is so wiped off, or swept away, or scoured, or scraped off, are they compared, Lam. 3.45. Yea, such they were, even in God's repute: and accordingly it is here intimated, that by him they should be so dealt with. See Jer. 6.30.

*{sitteth upon the ground*} As the manner is of mourners, Ezra 9.3. Job 2.8,13. chap. 47.1. Lam. 2.10. Ezek. 8.14. Yet withal, alluding to the site, and sight of a sacked city, that having her stately buildings, either pulled down, or burnt down, seems to lie in the dust; or to be, as a body dissolved into dust, 1 King. 20.10. Psalm 103.14. ch. 25.12. and 26.5.

### CHAPTER 4

**Verse 1.** *{And in that day*} In those times, as chapt. 3.18. This chapter belongs to the former prophecy, contained in chapt. 2. and 3. And this first verse of it, to the menaces denounced in the chapter next before-going, v. 25,26. Concerning the destruction of their men, and desolation that thereupon should ensue; further here amplified by such a paucity, and scarcity of that sex surviving, the war having consumed the most of them, (the like whereunto, see chap. 13.22.) that many women should be content, yea solicit, to come upon any terms, though never so unequal and unreasonable, under one man's wing, that he may be accounted as an husband, and head to them; and they may not be deemed to want such an one. So some take that, Jer. 31.22. but of that in its place.

*{seven women*} i.e. that is many women. As Psal. 119.164. Prov. 24.16. ch. 30.26. Jer. 15.9. A certain number, for an uncertain. So Zach. 8.23. *ten men* there; as *seven women* here.

*{shall take hold*} Contrary to the modesty, required in that sex; rather to be sued, and sought unto by the other; than themselves to seek and sue to them.

*{of one man*} Contrary unto that natural disposition, which in that society, is not willing to admit compeers; marriage, and majesty, enduring no co-partnership. And the wife superinduced, therefore, is said to be *a vexation*, and, *a vexer*, Levit. 18.18. 1 Sam. 1.6.

*{we will eat our own bread*} We will find ourselves meat, drink, and apparel. We will expect no such means of maintenance from you, as the law ties husbands to, in regard of their wives, whether they have one, or more, Exod. 21.10.

*{bread*} For all manner of food; as Gen. 28.20. ch. 3.1.

*{our own bread*} That which we will earn ourselves. See Proverbs 31.27.

*{and wear our own apparel*} Either, wrought with our own hands; or procured by our own employments, otherwise. See Proverbs 31.13,18,19,22,23.

*{only, let us be called by thy name*} Heb. *let thy name be called upon us*. That is, let us be called, and accounted yours; to wit, your wives. So Jacob, Gen. 48.16. *Let my name be called upon them*: that is, let them be called and accounted mine, to wit, my sons.

*{called*} That is, *be*; or, *be accounted*; as ch. 1.21. but alluding withal, to the usual manner of calling the wife by the husband's name, Joh. 19.25.

*{to take away our reproach*} For it was deemed a reproachful thing among that people, for a woman, as to be without issue, 1 Sam. 1.6. Luk. 1.25. (for barrenness was accounted a curse, Exod. 23.26. Deut. 7.14. and fruitfulness a blessing, Psal. 127.3. & 128.3.) so to want an husband; to live single as one, that no man regarded, or looked after, ch. 54.4. Jer. 30.17. and that therefore could not have issue, in an honest and warrantable way. Hence it is mentioned, as one dismal effect of God's judgments on this people, that *the maidens were not given in marriage*, Psal. 78.63. See the story of Jephtha's daughter, Judg. 11.36,37. This the apostle seems to have had an eye to, 1 Cor. 7.36.

**V. 2.** *{In that day*} *At that time*; or, *Then*: as chap. 2.20. or, *And then*. For the better connection of it with the rest of the context, as ch. 3.6. but here, *then*: for *after*: as ch. 3.25. And, as the particle *then*, is oft with us a note, not of the time present, but of the time ensuing. For, the prophecy, or predictions here following, were to take effect: Not what time they should be in that desolate condition: but after these calamities overpast, and the people of God by these afflictions thus purged: the incorrigible wicked being swept away, and the residue reformed, v. 4. ch. 1.26,27. For this sermon, or prophecy, the prophet concludes, as the former, with gracious promises, for the support of the faithful; and with a prediction, as most think, of the exhibition of the Messiah, and the restoration of the church under him, wherewith also he began the same, ch. 2.2.

*{the branch of the Lord*} The promised Messiah: the Lord Jesus. Whose name is said to be *Tsemach*, that is, *bud*: or, *branch*, Zach. 3.8. & 6.12. and is so called: partly, in regard of his descent: his issuing from the root of Jesse, the stem, or stock of David, budding and sprouting forth again, when it was much decayed, and in a manner, to sight, dead, ch. 11.1. and 53.2. and partly, because all life of grace, and spiritual blessings are contained in him, as leaves, blossoms, and fruits, in a *bud*, or *branch*: and from him, springing and sprouting forth, are derived unto all those, that are ingrafted into him and have interest in him, Rom. 6.5. and 11.17,24. 1 Cor. 1.30. In regard whereof, he is also further termed a *bud*, or *branch, of righteousness*; Jer. 23.5. & 33.15. The Jewish doctors themselves, expound it of the Messiah; and many of ours therein, concur with them. Yet others understand it of the church. That as their land, though wasted by former wars, ch. 1.7. & 32.13. and much more also, by occasion of the Babylonian deportation, ch. 3.26. seemed never likely to recover, and return to his former fertility and beauty again, Jer. 30.17. yet should become, both after the Assyrian incursion and devastation, as also after the return from the Chaldean captivity, as fruitful and beautiful, as ever before, chap. 32.16. & 35.1,2. Jer. 33.10,13. So the church, and people of God, called his pleasant plant, ch. 5.7. though it seemed so to be impaired, and wasted, by the foregoing calamities here denounced; and the long continuance thereof, during the Babylonian deportation, and bondage, that it was deemed as a dead corpse, or plant, never like to recover life again; much less to attain to any such flourishing estate, as before it enjoyed; yet should again spring forth, and sprout out of the dust, and be restored to as glorious a condition, as ever, chap. 26.19. & 37.31. & 44.3,4. Ezek. 21.21. & 37.11,12,19. Others again conceive, that by the *bud*, or *branch*, here mentioned, is understood the Spirit of God, and the graces of it, that should in great abundance, through God's blessing on the labors of his servants in their spiritual husbandry, 1 Cor. 3.6,9. spring forth, and manifest themselves more gloriously than ever, in the lives and courses of his people, v. 3. chap. 1.26,27. & 60.21. & 62.3,11. See the like phrase, Psal. 85.11. ch. 45.8. I conceive the second interpretation, to be most agreeable to the course of the context.

*{branch of the Lord*} Because, which way soever we take it, it is from him. It is he that caused the Messiah to spring from the withered root of Jesse, Psal. 132.11,17. Jer. 33.15. Zach. 3.8. Act. 13.23,33. It is he, that causes his church to spring up again, out of her dust, ch. 26.19. & 55.10,13. Ezek. 37.12. It is he, that causes the graces of his Spirit, to spring abundantly forth, from the hearts of those who were barren and fruitless before, chap. 44.3,4. Ezek. 36.26,27. 1 Cor. 3.7.

*{shall be beautiful, and glorious*} Heb. *For*, or, *to beauty and glory*. As, *for glory*, Zach. 3.5. and, *for a crown of glory*, chap. 28.5. or, simply, *beauty and glory*; as it is rendered, Zach. 3.5. that is, *beautiful and glorious*; the abstract for the concrete: as ch. 3.25. So, *desolation*, and, *unto desolation*, are one and the same, ch. 1.6. with Jer. 12.11. See ch. 24.16.

*{beautiful*} Or, *beauty*. The word is rendered *glory*, chap. 13.19. & 23.9. & 24.16. and elsewhere. But *glory*, and it, are here distinct. And it seems rather to signify such *loveliness*, *comeliness*, and *pleasantness* unto the eye, as makes amiable, desirable, delightful. So, *a pleasant heritage*, Jer. 3.19. and, *a pleasant land*, Dan. 11.16. For, it comes from a word that signifies *a roe*; a comely smooth-skinned creature, and delightful to behold; whereunto therefore, the spouse in the Canticles, likens her love, Cant. 2.9. and her love, his spouse's two breasts, to two *fawns*; or young ones of that kind, as most take it, Cant. 4.5. & 7.4. nor much differs it from those lovely creatures; which Solomon would have the wife like unto, in her husband's eye and esteem, Prov. 5.19. This word therefore implies such a *comeliness*, or *loveliness*, as makes amiable, and draws affection to it: the other, such a luster, as stands with state. Both joined together, very fitly express the exceeding great amiableness, mixed with no less majesticalness, that is found in the person of Christ, and in his church, and in his ordinances, and in the graces of his Spirit, Psal. 45.2,3,4. & 110.2,3. Cant. 1.9,16. & 4.1. & 5.10. & 6.4. ch. 52.7,8. & 60.1,14. & 62.4,5. Rom. 10.15. 2 Cor. 3.7,12,18. and 10.4.

*{and the fruit of the earth*} Or, *of the land*: as ch. 1.19. alluding to that fruitfulness that the land formerly had, Gen. 26.12. Deut. 8.8. and should attain to again; both, after the removal of the Assyrian army; and again, after their return from the Chaldean captivity: though it had lain so long time waste, Jer. 31.5. See ch. 30.23,24. Ezek. 36.8,11,35. where it is said, *The land that had lien waste became as the garden of Eden*. But to be withal spiritually here understood of the fruits of the Spirit, holiness, righteousness, and the like: that should spring forth, and appear in the lives and courses of God's people, proceeding from the inward principle of grace in their souls, chap. 45.8. & 61.3. Ezek. 47.12. Gal. 5.22,23. Phil. 1.11. Heb. 6.7. and 12.11. Jam. 3.17,18.

*{shall be excellent*} Heb. *excellency*. Or, *for*; or, *unto excellency*: as before. The word properly seems to signify *gayness*; for it comes from a root, which that in the Greek answers: from whence we have our English word, *gay*; And it is a title given to a chief degree among the rabbins, as you would say, *excellent*; or, *illustrious*. Hence, *the excellency of Jacob*, Psalm 47.4. yet is it frequently taken in the worst part, for *pride*, Prov. 16.18. because of *excellency*, and *gayness*, people are wont to grow proud, Ezek. 28.12,17. and in *gayness*, to express their pride, ch. 3.16. & 13.19. & 23.9. But here it is taken for *excellency*, and of the excellency of the fruit of that land, see, Numb. 13.24,27. ch. 1.19.

*{and comely*} Or, *goodly*: for *comely* is not the usual commendation of *fruit*. Heb. *comeliness*, or, *goodliness*: As in the other before. The word seems to import somewhat more than *comeliness*, and to be a degree above it: It is that, that was rendered *bravery*, chapter 3.18. See chapter 28.1,4.

*{for them that are escaped of Israel*} Heb. *for the escaping*; as ch. 10.20. those that through God's mercy and goodness, being protected and preserved, shall escape and survive the forementioned calamities. See ch. 1.27.

*{of Israel*} See ch. 1.3,4.

**V. 3.** *{And it shall come to pass, that*} Heb. *it shall be*; as ch. 2.2. with a defect of the particle; as ch. 3.24.

*{he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem*} The sanctified estate and condition of the remnant so preserved, in the state of God's church now reformed, ch. 1. ver. 25.

*{left*} Not swept or taken away by the forementioned judgments, ch. 1.9. & 3.26. See v. 2.

*{in Zion*} *Zion*, and *Jerusalem*, for God's church; as chapter 1.27.

*{shall be called holy*} Shall so *be*, and be so *reputed*, as Gen. 21.21. ch. 1.26. & 44.5. & 56.7. Heb. *holy shall be said to him*; or, *of him*: For so also is the particle used, Gen. 20.13. & 26.7. Esth. 3.2. Psal. 91.11. See the like phrase, ch. 61.6. So ch. 60.21. *Thy people shall all be righteous*; and ch. 62.12. *They shall call them the holy people*: for *holiness*, and *righteousness*, are here all one. See Act. 15.9. & 26.18. 1 Pet. 1.2. & 2.9.

*{even every one, that is written among the living in Jerusalem*} Or, *written unto life*; or, *written for life*: as 2 Sam. 15.21. Prov. 10.16,17. whom God had foreappointed to escape and survive the calamities of the times: as if he had made a list of them, and enrolled their names in some book, Dan. 12.1. a type of the elect, whose *names* are said to be *written in heaven*, Luke 16.20. and to be entered into *the book of life*: or, *of the living*, Psal. 69.28. Phil. 4.3. Rev. 3.5. & 17.8. & 20.12. kept by the *Lamb*, the Lord Jesus, the Master of the rolls in heaven, Rev. 13.8. Wherein none are recorded, but such as are designed, as well unto grace, righteousness, & holiness as to life, glory, & happiness: unto sanctification, as well as unto salvation, Ps. 69.28. Ephes. 1.4. 2 Thess. 2.13. 2 Tim. 1.9. Jam. 2.5. 1 Pet. 1.2. See also Exod. 32.32.

**V. 4.** *{When the Lord shall have &c.*} This has reference to that *Then* v. 1. When the reformation before spoken of shall be thoroughly effected, ch. 1.25,27.

*{when*} Heb. *if*. So is the conditional particle used, Job 21.6.

*{washed away*} An allusion to the legal and ceremonial washings, Levit. 15.5,8. Heb. 9.10. types of cleansing from the filth of sin, by the efficacy of Christ's blood and Spirit, Ezek. 36.26. 1 Cor. 6.11. Heb. 9.14. and 10.22. 1 Pet. 1.2. 1 Joh. 1.7. Rev. 1.5. and 7.14.

*{the filth*} Heb. *ordure*: or, *excrement*. The word imports all such filth, or excrement, as *comes forth* from the body, (for thence it is so termed: nor need we for the notation of an Hebrew word, to have recourse to an Ethiopian term, said to be used, John 11.39. for *to stink*) either upward, as chap. 28.5. 2 Pet. 2.22. or downward, as Deut. 23.14. Ezek. 4.12. but is used more generally, for any exceeding foul, or filthy thing, as of such garments, Zach. 3.3,4. and for sin, and wickedness, spiritual filth: showing how loathsome and abominable sin is in God's sight, Ezek. 24.6. Matth. 15.18,20. 2 Cor. 7.1. So is it here taken: and so Prov. 30.12. where Agur says of some, though seeming, and deeming themselves pure: that yet, *they are not washed from their filth*.

*{of the daughters of Zion*} Whose pride, vanity, wantonness, and other excesses, had no small share among the procuring causes of the judgments before menaced. See ch. 3.16. Though by *daughters of Zion*, some understand here, the cities of Judah, whereof Zion or Jerusalem, was as the mother, Jer. 34.1. But the former is more agreeable to the other passages of this particular prophecy.

*{the filth of*} Them. Thereby intimating, that those gaits, and garbs, and courses, and carriages, that they prided themselves in, and accounted their *bravery*, chap. 3.16,18. were such in deed and truth, as made them odious, loathsome, and abominable in God's eye. See the contrary, 1 Tim. 2.9,10. with 1 Pet. 3.3,4.

*{and shall have purged*} Heb. *washed out*: as 2 Chron. chap. 4. verse 6. Ezek. chap. 40. ver. 38. or *driven away*, *carried away*, *cast out*, *removed*: as the same, Jer. chap. 51. verse 58. and as the like, ch. 11. verse 12. shall have severed, and cast out, as dirt, or dung; or as dross, in regard of the metaphor following. And the prophet may seem to have made use of such a word here, as might well fit with both.

*{the blood*} Heb. *bloods*, used commonly for *murder*, Psal. 9.3. ch. 33.15. Hence, *a man of bloods*, for a *bloody*, a bloody-minded, a murderous man, Ps. 5.6. and *men of bloods*, for the like, Ps. 26.9. It is used also for the *guilt of blood*, Exod. 22.1,2. or *bloodguiltiness*, Psalm 51.14. It is put here for oppression, and all manner of cruel carriage, which is as *murder* in God's account, Mic. 3.10. Hab. 2.12. the common sin of the one sex as those before mentioned, of the other. See ch. 1.15,23. & 3.12. & 14.15. Yet, some understand it more generally of all manner of uncleanness: because blood defiles, ch. 9.5. Ezek. 16.6. Hos. 6.8.

*{of Jerusalem*} Therein spilt, 2 Kings 21.16. Ezek. 9.9. and therewith defiled, Numb. 35.33,34. Psal. 106.38. or the cruelty exercised by her inhabitants, chap. 1.15. Ezek. 22.6,9.

*{from the midst thereof*} Or, *out of it*: as Numb. 14.13. Judg. 10.16. Amos 2.3.

*{by the spirit of judgment*} By judgment executed upon the evil among them, Ezek. chap. 20.38. See chap. 1. verse 27. and by a spiritual work of judgment, in severing between the flesh and the spirit, in the souls of the faithful, Heb. chap. 4. verse 12. Or, as some, by working repentance in them, Act. 5.31. & 11.18. by which men are judged, & judge themselves, Jer. 31.18,19. 1 Cor. 11.31,32.

*{and by the spirit of burning*} So the very same word is used, chap. 40.16. and the verb whereof it comes, does most frequently so signify, Exod. 22.6. chap. 1.31. & 9.18. and elsewhere: and thereof was that place, called *Taberah*, Num. 11.1,3. because God there came to judgment with them by fire; as he speaks, Amos 7.4. and the allusion is to the trying of ore, or the casting of metal, whereby the drossy metal, is severed from the purer substance, and either consumed, or cast away. See chap. 1.25. yet some render it, *the spirit of amotion*; or, *consumption*: or, *removal*. Because the verb it comes of, signifies sometime *to depasture*; or, *eat down*: as beasts do grass, Exod. 22.5. chap. 3.14. and sometime *to remove*, or, *take away*, 1 King. 22.46. 2 King. 23.24. But the former seems more proper to this place. And it is deemed to have respect to the fire of God's zeal, c. 9.7. & 26.11. Ezek. 36.5. or to the fire of the Spirit, 1 Cor. 3.13,15.

**V. 5.** *{And the Lord will, &c.*} Here follows a promise of God's gracious presence among his people, thus purged, in all places of their abodes, as well for direction, and guidance, as for protection and defense: expressed in way of allusion to his leading them through the wilderness, in their journeying toward the land of Canaan. For unto that usually, is reference (as to one of the most remarkable, and miraculous passages of God's providence, in behalf of his people) both in the relations of their return from the Babylonian captivity, and other like deliverances in those times vouchsafed them; as also in the predictions of the restoration of the church under Christ. See chap. 40.3,4. and 41.18,19. & 42.16. & 43.2,20. & 49.9,11. & 51.9,11.

*{create*} Do strange works, like works of creation; such as are above, or beyond the power of nature, and beside the ordinary course of the creature, for the safety and welfare of his people, ch. 41.20. & 43.19. & 65.18.

*{upon every dwelling place of mount Zion*} Or, *over*: as Psal. 105.35. upon, or over every place of the habitations of his people. Protection they shall have wheresoever they abide, ch. 8.14. Ezek. 11.16. See ch. 32.18,19. & 33.20.

*{of mount Zion*} A type of the church. See ch. 2.2.

*{and upon her assemblies*} Or, *places of meeting*. The word coming from a verb, that signifies *to cry, call, or read*, is used first for *reading*, or Scripture read, Neh. 8.8. and thereof has the Turkish *Alcaron*, its name. Secondly it is used for *an assembly*, or *a meeting*; not for the hearing of the Scripture read and opened only, Deut. 31.11. Acts 13.44. but for other solemn service also, Levit. 23.7,27. so called, from the *calling* of them together, chap. 1.13. Lastly, it seems here to be put for the places of their assembling and meeting together for such purpose: as the like word is used, Psal. 74.8. Lam. 2.6. opposed hereunto, or distinguished from their private houses, or places of abode, mentioned in the former branch. So the meaning is, that God would so protect them, that they might, not only sit safely and quietly in their several places of abode, Zach. 3.10. but assemble also and meet together for the public service of God, without fear of danger or disturbance, Exod. 34.14. having God and Christ himself, above, about, and among them, to protect and secure them, both in the one place, and in the other, Ps. 46.5. Zach. 2.5. Matt. ch. 18.20.

*{a cloud, and smoke*} For, *a cloud of smoke*; or, *a smoky cloud*. A cloud like smoke, or as thick as smoke, Exod. 19.9,18. See the like, verse 6. and Prov. 22.15. compared with Prov. 28.15. So the most expound that, Matth. 3.11. *the Holy Ghost, and fire*, and, *water and the spirit*, Joh. 3.5.

*{a cloud*} Alluding to the *pillar of cloud*, or *cloudy pillar*. That both conducted and protected them in the desert, Exod. 13.21. and 14.19. & 40.38.

*{and smoke by day*} Because in the daytime fire is not so conspicuous, as *smoke*, or some thicker vapor, Josh. 18.20. Joel 2.39.

*{and the shining of a flaming fire by night*} This likewise alludes to that pillar that conducted the people. Which being one and the same, appeared as a thick cloud without light by day, partly to be the more visible in the light; sunlight, or sunshine especially that uses to dim fire: and partly to cover, shadow and shelter them from the heat of the sun, more vehement and offensive in those waste places, and sandy grounds, Psal. 105.39. chap. 32.2. and as a flame of fire in the night: both that they might see it, and their way by it, and follow its conduct, when by night they traveled, as sometime they did, Numb. 9.21. and neither miss their way, nor, miscarry in it, as they might otherwise in the dark, Joh. 11.9. 1 John 2.11. And again to make the night the less uncomfortable to them, when they made stay in those uncouth deserts. And that one and the same pillar did both those offices, and had two such several appearances with it, appears hereby: in that when it passed over the heads of that people, (at which time they were *baptized* with it, 1 Cor. 10.1,2. it dropping or mistling down upon them, to refresh them, Psal. 68.9.) and came to the rear of them, where it stayed and stood still, to keep them and the Egyptians asunder; it appeared at the same time, as a dark cloud to the Egyptians on the one side: and as a bright light to the Israelites on the other side, Exod. 14.19,20,24.

*{a flaming fire*} Heb. *fire of flame*. So Lam. 2.3. Joel 2.5.

*{for upon*} Or, *over*. As before.

*{all the glory*} All God's people: who are his glory, verse 2. whom he makes partakers of his glory: as he did Moses, Exod. 34.29,30. 2 Cor. 3.18. in whom he is and will be glorified, Psalm 29.9. ch. 61.3. Rom. 8.30. 2 Thess. 1.10. and whom by works wrought, as well for them, as in them, he makes glorious oft, even in the eye of the world, Psalm 84.11. & 85.9. & 149.4,9. chap. 60.1,2. See ch. 11.10. & 22.24. or, as I conceive the plain meaning to be, that that glory, or goodly and glorious estate, that God would advance his people to, after restoring them from their former dejected and distressed condition, should continue firm, and steadfast, under God's protection, overspreading every part of it. See chap. 32.15,19. & 33.17,21. & 35.1,2,9,10.

*{shall be a defence*} Or, *a covering*. For the word here used, comes from a root but once read, that signifies *to cover*, and by covering, *to protect*: which is the very proper notion of the word, *protect*. It is used by Moses in the blessing of Benjamin, Deut. 33.12. *The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him, he shall cover him every day*, or *all the day long*: that is, continually, and constantly. A good comment upon this place. Which may also be rendered, as our translators there supply it, *he*, (that is, the Lord) *shall be a covering*, See v. 6. It may have in respect in general, unto choice matters of value, price, and regard, which men are wont to keep close covered, as well to keep fair, as for safety otherwise. But it is supposed more specially to allude to that *cloud*, that covered the Tabernacle, a type of the church, Psalm 15.1. When it was within filled with the glory of God, Exod. chapter 40. v. 34,35. Numb. 9.22. The word is found only in two other places, Psalm 19.5. & Joel 2.16. and it is in both those places used for one and the same thing: to wit, *the bridegroom's chamber*, *closet*, or *bower*. For this was, as some tell us, such a green *booth*, or *bower*, as in the feast of Tabernacles, they made use of, Levit. 23.42. Num. 8.15,17. (though others say, *a canopy*, supported with four perches, or poles, at the four corners, under which the bridegroom and bride received their solemn blessing, Psalm 128.) wherein the bridegroom solaced himself with his bride. A place as of secrecy, security, and safety: so of solace, and delight; not unfit to represent, as well the comfort and joy; as the immunity and safeguard, that Christ, the Bridegroom, by his gracious presence affords to the church his spouse, Psalm 31.20. and 91.1. being both *Sun*, *Solace*, and *shield*, or shelter unto her, Psalm 84.11. See Cant. 2.3. But it may justly be questioned, whether the use of either of these, were so ancient, as either David's time, or Esay's. Only this we are sure, that the word here made choice of by the prophet Esay to decipher God's protection of his people, is in Scripture used for that wedding room, whatsoever it was.

**V. 6.** *{And there shall be*} Or, as some, *he shall be*. He, the Lord. Of whom, v. 5. But the verb here is feminine. Others, *of which*, protection *there shall be*. Or, most fitly, as I suppose, *which*, (to wit, *covering*, supplied from the verse before) *shall be*. For the copulative is frequently put for the relative; as ch. 5.4. Job 20.11,19. and 37.5. Jer. 6.20. Mal. 3.1. with Matth. 11.10. Or, *And it shall be*. For he proceeds to illustrate the use of the forementioned *covering* by divers other similitudes, and resemblances, as affording protection against, and freedom from all sorts of annoyances, (see Psalm 91.1,13. ch. 25.4. and 32.2.) not to speak of some other covert, divers from that before spoken of.

*{a Tabernacle*} Or, *tent*; or, *as a tabernacle*: or, *as a tent*. The note of similitude supplied: as Psalm 11.1. and 84.11. ch. 21.8. Alluding, as some think, to that *tent*, (for so it is termed) made of stuff woven out of goats' hair, wherewith the Tabernacle was covered, Exod. 26.7. or those other coverings of *rams' skins dyed red*, and of *badgers' skins*: with both which, that *tent of goats' hair* was covered, Exod. 26.14. and 36.19. to preserve both the *Tabernacle* itself, and that *tent* with it, from the annoyances of wind and weather. The word itself is sometimes used for the holy *Tabernacle* Psalm 76.2. and for the *Temple*, Lam. 2.6. which is mentioned also by that term, as a place of security and protection, (such as were *sanctuaries* with us, in times past esteemed. See ch. 8.14.) Psalm 27.5. and 31.10. It is used also for *a shed*, or *a cottage*, that a garden, or vine-dresser, and keeper, is wont to have in the garden, or vineyard, to retire to in a storm, chap. 1.8. Job 17.18. and of that *booth* which *Jonas* made him of the plant that he found growing near to Nineveh, to sit under it in the shade, Jon. 4.5. And to these latter rather, I suppose, in regard of what follows, that the prophet here alludes, if not to another *shelter*, or *covering*, called *the covering for the Sabbath*, 2 Kings 16.18. Which was built in the Temple, either, as some, for the Levites, that waited as porters at the gates of the Temple in their weekly courses, to repose themselves in; or for the people, that on the Sabbath there assembled, to betake themselves unto, when occasion was, either for shelter, or for shade.

*{for a shadow in the day time from the heat*} That which was the use of the *cloud* to the Israelites, Psalm 105.39. and of Jonas his *booth*, while it lasted him; whereof he had much joy and comfort, while he enjoyed it: but no less grief and vexation when he lost it, Jon. 4.6,8. But this, as no less useful, or much more rather, and in a better sort, than that: so more permanent, even as durable as its author and creator, verse 5. See ch. 25.4,5. & 32.2. Rev. 7.15,16. & 21.3,4.

*{for a shadow*} To shade, or to shelter, by making *a shadow*, Ezek. 31.3.

*{and for a place of refuge*} Such as the feebler sort of creatures are wont, in hazard of their lives, to betake themselves unto, Psal. 104.18. and such is the Lord said to be unto those that are his; and that such an one, as never fails, Ps. 9.9,10. and 46.1. and 61.3. and 62.8.

*{and for a covert from storm, and from rain*} Such as keepers, before, were said to set up in places where they kept, to have at hand, when occasion was, for such purpose. It is used also for such *coverts* as wild beasts are wont to to make use of, to lurk, and to shelter themselves in, Psal. 10.8,9. Lam. 3.10. and it is by God's people attributed to God, as their surest, and safest *covert*, Psalm 32.7. and 119.114. and by their enemies in derision; *let him rise up, and be your covert*, Deut. 32.39. See ch. 32.2.

*{from storm*} The word is sometime used for an *inundation* of land-waters, breaking in upon the swelling up of some stream, or flood: as Ps. 90.5. Hab. 3.10. but most frequently for a *storm* of showers, or rain, Job 24.8. Psalm 77.17. chap. 30.30. and 32.2. and so here.

*{from storm, and from rain*} That is, *from storm of rain*; or, *a rainy storm*: as, *storm, and tempest*, for a *tempestuous storm*, chap. 29.6. and, *from the wind of storm, from the tempest*; that is, *from the tempestuous storm of wind*, Psalm 55.8. So, *fire and brimstone*; for, *fire of brimstone*, or, *sulfurous fire*, Gen. 19.24. Psalm 11.4. Rev. 14.10. and 21.8. and, *a cloud and smoke*, for, a smoky cloud, verse 5.

### CHAPTER 5

**Verse 1.** *{Now will I sing*} Here begins our prophet's third sermon, composed in form of a ditty, or song. In the first part whereof, he lays down, under the parable of a vineyard, the great care and cost that God had been at with his people, and their unworthy carriage again towards him: his goodness to them, and their unthankfulness to him. That which he began also his first sermon with, chap. 1,2,3.

*{Now, &c.*} In the former part of this verse, is the title, or inscription of this discourse; or of the first part, at least, of it.

*{I will sing*} As Moses did by God's appointment. Deut. 31.19. & 32.1. So Deborah begins her song, Judg. 5.3. and David, Psalm 101. singing of *mercy and judgment*; as both Moses, and our prophet here.

*{sing*} That is both pen, and utter, as Psalm 45.1,2. & 144.9. Deut. 31.30.

*{to my wellbeloved*} There are that render it, *for my beloved*, in his behalf. As, *for Solomon*, Psal. 72. but our version may well stand, as dedicating and directing it unto the party so denominated and written to his honor. So David, *to thee, O Lord, will I sing*, Psalm 101.1.

*{to my wellbeloved*} That is, to Jesus Christ, the *wellbeloved* of God the Father, Matth. 3.17. and 17.5. Ephes. 2.6. called also *his Son of love*, Col. 1.13. Whence Solomon also, a type of Christ, is by the word here used, from God himself, termed *Jedidiah*, 2 Sam. 12.25. (which title also Moses gives to Benjamin, in blessing him, Deut. 33.12.) that is, *the beloved of the Lord*. And the church's *beloved*; so oft styled in the Canticles; Cant. 1.13,14,16. & 2.3,8,10,16,17; &c. and her *love*, Cant. 2.7. & 8.4. as she also is said to be his, Psal. 60.5. & 108.6. Jer. 11.15. & 12.7. Some therefore suppose it to be spoken in the person of God the Father, the Lord of the vineyard, speaking to Christ his Son, & Heir, concerning his vineyard, Mat. 21.33,37. Others rather, in the person of the prophet, (not, as some would have it, as of kin to Christ, supposing him to have been of the tribe and seed-royal, a thing altogether uncertain. See ch. 1.1. but) as being (therein like to John Baptist, John 3.29.) a friend and well-wisher both to Christ, and to his church; to the Bridegroom and his bride.

*{a song*} A discourse made in meter, that it may be the more easily and readily learned, the better remembered, the more frequently chanted; and being commonly in the mouths of all sorts, be transmitted from age to age, and remain unto all posterity; as we find by experience, that the Psalms which we have turned into meter, are generally more familiar, and in more frequent use with us, than any other part of Scripture. See Deut. 31.19,21.

*{of my beloved*} Either commanded of him, as Deut. 31.19. or suggested by him, as 2 Sam. 23.2. or composed in his name, and in his behalf; for it is a song of expostulation and complaint, concerning the wicked and unworthy demeanor of God's people towards him, who had been so careful of their good: not unlike those, Deut. 32. Psal. 78. & 106.

*{my beloved*} The word differs a little, but not much from the former. And as Solomon the son had his name from the former: so David his father from the latter: for it signifies one's *beloved*. Yet some render it here *uncle*, and some *cousin*: upon that groundless supposition above mentioned: that Esay should be of kin to Christ. And it is true indeed, that the word here used, does, sometime more strictly signify *an uncle*, Levit. 20.20. & 25.48. and seems sometime enlarged to any one near of kin, as Amos 6.10. See Jer. 32.7,8,12. but it is used as commonly for *a friend*, or one *beloved*; and that above thirty times in that short book of the Canticles: and they are far out therefore, that imagine it never to be so used.

*{touching his vineyard*} So the particle is taken, Gen. 20.13. & 26.7. Psal. 91.11. Yet it may here be rendered, and that is indeed the most proper and usual signification of it; *to*, or, *unto his vineyard*; as composed in his person speaking unto his vineyard: or to be sung sometime by him in in person, when time should be, to his vineyard; which they suppose done in effect, when he propounded to them, that parable concerning the vineyard, Matth. 21.33,34. Mar. 12.1,12. Luk. 20.9,16. but the former seems better. See ch. 27.2.

*{his vineyard*} His church; as it is expounded, v. 7. Howbeit, what some hence gather, that this song was framed in allusion to such merry songs as in vintage time they used in the vineyards, ch. 16.10. & 17.2. being such a mournful ditty, seems not so probable.

*{My beloved hath*} Here begins the song itself.

*{my beloved*} Christ, as before.

*{hath a vineyard*} So is the church usually styled in Scripture, as a place that men have much care of, take delight in, and expect pleasant fruit, and no small gain from, Gen. 49.22. Ps. 128.3. Cant. 2.15. & 6.12. & 8.11,12. See Ps. 80.8. chap. 27.2. Jer. 20.21. Ezek. 15.2,6. Hos. 10.1. Matth. 20.1. & 21.28,33. Luk. 13.6. and 20.9.

*{in a very fruitful hill*} Heb. *in an horn, the son of oil*; (as Psalm 104.15.) or, *fatness*, as 1 Chr. 4.40. *an horn*, that is, as most, *an hill*; and hilly places are deemed fittest for vines, Psal. 80.10. some, *an high hill*. For *horn* is used for height, Psal. 75.5. as being the most eminent part of any horned beast. Others an *horny hill*, such as bowing like an half moon, may receive the sunbeams at all times of the day, both morning, noon, and evening; and on every side, for the better ripening of the grapes: and are in some other languages said to be so termed; and, they suppose an allusion to the mountains of Israel, Jer. 17.3. & 31.5. & 33.13. and *the son of fatness*, that is, a very fat, and rich soil: The one term importing the commodiousness of the situation: The other, the richness of the soil. Yet some suppose them both to intimate one and the same thing. The *horn* being put for the excellency of any thing; as one of Job's daughters is named *Keren-happuch*, that is, *the horn of complexion*, as we term it, or, *of beauty*, Job 42.14. and *the son of fatness*, for *exceeding fat*; as *the son of the morning*, for exceeding bright and illustrious, chap. 14.13. so it would be rendered word for word, *the horn of the son of fatness*, or, *the horn, and the son of fatness*, (a defect of the copulative, as chap. 32.13.) that is, *in a principal fat*, or, *a principal and very fat* soil: alluding to the land of Canaan, wherein God had seated that people, Numb. 13.27. Deut. 8.7,9. and 11.9,12. Psal. 16.9. & 88.9. Ezek. 20.6.

**V. 2.** *{And he fenced it*} He spared for no pains nor cost about it, either for the manuring, or fencing of it, verse 4. Mark 12.1.

*{fenced it*} Made a fence, a wall, a hedge, or both about it, (see v. 5.) to keep out, as strangers, that might crop it: so wild beasts or cattle, that might spoil, or annoy it, Exod. 22.5. Cant. 2.15. an emblem of God's care for, and providence over his people, ch. 27.3. Psalm 125.2. Zach. 2.5. See Job 1.10.

*{and gathered out the stones thereof*} Heb. *he stoned it*. The word here used, signifies sometime to *cast stones* at one, 2 Sam. 16.6,13. Sometimes *to pick stones* out of a place, as ch. 62.10. and so here. As the casting of stones into a field, is said to spoil it, 1 King. 3.19. so the picking of them out is wont to amend it; because stones hinder the growth of plants, and makes the land, or ground, less fertile. A type of God's care to free his people, as well from annoyances within, as to protect them against incursions, and surprisals of enemies from without. See Zach. 2.5. & ch. 4.5,6. Some expound the fencing, of keeping them within compass by the law: the picking out of stones, of the prohibition of evil things therein forbidden: others, of the casting out of idol-worship, and idols, Deut. 7.25. and 12.2,3. And others of expelling the Canaanites, and other wicked people before them, and from among them, Exod. 23.27,30. Psa. 44.2. But these things seem over-curious.

*{and planted it*} He settled his people in the land, Psal. 44.2. & 80.8,9. where they had been but strangers before, Ps. 105.12. as a vineyard planted with strange plants, brought from some foreign soil, chap. 17.10.

*{with the choicest vine*} Heb. *Sorek*. (and so Jer. 2.21.) which is the name of a place, (whether in the Philistims' country, or in the land of Israel, uncertain) where Dalila dwelt, Judg. 16.4. from from whence some suppose, that this kind of vine had its name. Some of the rabbins therefore read the words here, *He planted it* with plants, or slips of *Sorek*. It is agreed upon, that it signifies a very choice kind of vine; whose grapes, say some of them, had no grains or stones in them. But that is scarce probable. See Gen. 49.11. ch. 16.8. and 19.9. Of the color of this vine were some horses, mentioned, Zach. 1.8. as some in Greek called, *Spadices*, of the like. Some suppose it to intimate the Jewish people, as a choice seed, descended from the loins of those their worthy ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and by God therefore set apart for his peculiar, Deut. 7.6, 8. & 9.27,29. Others, of God's precepts that he had planted his church with, Deut. 4.8. ch. 42.21. Rom. 3.1,2. But we may not descend unto such niceties, and particularities, in the exposition of a parable. And these branches thus expounded, fall one into another. See more hereof, on Jer. 2.21.

*{and built a tower in the midst of it*} So Mark 12.1. A place for the keepers of it, to retire to, and lodge in, so situated in it, that they might overlook the ground, ch. 1.8. *in the midst of it*. Either simply, *in it*, as ch. 7.22. or, *in the midst*; as a place most convenient for oversight. Of Jerusalem some expound it, wherein, as in a watchtower, the priests and princes resided. See Jer. 6.27.

*{and also made a wine-press therein*} Heb. *hewed out*. Of wood, or stone, Prov. 9.1. ch. 10.15. and 22.26. Mark 12.1. It is said, he *digged out*. But that seems spoken, not of the press, but of a place to set a vessel in, to receive the wine from the press. This some expound of the altar, streaming with the blood of beasts offered in sacrifices, (See ch. 1.11. & 29.1,2.) like the liquor of grapes, Gen. 49.11,12. Deut. 32.14. Others, of the priests and prophets, who, by their preaching, pressed out of God's people good works, and pious offices, as pleasant liquor, very grateful to God, Heb. 13.16,21. Judg. 5.13. But of that, as of the rest.

*{and he looked*} Heb. *expected*. After so much care had of it, and means used about it, he expected, and waited until time of year, then making account to receive fruit answerable to the cost and pains that he had been at with it, Matt. 21.34. 1 Cor. 9.7. Heb. 6.7. Jam. 5.7.

*{that it should bring forth*} Heb. *make*; as Gen. 1.11,12. Matt. 3.8,10. & 7.17,19. So in the next clause, and v. 10.

*{grapes*} Grapes, of some kind or other, it could not but produce, unless it were wholly barren. But the meaning is, such grapes as those plants, or slips wherewith he had planted it, used to bear. By *grapes* therefore, here, we are to understand good *grapes*, or choice *grapes*; as, *garments*, for clean *garments*, or goodly *garments* Zach. 3.5. A defect of the epithet, not unusual, So c. 1.18. *wool*, for white *wool*, c. 28.8. *no place*, for *no clean place*, Mal. 1.14. *a male*, for a sound *male* opposed to a *corrupt* one: as here *grapes*, opposed to filthy, bad, *noisome*, *naughty*, stinking ones.

*{and it brought forth wild grapes*} Most interpreters; (some Greeks only excepted, that render it *thorns*) the Latin especially run in a track, expounding the word, *wild-vines*; so called in Latin, because they use to grow in the hedges, or edges of grounds. And to mend the matter, (because that is the name, not of the fruit of such, but of the plant itself; and the translation therefore seems not to sound well;) They tell us, that the plant is put for the fruit. But we need not involve ourselves in any such difficulties; the sense of the word being plain enough of itself: The verb whereof it comes, signifies, first *to rot*, ch. 50.2. then *to stink*, Exod. 7. v. 18. & 8.14. & 16.20. Because rotten things use to stink, and because things rotten and stinking, are naught. In the third place, it signifies to be *evil*, and *naught*; Dan. 6. v. 14. and hence the word in the feminine singular, Ezr. ch. 4.12. a *bad*, *evil*, or *naughty* city; and the same here in the masculine plural, to answer unto and agree with the word *grapes*, *rotten*, *filthy*, *noisome*, or *naughty*, to wit, *grapes*: like those *naughty figs*, Jer. 24.2,3. or rather like those *grapes of gall, and bitter clusters: yielding wine like the poison of dragons, and venom of asps*, Deut. 32.32,33. The word *grapes* is not in the text, but may well be supplied from the former branch: though there be no necessity so to do: since it may be rendered *naughty*, or *noisome* ones. So the very like word is used, Job 31.40. for *noisome* or *naughty*, to wit, herbs: that is, *weeds*: such as grow among corn: of which, Matth. 13.25. where the word used, would rather be rendered *weeds*, than *tares*. Nor can I assent to those, who make that here spoken of, a figure of hypocrisy, carrying a fair show of piety, as these do of good grapes, without inward power, 2 Tim. 3.5. Since that the vices, and crimes hereby said to be resembled, ver. 7. as those also that Moses speaks of, and our prophet elsewhere taxes, in foregoing parallel places, are such as too openly publish, and make profession of impiety and cruelty. See ch. 1.21. and 3.9,15. The defect, as of the adjunct before, in *grapes*, for *good* grapes; so of the subject here in *bad*, for *bad grapes*; is neither infrequent in other languages. For so in the Greek, Matth. 23.15. we read *sea, and dry*, (agreeable to that, Gen. 1.10.) by a defect of the subject; which, in our English, we render, *sea, and land*; by a defect of the adjunct; nor unusual in the Hebrew: for so, Psalm 38.7. *loathsome*, for *a loathsome* disease; (for disease is not in the text:) so, *untempered*, for, *untempered*, or, *ill-tempered mortar*, Ezek. 13.10,11,14,15. & 22.28. See further, ch. 17.5.

**V. 3.** *{And now*} Having showed how his vineyard had frustrated his expectation, he first requires the judgment of others, even of those themselves whom it concerned, and were parties in it, what they deemed it deserved to have done unto it, v. 3,4. and then relates in what manner he purposed to deal with it, v. 5,6.

*{O ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah*} That the equity of his proceedings may the more evidently appear; he is content to make them judges in their own cause: *judge* (says he) *I pray you, between me, and my vineyard*: as if he should say, Tell me what yourselves would in the like case do, so served as I have been with my vineyard. So chap. 1.18. 2 Sam. 12.2,6. Jer. 2.5. Mic. 6.3,7. Matth. 21.40.

*{inhabitants, and men*} Heb. *inhabitant and man*. Taken collectively, as ch. 20.6. & 3.2. ver. 7. or distributively, as if he had said, Let any one of you pass sentence between me and it; as daring, and being content to put his cause to any reasonable man's decision.

*{of Jerusalem, and of Judah*} See ch. 1.1.

**V. 4.** *{What could, &c.*} Implying, that nothing as wanting on his part, could be pleaded; in regard whereof he should come short of what he expected.

*{what could have been done*} Heb. *what was there to do*? What was more to be done? as 2 King. 4.13.16. Esth. 6.6.

*{to my vineyard*} Or, *for my vineyard*; as Psal. 72. *for Solomon*: and *for his land*, Joel 2.18.

*{that I have not done*} Heb. *and I have not done*. The copulative for the relative; as ch. 3.6.

*{in it*} Or, *for it*; or, *to it*, or, *about it*; that might any way further the fructifying of it.

*{wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?*} Heb. *wherefore did I expect, &c. and it brought forth, &c.* Why has it failed mine expectation? See somewhat the like syntax, Rom. 6.7. *grapes*, and, *wild grapes*. See ver. 2. It did not so much prove barren, and yielded no fruit, which yet were sufficient to justify mine intended proceedings with it, Mat. 24.19,20. Luk. 13.6,7. Joh. 15.2. But it brought forth filthy, naughty, noisome fruit, Heb. 6.8.

**V. 5.** *{And now, go to, I will tell you*} He proceeds to relate his purpose, having formerly propounded the ground of it, and left the equity of it to be deemed by themselves; so Mat. 21.40,41. Mar. 12.9. Luk. 20.15,16. And the prophet here passes from person to person; speaking now in God's person, as before in his own. See ch. 1.9.

*{what I will do*} Heb. *what I am doing*; That is, am about to do; will do speedily, without further delay; as ch. 3.1. and 43.19.

*{to my vineyard*} Or; *with it*; as Ps. 147.20. Jer. 2.18.

*{I will take away the hedge thereof*} I will take no more charge of it, nor care for it; but expose it to spoil, and let it run to ruin. I will withdraw my protection and providence from my people, and suffer mine enemies to break in upon their land, Psal. 8.12,13. and 106.29.

*{I will take away*} Heb. *I will taking away, take away*. That is, I will utterly, or certainly, take away; as Gen. 2.17. But in this place a defect of the verb finite: as Eccles. 9.11. See ch. 59.13.

*{the hedge*} The word properly signifies a fence of thorns, or the like, Prov. 15.19. Hos. 2.6. Mic. 7.4.

*{and it shall be eaten up*} By beasts breaking in upon it, Psalm 80.13. That is, wasted and destroyed, by hostile invasion, See ch. 1.7. and 3.13. Heb. *it shall be for eating up*. Or, *that it may be for eating up*: Josh. 24.9. Mal. 1.9. as being good for nothing else, Matthew 5.13.

*{and I will break down*} Heb. *breaking I will break down*; as before. A defect of the copulative, as ch. 3.24.

*{the wall thereof*} *Her stone-fence*. As it is fully expressed, Pro. 24.32. nor seems it otherwise taken, Eccles. 10.8,9. Lam. 3.9. Hos. 2.6. So this and the former are commonly distinguished; as also the Jewish doctors here observe: though some of ours would have them both one. See Psalm 80.12. & 89.40,41.

*{and it shall be trodden down*} Heb. *and it shall be for treading down*; as ch. 28.18. Mic. 7.10. Or, *that it may be for treading down*: as before. That it may be for cattle to tread down, and depasture at pleasure, ch. 7.25.

**V. 6.** *{And I will lay it waste*} Heb. *wasteness*. That is, utterly, or extremely waste: as ch. 7.19. *the valleys of wasteness*. In which two places only, is the word found. See ch. 1.7.

*{it shall not be pruned*} To take off its superfluous branches, that spend its sap, and hinder the fructifying of it, Lev. 25.3. Joh. 15.2.

*{nor digged*} As Luk. 13.8. So the Greek, and old Latin here; though otherwise, elsewhere. Or, *hoed*; as the later Latin versions import, both here, & ch. 7.25. Or, *dressed*; having reference to the ground, as the former to the plants: (for the word signifies properly, *to keep in order*, 1 Chr. 12.33,38.) to rid it of weeds and briars, and to loosen the earth about the roots of the plants. The spade, or hoe, being for vineyards, chap. 7.25. as the plow for cornfields, Jer. 4. ver. 4.

*{but there shall come up briers, and thorns*} It shall be overgrown with such noxious plants, bushes, and shrubs, for want of husbandry, which by those means might have been prevented, Prov. 24.3,30. ch. 7.23,24. & 32.13.

*{but*} Heb. *and*; ch. 1.3.

*{briers and thorns*} Joined frequently together, ch. 7.23,24,25. & 9.17. & 10.17. & 27.4. Heb. *briar*, and *thorn*: as *weed*, for *weeds*, Job 31.40. The former word seems to signify such a kind of thorny plant, as for stiffness, and stubbornness, or hardness, is compared to an *adamant*, as most expound it, Zach. 7.12. for the sharpness of its prickles to the *point* of an *adamant*, Jer. 17.1. For, the same word is for an adamant, or diamond, (for all is one) supposed to be used in both these places: but thereof see on Jer. 17.1. The latter, is usually in the Latin, rendered by a word that answers our *bush*.

*{I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it*} Heb. *and I will charge the clouds from raining rain upon it.*

*{and*} For *also*: as Jer. 1.13.

*{command*} Or, *charge*. For the word is used, as well for prohibition, as for precept. So Deut. 2.37. where the same word is found.

*{that they rain no rain*} Heb. *from raining rain*. As *from seeing*, Psal. 69.23. *From redeeming*, chap. 50.2. *From saving*, *from hearing*, ch. 59.1,2.

*{rain rain*} As *fear fear*, ch. 8.12. *sleep sleep*, Ps. 76.5.

*{on it*} That being not watered it may wither away with drought, chap. 1.30. Amos 4.7. Some interpret all these several branches, in a more mysterious way: understanding by plucking up the hedge, and pulling down the wall: some, the abrogating of the covenant between God and them, Zach. 11.12,14. Others, the taking from them his law, that severed them from other people, Ephes. 2.14. and kept them within compass, Gal. 3.23. By making them desolate: the depriving them of their civil state, and lawful polity: by not pruning and digging: the taking away of the priestly ministry, Hos. 3.4. Luk. 13.8. By the briars, and thorns, springing up: idolatry and other corruptions springing up among them, 2 Sam. 23.6,7. ch. 27.4. By forbidding the clouds to rain on them: the bereaving them of their prophets, Psal. 74.9. ch. 30.20. But these curiosities, the graver and soberer sort of interpreters, do not unjustly refuse and reject.

**V. 7.** *{For the vineyard, &c.*} Hitherto was the parable. Now follows the explication of it, applied unto God, and his people: showing how the case stood between God and them: how they had failed in their duty, and what for the same was to befall them.

*{For*} So some, as rendering a reason, why it should not so have been with it, as it was: because it was God's vineyard, v. 1. and the place that he desired to delight in, Psal. 132.14. but that goes too far backward. Others therefore rather render it, *Truly, Verily, Surely*: as Job 8.6. & 20.20. & 28.1. because having made an end of the parable, he proceeds now to expound it. See, ch. 7.9.

*{the vineyard*} See v. 1.

*{of the Lord of hosts*} See ch. 1.9.

*{is the house of Israel*} See ch. 1.24. & 2.5.

*{and the men of Judah*} In a more special manner, as ch. 1.1. Hos. 4.15. & 11.12.

*{men*} Heb. *man*: as v. 3.

*{his pleasant plant*} Heb. *his plant of delights*, or, *pleasures*; that is, in which he took exceeding great delight, Psal. 132.13,14. so Jer. 31.20. *a child of delight*. For, a child, that God has taken very much delight in: David uses the terms very frequently, thereby to express the great delight he took in God's law, and his word, Psal. 94.19. and 119.16,24,70,77,92,143,174. and Solomon of the delight that God takes in his Son, Prov. 8.30. as also, of the delight that the Son of God takes in the sons of men, Prov. 8.31. that is, as here in his church, while it continues faithful unto him.

*{plant*} See ch. 60.21. & 61.3.

*{and he looked for judgment, &c.*} See v. 3,4. *judgment*, and *justice*; the execution of the one, and exercise of the other, were the good *grapes*, or fruit, that God expected from his people, Mic. 7.1.

*{but behold oppression*} To wit, there, where judgment ought to have been, in places of judicature, at the bar, and in the bench of justice, Eccl. 3.16. See ch. 1.23. & 3.14,15. So Jer. 4.23,36.

*{but*} Heb. *and*. As v. 2. so v. 6.

*{behold*} Spoken by way of admiration, at so strange a degeneration. See ch. 1.21. Jer. 2.21.

*{oppression*} As some render it, *a consociation*, or *conspiracy*, from a word that signifies *to cleave fast together*, Job 30.7. 1 Sam. 26.19. ch. 14.1. and understand it of the wicked judges and officers conspiring and combining together to do injustice, Hos. 6.8,9. Mic. 7.3. or, as most, *a scab*; or, as some, from the former root, *a cleaving scab*. Such an one, as cleaves, or sticks fast to the body; or causes the body to stick fast to the raiment. So are two other words of the same stock, with very small alteration, used, Levit. 13.2,6,8. & 14.56. See ch. 3.17. The word is by the prophet here used, to make an elegant consonancy, between it and its opposite; such as is also in the next clause, and is with him very frequent. The meaning is, that the judge whose office was to be as a physician, to relieve and heal such as were vexed and wrung by the iniquity of their oppressors, ch. 1.17. and 3.7. was a worse disease to them that repaired to him for ease and relief; as a grievous scab, or sore, that sticks so fast to him, that a man cannot easily be rid, or recovered of it; so that in them the proverb was verified, *a prating physician, a second disease to his patient; a bad one, worse than the disease itself*. The judges worse than their oppressors; what they sustained by the one, more grievous than what they suffered by the other. See ch. 3.15. Others fleeced them; They flayed them: Others bruised their flesh; They broke their bones, Mic. 7.2,3. The word does not signify *leprosy* simply, as some would have it, no more than the word, *plague*, or *stroke*; though joined also oft with it, Levit. 13.3,39. &c. but any such *scab*, as was before said, either leprous, or other, Levit. 13.2,6. and 14.56.

*{for righteousness*} Or, *justice*, joined commonly with judgment; as if these two were inseparable companions: and without justice, judgment, no judgment, or a scab of judgment rather; as our prophet here speaks, chap. 61.8. See Gen. 18.19. Psal. 33.5. and 89.14. & 96.2. Prov. 1.3. & 21.3. 2 Sam. 8.15. ch. 1.21. & 33.5. and 56.1. Jer. 5.1. & 9.23. & 22.15. & 23.5.

*{but behold a cry*} The cry of the oppressed, crying out of their oppressions and wrongs done them; and crying to God, when they can get no relief with man, Exod. 22.22,23,27. Job 19.7. Psal. 12.5. Eccles. 4.1. Lam. 5.4. And these were of the *bad grapes*; fruits not of the spirit, but of the flesh, Gal. 5.19,23. complained of before v. 2.4.

**V. 8.** *{Woe unto them, &c.*} The parable being before propounded, v. 1,6. and expounded, v. 7. the prophet now proceeds unto a more particular enumeration of some principal heads of those bad fruits, before touched upon, with denunciation of judgments proportionable in some sort thereunto. See the like, Amos 2.9,12,15,19.

*{woe*} An usual term of denunciation, chap. 29.1. & 30.1. & 31.1. See chap. 1.4.

*{woe unto*} The particle, *unto*, though necessarily to be understood, yet is here omitted; and with the interjection here used, very seldom expressed, once only, that is observed; the inseparable one, Ezek. 3.13. and once the separable, Jer. 48.1. and instead thereof, twice the particle that signifies *upon*, Jer. 50.27. Ezek. 13.3. but oft expressed with another denunciative very near this, ch. 3.9. and elsewhere.

*{unto them &c.*} The first head of the evils, or crimes more especially instanced in, is the grievous oppression of the greater and richer sort, exercised by them upon their poor neighbors, in expelling them out of their houses, that stood near them, and their lands, that either lay within, or bordered upon their own; thereby either to multiply their own places of abode, or to enlarge their own demesnes. See 1 King. 21. & Mic. 2.2.

*{that join house to house*} Heb. *makers of house to touch by house*. Not that they removed houses out of their places, to adjoin them unto their mansions: but that they added houses to houses: others, to those that they were formerly possessed of, Psal. 83.12. That they might have variety of places to repair to, according to the times and seasons of the year, Amos 3.15. Or to make use of otherwise. So Hos. 4.2. *bloods touch bloods*; That is, murder is added to murder: one comes in on the neck of another. *House to house*; for, one house to another; and *field to field*: That is, one field to another. As, *man of man*; for one man of another, ch. 3.5.

*{that lay field to field*} Heb. *field to field they will make to approach*. A double defect, both of the copulative, *and*; as Exod. 15.9. ch. 3.24. and of the relative; as 2 Chr. 28.9. chap. 42.5. *to those that, &c.*

*{will make to approach*} So have done, do, and will do. See such use of the future, ch. 3.16. Joh. 11.44.

*{field to field*} By taking in those that lay between some of their own, on either side, and so making them to meet; or by encroaching upon, and taking in those that on any side joined to them, Amos 1.13. compared with Jer. 49.1. Job 24.2. forbidden, Prov. 22.28. & 23.10.

*{till there be no place*} No room for any to dwell by them, when they have engrossed all to themselves.

*{that they may be placed*} Heb. *and ye may be made*, or, *make yourselves to dwell*. The copulative for the finitive; as chap. 2.3. The passive for the reciprocal; as ch. 1.16. And the person changed; as ch. 1.29.

*{alone*} As if the whole land were given them to inhabit. Ezek. 11.15.

*{in the midst of the land*} Or, *in the land*; as v. 2,5. ch. 7.22.

**V. 9.** *{In mine, &c.*} The judgment follows, proportionable to the offense. And that, for fuller assurance, confirmed with an oath; as 1 Sam. 3.17. ch. 22.15. Psal. 110.4.

*{In mine ears, said the Lord of Hosts,}* That is, *in my hearing*: as Luk. 4.21. I heard when God spoke it, Psal. 62.11. Or, God by secret inspiration revealed it to me, ch. 22.14. He told me it in mine ear; as 1 Sam. 15.16. So some. But because the affix, or pronoun is wanting, (which is not altogether, unusual, Psal. 91.4. ch. 1.3,15. & 3.12.) nor is the verb in the text. For the Hebrew has no more than, *in the ears the Lord*, or, *of the Lord, &c.* (and yet is that verb also sometime wanting; as 1 King. 20.34. ch. 46.4.) Others therefore, and those not a few, thus render it; *In the ears of the Lord of Hosts*. That is, This your cruel, and injurious carriage is gone up into God's ears: as Gen. 18.20. 2 Chr. 28.9. Ezr. 9.6. Jon. 1.2. He sees it, and takes notice of it, though you think he does neither behold nor regard it, Psal. 10.11,13,14. and 94.4.

*{the Lord of Hosts*} Who is able to right those whom you wrong: and to avenge them on you, Psal. 146.7. Prov. 10.11. & 24.15,16. See ch. 1.9,24.

*{of a truth many houses shall be desolate*} Heb. *if many houses be not desolate*. A defective, but emphatical form of swearing. See Psal. 95.11. As if he had said: *Let me not live*; or *let me not be God*; or *let me not be deemed a God of truth, a God of my word; let me never be believed*; if such a thing be, which he means shall never be. So c. 22.14. & 62.8. Or if such a thing be not, which he is fully resolved shall be: as in this place. See the like forms with man, Gen. 14.23. Ps. 132.3. wherein, out of a cautious shunning dismal expressions, they used in swearing to omit the terms of execration, which yet in the form of the oath was implied, and was to be supplied to make the sentence entire: yea, sometime was, but in a more sparing and indefinite way, for the most part, expressed. See Ruth 1.17. 1 Sam. 3.17. 1 King. 19.2.

*{of a truth, &c.*} *Saith he*, is to be supplied. As the like is very usual, in the relation of the speeches, either of God, or others, See 1 King. 1.17. & 20.37. Psal. 105.15. with 11. & 132.14. chap. 47.4.

*{many houses*} The multitude, and variety of your houses, so gotten, shall do you no good; you shall have no benefit by them, little joy of them. See Amos 3.15. & 6.11.

*{desolate*} Heb. *for*, or, *unto desolation*. Designed for it, and brought to it, as Jer. 2.11. See ch. 1.7. Your houses shall stand empty; the inhabitants being either driven out of them, Mic. 2.10. or destroyed, and deceased in them. Amos 6.9,10.

*{even great and fair, without inhabitants*} *Even*, wanting; as ch. 51.22. Heb. *great, and good*; as we use to say *goodly*. So Deut. 8.12. Neither the largeness, nor the fairness of your houses, shall procure you security, or afford you safety, Amos 3.15.

*{without inhabitant*} Heb. *from no inhabitant being*. That is, *for want of inhabitants*, or *because there is no inhabitant* in them. So Jer. 4.7. See the like, ch. 50.2.

**V. 10.** *{Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath*} As their houses shall stand empty; so their land shall lie waste and barren; as well those, that thus they came by, as those which they were formerly possessed of. The one parcel so gotten, shall bring a curse upon the whole. See ch. 7.23. Hag. 1.6.

*{ten acres*} The word signifies, first, *a pair*, or *couple* of oxen, Job 1.3. asses, Judg. 19.10. mules, 2 King. 5.17. Or other beasts, whether yoked, or unyoked; yea, sometime not of horse only, but of horsemen, chap. 21.7,9. In the second place, it is used for such a parcel of ground, as a pair, or yoke of oxen could ordinarily plow in a day, 1 Sam. 14.14. which among the Romans, was esteemed to be of two hundred and forty foot in length, and one hundred and twenty in breadth.

*{shall yield*} Heb. *make*. As vers. 2. Hos. 9.16. & 10.1. to *make wine*, for to *yield wine*, as to *make milk*, for to *yield milk*, ch. 7.22.

*{one bath*} That is, but *one bath*; not of grapes; but of wine, made of the grapes, that it shall bear. For the *bath* was a measure for *liquid* things, yet not the least in use for them, as some say; *hin*, was far less, Levit. 23.13. Ezek. 4.11. (and the log less than that, Levit. 14.10,12, &c.) and it contained about eight of our gallons, the tenth part of an homer, Ezek. 45.11. So that an whole acre of ground, planted with vines, should not yield so much, as one whole gallon of wine.

*{and the seed of an homer*} For, *an homer of seed*. So also, Levit. 27.16. The *homer* was a measure, as well for grain, as for liquor, containing ten, either baths; or ephah, Ezek. 45.11. And it had its name, either from the *heap* that so much corn as that measure contained, laid together, would make; or because it held as much as an *ass* might well bear.

*{shall yield*} Heb. *make*, as before.

*{an ephah*} That is, but *an ephah*; no more than *one ephah*; as *one bath* before. Which *ephah*, was a measure for dry things; as the *bath* for liquid, and of the same quantity with it; the tenth part of an *homer*, Ezek. 45.11. much about our bushel; so that their corn grounds should not yield them above the tenth part of their seed; they shall *carry out much, and bring in but little*, Hag. 1.6.

**V. 11.** *{Woe unto them that arise early in the morning*} The second crime charged on them, their excess and riot: sensuality joined with security, ver. 12.

*{that rise early*} Heb. *the early risers*. As making a daily exercise of it. So Psal. 127.2.

*{rise early*} That rise early to their drink, as worldly men to their work, Psal. 127.2. as being never well, till they be at the wine, the one; at their work, the other. (So Zeph. 3.7. *They arose early to corrupt their actions*.) And in swilling, and drinking, passing away, and lavishing out the time assigned and allotted to labor, and to more serious and necessary employments, according to the condition of men's several places, Psal. 104.22. Eccl. 10.16,17.

*{that they may*} A defect of the particle finitive; as Zeph. 3.7. See ch. 7.25.

*{follow strong drink*} As Psal. 119.150. *that follow mischief*, pursue it as eagerly as one does his fleeing foe, or his trade. See ch. 1.23. so *to seek* after it, Prov. 23.30,35.

*{strong drink*} Not wine, but other such drinks, made of honey, dates, rice, malt, or other grain, that for strength, oft-times, come not short of wine, and (whereof also they have their name) do make drunk, as well as it, Num. 6.3. Judg. 13.4,14. chap. 29.9. And though ordinarily distinguished from wine, v. 22. yet used here to comprehend both; and so ch. 56.12.

*{that continue unto night*} Heb. *continuers*, or, *drawers out of*; to wit, their drinkings. For there is a twofold defect, both of the copulative, as v. 8. and of the noun, after the participle: in the like case expressed, Psal. 127.2. or simply, *staying* at it, sitting by it, to wit, *at*, or *over the wine*, Prov. 23. v. 30.

*{unto night*} Heb. *in*, for *unto*; as Gen. 11.4. Ezr. 9.7. *twilight*, which may be understood either of the *even twilight*, as Job 24.15. Prov. 7.9. they stay by it, from morning to night, all the livelong day, as we used to speak; or of the *morning twilight*, as the word is used, Job 7.4. 1 Sam. 30.17. from morning to morning, spend night and day, in drinking and reveling: as they are never well, till they be at it; so they can never give over, when they are once set to it, Deut. 32.19. Prov. 23.35. chap. 56.12.

*{till wine inflame them*} A defect of the particle; whether we are to understand it, *till*, as some, or, *that*, as others: the one implying the issue, or effect; the other, the purposed end.

*{wine*} Whence it appears, that the word used in the former branch, does there comprehend both; as does also here the word, *wine*.

*{inflame them*} So is the word used, Ezek. 24.10. Obad. 18. and that is indeed the ordinary effect of wine and strong drink, immoderately taken, to inflame the body, Jer. 51.39. to bring fevers and calentures, such as have thereof their name, Deut. 28.22. yea, to inflame it with filthy lust, Gen. 19.32,36. Hos. 4.11. Yet because the word sometime also signifies, *eagerly*, or *ardently to pursue*, Psal. 7.13. & 10.2. Lam. 4.19. Some therefore render it, *till the wine pursue them*: as they pursue it, so it pursues them in that manner, that it does surprise them, and master them, and take wits, reason, and understanding, from them, Hos. 4.12. Prov. 20.1. but the former seems the sounder.

**V. 12.** *{And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts*} They abound excessively in all manner of delights, abandoning themselves wholly thereunto: not that the things here mentioned, are of themselves evil; but as in their women's attire, and ornaments, ch. 3.18,24. So here the excess in them and abuse of them, is that which is condemned. So Amos 6.4,6.

*{harp*} The name of a musical instrument. Whence one, in the Greek, has its name, said to be strung with wires, and to yield somewhat a mournful, or querulous sound. See ch. 23.16. But whether of the same form with our harp, is uncertain.

*{viol*} Another musical instrument, chap. 14.11. so called, because it was bellied out after the manner of a bottle; so also called, ch. 30.14. Jer. 13.12. See ch. 22.24. Which not unfitly answers our, either lute, or viol. The instrument, in Greek, having its denomination from this is acknowledged by some of them, to have its original from the Phenicians; under which name, they sometime include the Syrians also, and the Jews, not from the Cappadocians, as some of ours. And it was among them, accounted to make a sweeter melody than the harp. No musical instrument is, in Scripture, more frequently mentioned, than these two; and they are oft joined together, 1 Chro. 15.28. 2 Chro. 20.28. & 29.4. Psalm 81.2. & 150.3.

*{the tabret*} The word coming from one that signifies *to beat*, includes, both drums, such as they used to beat at the slaughtering of their children, in sacrifice to Moloch, whereof the place of those horrid rites had its name, ch. 30.33. Jer. 7.31,32. and *tabors*, such as they used commonly in their feasts, and merry meetings, ch. 24.8. Jer. 31.4.

*{and pipe*} Or, *flute*; A wind-instrument, (as an hand-instrument the former;) so called, because *hollow*, or *pierced* through. See chap. 2.19. and 38.20. *tabor and pipe*, are both joined together, as here, so elsewhere, Exod. 15.20. Judg. 11.34. And were used commonly, as among us in dancing, from whence the frequent use of the *pipe* therein, gave the name, in Hebrew, to the *dance*, Psal. 149.3. Jer. 31.15. Judg. 21.21.

*{wine*} Without which no feast, no banquet: called therefore *the feast*, or *the banquet of wine*, Esth. 7.7. *wine* put here for all delicious drinks, (See ver. 11. ch. 22.3.) as there, for all delicious fare, whereof wine is esteemed a principal, Esth. 1.7,8.

*{are in their feasts*} A defect of the preposition; as Numb. 12.8. Job 1.18. Yet some read it. *Are their feasts*. That is, their feasts consist wholly of these. There is nothing else to be seen, or heard in them, nothing pious, or serious: but all excess, and looseness. Contrary to that of the apostle, 1 Cor. 10.31. A pious sense; but I conceive; not here so fit a syntax, as the former is.

*{feasts*} Or, *drinkings*; for that cause so termed. So the word properly signifies. Hence the phrase, as of ordinary meals, *to eat* with one, Gen. 31.54. Psal. 41.9. Luk. 14.1. 1 Cor. 15.11. So of feasting, to *drink* with him, Esth. 3.15. and 7.1.

*{but*} Heb. *and*. as ver. 2,4. As their riotous excess, and sensuality was before taxed; so now their security, and contempt of God, that then they gave themselves wholly unto this dissolute and voluptuous course of life, without any regard of God's judgments, at that time, either present on others, or hanging over their own heads; as being not denounced only against, but in part also inflicted on the state wherein they lived. So ch. 22.12,13. Amos 6.4,6. Matt. 24.38,39.

*{they regard not*} Heb. *they will not behold*. So Psal. 28.5. where the same sentence is; *To behold*, for *to regard*; look after, take special notice of, ch. 22.11. Zach. 12.10. Of the form of speech, see ver. 8.

*{the work of the Lord*} His judgments, either incumbent or, impendent, Psal. 64.10. Hab. 1.5.

*{neither consider the operation of his hands*} Heb. *and the doing of his hands*; or, *his hands-doing, they see not*; or, *they have not seen*. They either consider not, nor take notice of the things themselves, ch. 42.25. Hos. 7.9. or, at least, take no notice of an hand of God in them, ch. 26.11. For it is too nice, that some of the Jewish doctors have, who, by *the work of God*, understand the law of God; by *the work of his hands*, the writing of it in the tables of stone, Exod. 32.13,14. As if they were taxed for not regarding, and looking after God's law, Job 21.14. And that likewise seems to be out of the way, which some of them have, with whom some of ours concur, who understand thereby God's works of creation, the celestial bodies that set forth God's glory, Psal. 8.3. & 19.1. As if they were reproved, for not giving themselves to the contemplation thereof. As also, that others of ours expound it, of their not taking notice of, and laying to heart the works of judgment, long before executed on the old world in Noah's time; and on Sodom, and Gomorrha in Lot's days, 2 Pet. 2.5,6. & 3.5,6. Jud. v. 7. But the prophet seems rather to point at some judgments then present.

**V. 13.** *{Therefore my people are gone into captivity*} The punishment inflicted, or doom passed upon them for this their sin, as sure to take effect, as if it were executed already. See the like judgment denounced upon the like grounds, Amos 6.7.

*{my people*} See ch. 1.3. & 2.6.

*{are gone into captivity*} Or, *are going*. Are as sure to go, as if they were going already. So Jer. 9.1. Joh. 3.18.

*{because they have no knowledge*} Heb. *for no knowledge*. Or, *because of no knowledge*. Because they are such brutish, senseless, and sensual people, Psal. 92.6. & 94.8. ch. 27.11. Or, for want of consideration, because they do not regard, and take notice of the hazardous estate they are in, and God's judgments suddenly like to seize on them, and having seized on the state in part already, ver. 12. Jer. 8.7. Mat. 24.39. Luk. 17.44.

*{and their honourable men are famished*} Heb. *and his honor*, or *glory*, (are, or shall be) *men of hunger*, or *famine*. *His*, to answer the word *people*, Which is, though a collective, (and the pronoun may well therefore be rendered *their*,) yet a singular term. *Honor*, or *glory*, for men of *honor*, or of *glory*; men *honorable*, or *glorious*: that are in great esteem, and make a great show in the world. So *pride*, for a man of *pride*: a *proud* man, Psal. 36.12. Jer. 50.31. *might*: for men of *might*, *mighty* ones, ch. 3.25. *peace*: for a man of *peace*, *a peaceable* man. Psal. 120.7. See ch. 1.21.

*{famished*} *Men of famine*: or *famished men*: as *men of vanity*, for *vain men*, Job 11.11. Psal. 26.4. *Men of wickedness*, for *wicked men*, Job 22.15. *Men of fewness*: for, *a few men*, Deut. 25.5. & 28.62. Of the word *men*, see ch. 2.9. the first term of the phrase, see more, Jer. 44.28. The meaning is: the great men, that now live in such pomp and state, and revel it in that manner, shall be starved for want, even of necessary food.

*{and their multitude dried up with thirst*} *Their*; Heb. *his multitude*: as before. That is, the meaner sort of them, opposed to their glory, or *glorious ones*: As *Adam* to *Ish*, vers. 15. *dried up with thirst*. For thirst, arising from want of drink, caused drought, ch. 41.17. Lam. 4.4. And the want of drink is more insufferable, and prejudicial to man's life, than the want of bread. The meaner sort of them shall suffer want, not of bread only, but of water too, which being the usual drink, in those parts, was more obvious than bread: and more necessary, in some sort, to the preservation of man's life, than it. Those, both great and small, high and low; that have so much abused those good creatures of God, when they had them in abundance, shall now suffer want in either kind of them, and for want of them shall perish. See chap. 3.1. & 65.13. Jer. 2.5. Hos. 2.3. Amos 8.13. For it is not to be conceived, as if the prophet's meaning were, that the one of them only should suffer hunger, and thereby perish; and the other only thirst: but, that both of them should sustain a grievous want of either; set forth in a rhetorical manner, as in way of distribution; for the fuller amplification and aggravation of the evil: such as with this prophet is very frequent. So ver. 15,16. chap. 28.17. and so, Psalm 106.17. Where it is said, that *the earth opened, and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram*. Not, but that it swallowed up the company of Dathan, as well as of Abiram; or, but that it covered as well the one as the other. See also Dan. 12.3. Howbeit a learned late annotator, because the word in this latter branch is found used sometime for *abundance*, and is applied unto wealth, Psalm 37.16. Eccl. 5.10. would have it also so taken here, and v. 14. and ch. 16.14. *abundance*; for men abounding in wealth: and so it will be the same in effect with the former.

**V. 14.** *{Therefore hell hath enlarged herself*} *Hell*. Heb. *Sheol*; a term used commonly for the *grave*, as Numb. 16.30. Psal. 30.3. & 55.15. & 86.13. Herein differing from that other, *keber*, which also signifies *grave*, or *sepulcher*, Psal. 5.10. & 88.11. ch. 22.16. that the former is of larger extent, than the latter: the latter signifying an artificial *grave*, or *sepulcher* only made by man's hand, whether by digging up the ground, or hewing into a rock, Matth. 27.60. or the like. Whereas the other comprehends as well the natural, as the artificial sepulcher; as well that by nature provided, as by man's hand procured, whatsoever place of receptacle a man's body after the soul's departure, is by dissolution, or for dissolution, bestowed in. Thus Jacob says, he would go to his son Joseph, to *Sheol*, whom yet he supposed not to be interred or laid in the ground: but devoured, and so buried, as we may so say, in the bowels of some wild beasts, Gen. 37.35. So Jonas calls the belly of the fish, that had taken him in, and swallowed him down, *the belly of Sheol*, Jon. 2.1,2. because it was like the grave to him, and was like to be the place of his dissolution. So when Hezekiah says, *Sheol cannot praise thee*, ch. 38.18. He means any dead, without distinction, whose bodies are now disposed in their places of dissolution, of what kind or sort soever.
